artifacts.layman_summary: Collects ten public sets of coding problems, tests, example programs and word lists and cleans them into one checked file, so later steps can study which algorithms AI models choose.
artifacts.name: gen_art_dataset_1
artifacts.summary: Provides full_data_out.json (exp_sel_data_out schema; 10 datasets, 61,469 examples, 96.2 MB; schema-validated and QA-passed) plus mini_data_out.json and preview_data_out.json, built by data.py (uv inline script, pinned) from sources downloaded at pinned revisions (data_sources.json; restore with restore.sh; verify with scripts/source_fingerprints.py --check). Datasets: (1) leetcodedataset: 2,869 LeetCode problems (input = problem text, output = reference solution). For the 20 bench-mapped problems, metadata_test_cases_json holds every I/O pair parsed to kwargs/expected, with case ids leetcodedataset:<qid>:<idx> and a status (ok / expected_is_error_message / unparseable); the references re-pass check() 20/20. metadata_bench_task maps 743->T02, 215->T03, 28->T04, 1->T05, 287->T06, 587->T07, 509->T08, 547/323/1971->T10, 300->T11, 56->T13, 347->T14, 435->R1, 684->R2, 210->R3, 34->R6 (1631/1514 T02 alternates; 1091 T01 related). 146 (LRU, T09) and 295 (median, T12) are absent, so their tests must be generated. (2) mercury: 440 human solutions of 20 bench-mapped problems, including T09 LRU (22) and T12 median (22), with runtime, structural markers and I/O-hack flags. (3) llm_creativity: 225 T02 find_path programs referenced as repo@commit:path with the repository's blind-judge labels mapped to T02 modes (dijkstra 132, bellman_ford_spfa 34, bidirectional 30, other 21, dial 5, a_star 2, floyd_warshall 1); no program text because the repository has no licence (fetch the code with scripts/download_all.py). (4) thealgorithms_python: 1,354 MIT implementations, 55 hand-labelled with bench task and mode, the rest usable as AST-rule negatives. (5) clrs_text: 2,910 CLRS-30 execution traces of 15 bench-mode algorithms for tracer tests. (6) humanevalplus: 164 tasks with EvalPlus tests for harness validation. (7) enamel: 164 expert-efficient references with size-levelled input generators for time-limit and stress calibration. (8) concreteness_norms: 39,954 Brysbaert words with concreteness, SUBTLEX frequency, Qwen3 token counts and Open English WordNet noun classes; 718 flagged neutral-noun candidates for neutral-twin and context-seed prompts. (9) kodcode_algorithmic: 2,767 GPT-4o test-verified solutions, 253 naming a bench mode. (10) xlcost_python: 10,622 GeeksforGeeks programs, 209 naming a bench mode. metadata_named_algorithms are regex hints, not verified labels; metadata_duplicate_of marks repeats. Known issues: LeetCode 1971 has 73 of 77 error-message outputs; two-sum has 8 cases with no solution; order-free answers need validity checkers (metadata_leetcode_answer_semantics). Not built here (left to the bench build): frozen task specs in new wording, spec-filtered hidden tests (and oracle tests for T01/T09/T12), labellers, gold sets and forecasts. Licences: Mercury and KodCode CC-BY-NC, XLCoST CC-BY-SA, the rest Apache-2.0/MIT; llm-creativity labels only. Reproduction: reproducibility.md (Python 3.12.14, 45 pinned packages in pyproject.toml); no LLM calls, $0 spend.
artifacts.title: Source data for an algorithm-choice coding bench

artifacts.layman_summary: We told an AI coding model not to use its favourite algorithm and measured which algorithm it switched to, testing whether its own 'standard alternative' answers predict the switch.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_1
artifacts.summary:
Behavioural screen on Qwen/Qwen3-8B (thinking off, vLLM 0.11, T=1.0) of two predictors of where probability mass goes when a prompt bans an algorithm. The proposed predictor is substitution by association: the model's own Borda-aggregated 'standard alternative to X' ranking. The baseline is the typicality ladder: baseline frequency renormalised over the surviving modes. Two path-search tasks are used: T1 unweighted grid path (6 modes) and T2 weighted shortest path (5 modes). The artifact provides:
(1) A reusable task suite: specs, 48 + 45 seeded hidden tests with per-case time limits, 22 reference implementations, and a sandbox harness.
(2) A validated labeller: runtime tracer + AST rules + a strategy-blind gpt-4.1-mini judge on disagreements, with a gold set adjudicated by gpt-4.1-mini, gemini-2.5-flash and deepseek tie-break. Both labellers get 22/22 references right; on evaluation gold, kappa runtime-vs-AST is 0.753, runtime vs adjudicated 0.843, combined label 0.966. gate_passed=false is flagged.
(3) data/samples.jsonl: 3,260 labelled programs in the shared screen schema (task, condition, paraphrase, model, decoding, label, passed, code, ...), poolable with other experiments.
(4) Frozen, sha256 hash-chained predictions (commitments.log); every event was committed before its generation.
(5) method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out) with one example per event plus all analyses in metadata.
Key results, descriptive only (2 tasks, 2 informative events):
- Baselines are fully collapsed (T1 100% BFS, T2 100% Dijkstra, also at T=1.3), so the frequency predictor is uniform and its nomination is always tied.
- Modal bans were obeyed (compliance 0.90 / 0.91) and landed entirely on one substitute: DFS for T1 (38/38 compliant correct samples), Bellman-Ford/SPFA for T2 (86/86).
- Association hit T2 but missed T1, where the Borda map nominated Dijkstra with clarity 0.20 and ranked DFS last. Log scores were T1 -2.82 vs -1.63 and T2 -0.75 vs -1.41; mean paired difference -0.27 nats/sample; association wins 1 of 2.
- The model's own free-text 'standard alternative' answers and the listall typicality cue nominated the realised substitute in both events (2/2). A post-hoc gpt-4.1-mini map shows the same ranking-vs-free-text split.
- Cumulative double bans failed (compliance 0.06 / 0.00): the model re-implemented the banned mechanism under other names ('backtracking' DFS, 'BFS with pruning' = SPFA). 41/94 and 58/100 recurrent programs never name the banned algorithm, so the succession stopped at step 2.
- Mention twins act as strong recommendations (+56 to +100 pp for 5 modes; 0 for 3), not placebos.
All 36 headline numbers were independently re-derived from raw files (audit/rederive.py), and placebo runs of the contest and T9 comparisons fail as expected. reproducibility.md gives an exact CPU-only Path A (byte-identical outputs verified, no API or GPU calls) and a full-regeneration Path B. OpenRouter spend was USD 0.27. Next-round implications: the ranking instrument diverges from free-text association; frequency-based typicality is uninformative under full collapse, while listall typicality is informative; multi-name bans need mechanism-level compliance checks.
artifacts.title: Where an algorithm ban sends an AI coder

artifacts.layman_summary: We asked an AI model to write path-finding code thousands of times, banned its favourite algorithm, and mapped inside the model where its choice goes; bans mostly fail and edits to its internals do not redirect it.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_2
artifacts.summary: Behavioural + activation-space screen of Qwen3-8B (bf16, thinking off, T=1.0, HF transformers generate on one NVIDIA L4; vLLM could not start) for two path-search coding tasks: T1 grid path (catalogue bfs, dfs, bidir_bfs, iddfs, astar, dijkstra_unit) and T2 weighted shortest path (dijkstra, bellman_ford_spfa, bidir_dijkstra, floyd_warshall, dial). Provides: hidden test suites (41/42 cases) and catalogue references (tasks/); a validated labeller (runtime tracer + AST rules + blind OpenRouter judge; gate kappa 0.90/0.94, runtime-vs-adjudicated 0.96/0.92); 1550 prompts with token ids (prompts/prompts.jsonl); every labelled program (data/samples_phase{A,C,D}.jsonl; method_out.json, exp_gen_sol_out, 2310 programs + 7 contest events). KEY RESULTS (descriptive, few events): baselines collapse completely (T1 200/200 BFS, T2 200/200 Dijkstra; mention:X keeps 50/50); prompt bans mostly fail (ban:bfs compliance 0.18: 62 BFS/29 DFS/9 unit-Dijkstra; ban:dijkstra 0.22: 72 Dijkstra/27 Bellman-Ford); on T1 the displaced mass lands only on BFS's geodesic neighbours on the read-position manifold (DFS 41, unit-Dijkstra 58; never A*/IDDFS/bidir at 71-95), T2 goes to the 2nd-nearest (Bellman-Ford). Hash-committed forecasts (predictions/, sha256 186f71...): geodesic proximity has the best mean log score (-1.43 primary) vs uniform -1.56; the model's own 'standard alternative' rankings are worst (-2.59). R-position probes: named->masked transfer 0.67 (T1 L27) / 0.54 (T2 L24) vs shuffled null ~0.2-0.3; T1 baseline decoder fails (R gate flagged). Manifold TwoNN ID 4.2/5.2 vs ~11.9/11.6 shuffled nulls. C3: ban-vs-mention shifts 61-99% residual, all inconclusive. C2: affine directional ablation of the modal mode (pre-declared R-plus-prompt variant, alpha 0.5/1/2, random controls with identical edit norms, common random numbers) moved 0/50 on both tasks (outputs 78-90% byte-identical to alpha=0, like random controls); exploratory full variant only degenerates at alpha 4. Reusable for next rounds: cache/hR_layer{8..28}.npy + hR_index.jsonl (read-position states; layers 8-20 and suffix means kept on the run volume only), directions/anchors/basis npz, results/*.json, figures/*. Independent audit (analysis/audit_rederive.py): 99 numbers re-derived, 0 mismatches, placebos fail.
artifacts.title: How prompt bans move an LLM's path-search choices

artifacts.layman_summary: Tests whether a code-writing AI model settles on its algorithm within its first few words, by restarting its answers from many cut points and reading its internal states.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_3
artifacts.summary: Screen of 'fork tokens decide the idea' on Qwen3-8B (bf16, thinking off, vLLM 0.11.0) with two path-search coding tasks built here (T1 unweighted grid path, T2 weighted shortest path; 40 seeded hidden tests each, 17 reference solutions) under a neutral baseline prompt and a modal-ban prompt (ban:BFS on T1, ban:Dijkstra on T2). Labeller: sandboxed runtime tracer (instrumented heapq/deque/queue, grid reads, edge passes, call depth) + AST rules + OpenRouter judge on disputes (gold-set gate). Measurements on one shared pool of ~10k labelled generations: (1) S6 pools at global T in {0.3,0.7,1.0,1.3}; (2) Forking-Paths-style resampling screen over 40 base paths (S=8 every 4th token over the first 92 tokens for ban paths), permutation-calibrated multinomial change points, token-level localisation, S=30 confirmation with control pairs and next-token entropies; (3) prompt swap at the commitment token; (4) fork-window temperature knob vs global-T sweep, matched random-window and AdapT-style anchored controls; (5) residual-stream probes (layers 8-28) at R, k=8/16/32/64, fork and commitment positions vs prompt-only predictor with permutation nulls. Outputs: generations/*.jsonl, forks.json, swap.json, knob_table.json, probes.json, summaries/, figures/, states/ (split npz parts), method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out) with the pre-registered verdict and rule trace.
artifacts.title: Do a few early tokens decide the algorithm?

artifacts.layman_summary: Tests whether nudging a language model's internal state toward 'brainstorm many approaches' makes it write a wider variety of correct path-finding algorithms, compared with simply asking it to.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_4
artifacts.summary: De-commitment steering screen on Qwen3-8B (thinking off) for two path-search tasks with hidden tests: T1 grid path (catalogue bfs/dfs/bidirectional_bfs/iddfs/astar/dijkstra_unit) and T2 weighted shortest path (dijkstra/bellman_ford_spfa/bidirectional_dijkstra/floyd_warshall/dial). Method: list-minus-implement difference-of-means direction d_dc (50+50 held-out frame paraphrases) at the last prompt token, layer L*=18 (held-out AUC 1.0 on all layers, d' tie-break), added as c*||h||*d_hat at R and every generated token; c swept over {0.25,0.5,1,1.5} + pre-registered bisection, c* chosen on pass rate only (T1 0.1, T2 0.25). Controls: HF c=0 hook, vLLM baseline N=200 (engine check passed), two random directions, variable-name placebo, breadth direction, cross-task transfer, enumeration prompt, modal ban and mention prompts, succession ban. Labels from sandboxed hidden tests + runtime tracer + AST rules, judge for disagreements; R0 and labeller gate pass on both tasks (2 revision rounds). RESULTS (verdict PARTIAL): T1 is 100% BFS in every arm except bans; steering never diversifies it (pass 1.00 -> 0.57 at c=0.25, still all BFS). T2: at c*=0.25 pass 0.78 vs 0.95, correct programs shift Dijkstra->Bellman-Ford (54 BF/23 D vs 7 BF/88 D), rarefied Hill-1 +0.65 [90% cluster CI 0.31, 0.97]; but random direction rand1 does almost the same (+0.59; dc-rand1 +0.07 [-0.26, 0.39]) so the gain is not direction-specific (beats rand2 and placebo). Enumeration prompt gives no diversity (T2 -0.08); the modal ban buys +0.79 at 1.5 pass points but most banned samples still use the banned algorithm. Commitment test: ban-minus-mention shifts R toward the list frame by 0.04/0.05 of the frame distance (exact permutation p 0.021/0.007; enumeration positive control 0.54/0.58). Hash-committed forecasts: on T2 the de-committed forecast scored best (log score -0.058 vs -0.219 frequency) on one informative event; T1 forecasts degenerate. Headline numbers re-derived independently (results/audit_rederivation.json); vLLM same-seed determinism failed on T1. REUSABLE: directions/ (d_dc per task and layer 8-28, rand/placebo/breadth), cache/hR_*.npy (R-states, on the run volume), tasks/ (specs, hidden tests, 12 references), labeller/ (tracer, AST rules, judge prompt), gold/gold_set.jsonl, data/samples.jsonl (2,940 labelled samples), forecast/ (sha256-committed forecasts), results/*.json, figures/fig1-5, method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out; one example per common-random-number slot, output = HF c=0 label, predict_<arm> = label|pass/fail).
artifacts.title: Steering an LLM to vary its search algorithms

artifacts.layman_summary: Compares Qwen3-8B before and after instruction tuning on two path-finding coding tasks to see whether tuning made it always pick the same algorithm, and whether steering its internals undoes that.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_5
artifacts.summary: Screen of alternate 4 ('instruction tuning installed the algorithm-choice collapse') on Qwen3-8B-Base vs Qwen3-8B (thinking off), two path-search tasks: T1 unweighted grid path, T2 weighted directed shortest path. 4140 programs, each run on 47/46 hidden tests and labelled by a runtime-signature + AST labeller with a blind LLM judge (gemini-2.5-flash-lite) for disagreements (reference gate: AST 100%, runtime never wrong; kappa runtime-AST 0.77; inter-judge kappa 0.93). 2x2 weights x format (T=1, top-p 1): instruct chat is collapsed (T1 BFS 200/200, Hill_cc 1.00; T2 Dijkstra 193/200, Hill_cc 1.16). The base model under the same chat tokens is more diverse (T1 BFS 49/57 correct, Hill_cc 1.58; T2 Dijkstra 63/90, Hill_cc 2.09); template-free base code is mostly broken (pass 5%/8%; T2 correct programs Bellman-Ford-modal 16/25). D_weights = Hill_cc(instruct_chat) - Hill_cc(base_chat) = -0.58 [-1.01,-0.15] (T1), -0.93 [-1.38,-0.46] (T2). Pre-registered verdicts: T2 INSTALLED_BY_POST_TRAINING; T1 MIXED (modal-share gap 14.0 pp, just under the 15 pp bar); no ALREADY_IN_BASE, so the alternate passes the screen (also under Hill_all). At the planned N (before the N=300 base extension) both read MIXED. Post-training concentrated the base model's existing mode rather than inventing one; the chat format also concentrates the instruct model on T2 (template-free Hill_cc 1.93 -> chat 1.16) and switches the base model's T2 mode from Bellman-Ford to Dijkstra. Mechanistic test: the paired instruct-minus-base residual difference at the read position (split-half cos 0.998, task-general cos 0.85-0.92, logit lens = answer-format tokens) subtracted over layers 8-28 is DESTRUCTIVE at c=0.5/1.0/1.5 (0/100 parseable), while norm-matched random directions keep format and algorithm; downstream layers amplify the subtraction (overshoot, gap_closed ~0 at L18/L28). Single-layer delta_18 fallback: c=0.25 keeps 94-98% pass with zero algorithm change (NO_EFFECT). R-only subtraction flips Qwen3 into thinking-style prose yet stated plans and correct programs keep BFS/Dijkstra. No knob restores diversity; the ban prompt does better (T2 Hill_cc 1.16 -> 1.99 at 0 pp pass loss). Hash-committed forecast from the base model hit top-1 on both ban events (DFS; Bellman-Ford), log score -0.47/-0.22 vs uniform -1.63/-1.41, but base-chat/typicality references did as well. All headline numbers were re-derived by an independent script (0 mismatches; placebo permutation tests reject at ~5%). Reusable outputs: runs/samples.jsonl (shared row schema, every sample), runs/labelled_*.jsonl, method_out.json (metadata = all analyses: collapse_screen, steering, rows.BUY / rows.PREDICT, labeller_qa, sharpening_direction), data/ (prompts, hidden tests, references), src/ labeller + harness, activations/ (residual states, deltas, band steering vectors; kept on the run volume), predictions/ (committed forecast).
artifacts.title: Did post-training cause Qwen3's algorithm collapse?

artifacts.layman_summary: We sampled 5,220 programs from an AI model at different randomness settings and prompt seeds and checked whether it picks a different algorithm or just rewords the same one.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_6
artifacts.summary: Screen on Qwen3-8B (vLLM 0.11.0, RTX 5090) over T1 (unweighted grid path search, any valid path) and T2 (weighted directed shortest path). 5,220 generations, each labelled by hidden tests + runtime tracer + AST rules + blind judge: A0 no-cue baseline (N=100/task); A1 temperature grid T in {0.3,0.7,1.0,1.3} x {top-k=10, top-p=0.95}, thinking off, N=100/cell; A6 the same grid thinking on, N=100/cell; entropy/word/semantic seeds; four creativity instructions; forced implementations; gen-then-select. FINDINGS: (1) Temperature and sampler do not change the algorithm. BFS share on T1 is 797/800 thinking off (every cell >= 0.99) and 800/800 thinking on; Dijkstra share on T2 is 797/800 off and 800/800 on. (2) Phrasings grow with T while ideas stay at about 1: on T1 at theta=0.8, phrasing clusters go from 3-4 at T=0.3 to 24-36 at T=1.3; log PPI slope about +1.2 per unit T, paired CI > 0. T2 shows a smaller rise (1-2 to 3-6 clusters; top-p CI includes 0). (3) Random seeds shift behaviour by <= 1 pp (90% CI within +-15 pp). At the read position, the entropy seed stays within paraphrase noise (displacement ratio 0.73 T1 / 1.16 T2), but the word seed on T1 moves the mode subspace 1.56x (CI 1.27-1.87), close to a neutral insert (0.81/1.29). The semantic seed moves R 3.4-3.7x; on T2 it shifts behaviour 66 pp toward Bellman-Ford (p=0.0004), on T1 only +2 pp toward bidirectional BFS (p=0.08). (4) 'Fully novel' and 'list 10 then implement' cut T2 Dijkstra by 15 and 11 pp. Gen-then-select reaches DA_idea@25 3.98/3.00 vs 1.26/1.00 for A0, at pass rates of 55%/75%. (5) Variance of trajectory states (first 64 generated tokens): complement variance rises steeply with T; the raw mode-subspace share is flat on T1 and rises slightly on T2; the excess over a data-matched null rises, so P7 is missed. (6) All thinking traces hit the 2,048-token cap; the first approach mentioned is BFS/Dijkstra in >= 98% of traces. Mechanical verdict: MIXED (S-T6 variance-share slope and random-seed equivalence at R fail). Hash-committed forecast: 6/8 hits. CAVEAT: the labeller gate failed by the strict plan criteria on both tasks, so results are descriptive. References agree 100%, population kappa(runtime, AST) is 0.88/0.85, gold agreement 93%/70%, and agreement on correct gold programs 92%/92%. REUSE: importable modules tasks/, tests/ (hidden tests + limits), references/, harness/, labeller/ (tracer, AST rules, judge, gold gate), prompts/, gen/, hooks/, analysis/. Per-sample rows (shared screen schema) are in results/samples.jsonl. Raw generations with token ids are in results/raw/. All results are in results/analysis.json and method_out.json metadata (deviations, gate, verdicts, forecast check, module sha256s). Figures fig1-fig6 are in figures/. Headline numbers were re-derived independently by verify_headlines.py; placebo tests are non-significant. OpenRouter spend was about $0.10.
artifacts.title: Do temperature and seeds change an LLM's algorithm?

hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: The next iteration answers how a 'do not use X' prompt moves the algorithm inside the model (what replaces X and where the ban acts) and runs the request's top-five prohibition with activation-space manifold, SAE, thought-anchor, lens and same-seed temperature readouts.
key_changes: Replaced the read-position share test (null: the ban shift at R lies 61-99% off the algorithm axes) with an output-space share test on forced-ratio latent probabilities (FRLP), an importance-sampling likelihood instrument that stays informative under a fully collapsed baseline and turns every single, sham and multi-ban into a measured event.

Named the generic-perturbation rival (every shortest-path perturbation, including random directions, landed on Bellman-Ford/SPFA) and made it the explicit alternative outcome, the 'latent ladder'. It is measured by an external profile built from a nonce ban, matched-norm random edits and the novelty instruction. The hypothesis now states that re-collapse alone is predicted even by pure renormalisation.

Added a co-primary route test: 2x2 key-value-cache patching plus temporal and layer knockouts, asking whether a ban acts through the prompt states and R or directly at generation time; FRLP drop as the effect size.
Added C5 'R knows how hard, not what': per-wording compliance against the shared ban direction at R, over about 100 existing ban wordings.

Froze the predictor set at four families (ladder, association, prime-and-veto, proximity). Dropped the Borda map and sampled frequency. The budget goes to events; prime-and-veto is the one new family, formalising the review's negation-promotion objection.

Fixed ban wording at 5 templates entered as a random effect. Set one gate definition (avoidance >= 0.5 plus >= 20 scored samples), mechanism-level labels, and a landing distribution over attempted programs. Compliant programs drive only the knob table, because 161 of 273 grid DFS programs fail through bugs.

Bench: a cheap presence pilot (N=50) before any task is frozen, disagreement-first build order, present-minor ban targets, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on confirmation. Screen (the two path-search tasks) and confirmation (new tasks plus Llama) are kept strictly separate.

Step 0 is CPU only and comes first: the locus probe on the saved forking-token states (cause recorded: the probe stage ran at 18:29, before the states were saved at 18:34), the geodesic k x layer robustness check, the cross-experiment perturbation table, and the corrected PREDICT/BUY tables.

Knob table on one statistic (rarefied Hill over compliant programs, banned labels excluded). Expected: bans replace the default (about 1.0 on shortest path) while perturbations mix two algorithms; generate-then-select becomes a ceiling row (SimpleStrat). The positive target is stated per task.

Request coverage: the literal top-five prohibition (TOP-5, ARC-5 and SCATTER-5 on a grid catalogue extended toward 10 algorithms, plus leave-one-survivor on shortest path), activation-space manifold plots at the validated locus, an SAE readout, thought anchors with an 8,192-token cap, the same-seed CRN temperature test, logit and tuned lens, and NLA/j-lens mapping.

Corrected the record: per-draw substitute counts (shortest path 272/272 in 5/5 draws; grid DFS 116/128, realised mode in 4/5 draws), the non-replicating cumulative ban, +66.3 pp, the read-position seed double dissociation, the preregistered verdict labels, and the missing executed outputs.

Closed bets: the R share test, affine ablation at R, the decommitment direction, the sharpening subtraction, forking-window temperature, sham-ban equivalence, and the ladder limit against clarity. Added a nearest-neighbour positioning line for each claim.
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: Best strands are leads: the ban substitute is predictable pre-ban, but n=2 and associate = runner-up. Deepen: likelihood ban matrices on many tasks, ladder rival and ban route tested head-on.
hypothesis_update.title: Prompt Bans Substitute, Not Just Subtract

critiques.description: BLOCKING CONTRADICTION 1, the five-draw substitute claim. Established item 4 ('that substitute replicated in five independent draws: DFS for BFS'), Section 1.11 ('Where the ban had compliant samples, they landed on the same substitute every time: DFS on the grid task (with a few unit weight Dijkstra programs)') and the closing summary ('collapses again on one substitute ... the same substitute in five independent draws') contradict Table 13, Table 34 and Section 1.6. In the geometry draw the 18 compliant grid programs are DFS 10 and unit-weight Dijkstra 8, and Section 1.6 calls this 'no clear realised mode'. Eight of 18 is not 'a few'. Recomputed per draw from the per-sample rows (compliant grid programs): association DFS 38/38, forking token DFS 40/41, decommitment DFS 16/18, instruction tuning DFS 12/13, geometry DFS 10/18; pooled DFS 116/128 (90.6%). The shortest-path claim holds: Bellman-Ford/SPFA 272/272 in all five draws. Moreover 'bans collapse the output again; they do not spread it' is contradicted on the grid task by the step-2 bans: geometry BFS+DFS sent 18 compliant programs to unit-weight Dijkstra, and decommitment BFS+DFS gave unit-weight Dijkstra 13 and A* 3.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite the three passages with per-draw counts. Shortest-path task: 5/5 draws, 272/272. Grid task: DFS realised mode in 4/5 draws; one HF-engine draw (62% banned share) with no clear mode (DFS 10, unit-weight Dijkstra 8). Add a pooled row to Table 34 with Wilson intervals. State that second-step bans on the grid task can spread compliant output over unit-weight Dijkstra and A*. Expected impact: clears half of the blocking flag. The headline survives in a weaker, correct form.

critiques.description: BLOCKING CONTRADICTION 2, the grid BUY verdict. Section 1.11 states: 'On the grid task no knob that kept 80% of the pass rate produced a second algorithm among compliant programs: the cumulative ban's gain came from programs that still used BFS'. Table 37's own row 'cumulative ban of BFS and DFS (decommitment) | 0.88 / 1.00 | yes | ... | BFS 65, unit weight Dijkstra 13, DFS 7, A* 3' shows 16 compliant programs over two non-banned algorithms. Table 13's exploratory geometry BFS+DFS ban shows pass 0.96 with 18 compliant unit-weight Dijkstra programs. Both counts reproduce from gen_art_experiment_4/data/samples.jsonl and gen_art_experiment_2/data/samples_phaseC.jsonl. The same knob failed by disguise in the association draw (pass 0.53, 5 compliant). The report therefore also never says whether the strategy's preregistered POSITIVE TARGET ('a knob that buys a second correct algorithm at under 20 points of pass rate') was met. It was met on the shortest-path task by the prompt ban (exp5, 0 points) and the semantic seed (7 points), and on the grid task only by this non-replicating cumulative ban.
critiques.suggested_action: Replace the sentence with the three draws of the cumulative BFS+DFS ban (decommitment 0.88/1.00 with 16 compliant; geometry 0.96/0.99 with 18; association 0.53/0.933 with 5) and call the grid BUY candidate non-replicating. Add one line stating the POSITIVE TARGET outcome per task. Expected impact: clears the other half of the blocking flag.

critiques.description: The selection rule is misreported and misapplied. The strategy (gen_strat_1 rationale) scores PREDICT 'on every informative event (banned mode present at >= 10% of the latent baseline, compliance >= 50%, >= 2 survivors)'. Section 1.1 omits this gate. Modal-ban compliance per draw, as 1 - banned share / as the compliant share: association 0.90/0.38 (grid) and 0.91/0.86 (shortest path); geometry 0.38/0.18 and 0.28/0.22; decommitment 0.51/0.18 and 0.46/0.38; instruction tuning 0.38/0.13 and 0.46/0.46. So the geometry events (which Table 14 calls 'primary'), both instruction-tuning events and the decommitment shortest-path event fail the gate under either definition. Under the stricter definition even the association grid event fails. Table 36's descriptive ranking ('the highest scoring forecasts ... the base model's own distribution and ... the decommitted distribution') therefore rests largely on gated-out events: the base-model forecast was scored only on instruction-tuning events, the decommitted forecast only on the decommitment shortest-path event, and the geodesic kernel only on geometry events. The BUY rule requires a winner 'on the pooled tasks and in direction on each task'. The report declares the prompt ban and the semantic seed tied using the shortest-path task alone (1.99 vs 1.988, from different experiments with different baselines). Table 37 also mixes raw Hill_cc and rarefied delta-Hill, and Hill_cc counts correct banned programs, which the report itself calls a flaw.
critiques.suggested_action: Quote the full PREDICT/BUY rule in Section 1.1. Fix one compliance definition (state which one the strategy meant, or report both). Add gate columns to Tables 14 and 36 and recompute the PREDICT means on gated events only. Recompute BUY with one statistic (rarefied Hill over compliant programs, i.e. excluding banned labels, at a common depth, with the 90% sample bootstrap the rule names), pooled and per task, and state the rule's outcome (which knobs advance) explicitly. Expected impact: +0.5 to +1. It makes the scorecard the next iteration acts on trustworthy.

critiques.description: The iteration added metrics, not samples, to an underpowered panel. Table 36 scores 15 forecast families on the same two modal-ban events, while the selection rule needs at least 3 events on which nominations disagree. The final hypothesis review's own power arithmetic needed roughly 66 pooled events for the confirmatory test. Running the same two events in five experiments buys replication of the substitute, not more events. More predictors and more readouts (decoder, geodesic kernel, decommitted, base-model, free-form, listing, first-rank, external map) over two events cannot select a survivor. The report concludes only that 'the contests need tasks whose baselines are not fully collapsed'. It does not say that the budget belonged on events, nor that the planned 12-task LeetCode bench may also be fully collapsed, which would make the typicality predictor uniform again.
critiques.suggested_action: State in the 'what we have learned' section that the next iteration's budget goes to events, not to predictors. Before freezing any bench task, run a cheap baseline pilot (N=50 at T=1.0) and keep only tasks whose second algorithm reaches the 10% presence cut. Add ban targets in the present-minor stratum, and hold ban wording fixed or model paraphrase as a random effect. Freeze the predictor set at the families that already exist. Expected impact: +0.5 on contribution of the next record.

critiques.description: Missing synthesis: random directions push the shortest-path task to the same substitute. The report treats Bellman-Ford/SPFA as the model's 'second preference' revealed by bans, but its own controls show that any perturbation lands there. In the decommitment experiment, random direction rand1 at c=0.25 moved correct programs to Bellman-Ford/SPFA 26 of 79 (vs 7/95 at c=0; dc minus rand1 +0.07). In the instruction-tuning experiment, band random direction 2 (c=0.5) turned all 33 correct programs into Bellman-Ford/SPFA, against Dijkstra 100/100 in the control. Table 26 shows this arm only as 'Hill_cc 1.00, delta 0.00, flip 0.36', hiding a complete algorithm switch. random1_Ronly gave Bellman-Ford/SPFA 9. The breadth and placebo directions, the semantic seed, the novelty instruction, the enumeration prompt and the base model all move toward the same algorithm. This is a direct rival to the main hypothesis (a ban-specific promotion of an associate), namely that any perturbation of the read-position state, semantic or not, spills mass onto the runner-up. The report never names it. It also bears on established item 5.
critiques.suggested_action: Add label composition to Table 26. Add a cross-experiment table of every shortest-path perturbation (prompts, steering, random and placebo directions, seeds, instructions) with the Bellman-Ford/SPFA share among correct programs and its pass cost. State the generic-perturbation rival in the 'what we have learned' section and list it among the alternates. Plan a discriminating test: matched-norm random read-position edits versus the ban at equal displacement, with common seeds, on tasks where the runner-up and the associate differ. Expected impact: +0.5. It changes what the next iteration should test.

critiques.description: The geometric claim (established item 6, 'mass moved to the edge of the banned region rather than to the opposite side') overreaches its evidence. (i) The grid read-position gate failed: the decoder reads the baseline as DFS 0.60 / unit-Dijkstra 0.27 / BFS 0.12 while the model writes BFS every time. (ii) DFS and unit-weight Dijkstra are also the model's typical runner-ups (free-form answers, base model), so proximity and typicality are not separated. On the grid event the geodesic kernel scored -1.337, behind the free-form answer (-0.112) and the listing control (-0.061). (iii) The claim rests on 18 compliant programs plus exploratory step-2 events with 18 and 5. (iv) Geodesic stability was assessed only by resampling point clouds (results/contest.json, geodesic_share_same_nearest 0.985), which the final hypothesis review warned is uninformative. No k or layer sweep exists, and MDS stress-1 is 0.22. (v) results/manipulation_sensitivity.json, not in the report, recomputes the flagged centroids and puts bidirectional Dijkstra (40.91) closer to Dijkstra than Bellman-Ford/SPFA (42.18). So 'the mass went to the second nearest centroid, Bellman-Ford/SPFA' does not survive the artifact's own sensitivity analysis. (vi) The request's literal test, prohibiting the top five, was not run.
critiques.suggested_action: Report the sensitivity matrix next to Table 12. From cache/hR_layer*.npy (CPU only), recompute the geodesic nearest neighbours for k in {5, 10, 15, 20} x every layer in the gate bands (24-28 for the grid task, 21-27 for the shortest-path task) and report rank stability. Rephrase item 6 as 'consistent with geodesic proximity and with typicality; not separated on these events'. Expected impact: +0.25 to +0.5, and it prevents an overclaim from reaching the paper.

critiques.description: The locus-diagnostic dead end is recorded but its cause is not, and the cause changes what to do next. gen_art_experiment_3/probes.json is 28 bytes ('{"summary": {}, "cells": {}}') with mtime 18:29. logs/states.out logs 'T1: states (300, 8, 21, 4096) saved' at 18:34:34 and T2 at 18:34:50. The probe stage ran before its inputs existed. The states are on disk (states/T{1,2}_part_001-005.npz, 790 MB, read-position cosine >= 0.9997), so the measurement that decides whether every geometric analysis should move to generated tokens is a CPU-only re-run, not a missing experiment. The report calls it 'a technical failure, not a negative result' but gives the next iteration no route to it.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the timestamps and the state file locations to the dead-end entry. Make 'run the locus probe on the saved states (read position, generated tokens 8/16/32/64, fork and commitment positions vs shuffled labels; the preregistered 20-point rule)' the first step of the next iteration, before any new generation. Expected impact: resolves an undetermined preregistered diagnostic at near-zero cost.

critiques.description: Coverage against the original request is partial. Not addressed: (1) 'analyze with thought anchors, NLA, SAE'. None was run, j-lens is never mapped, and the logit lens appears only for the sharpening direction. (2) 'prohibit the top 5 in prompt, and see if the implemented count moves to the edge of those 5, or to the opposite side'. It was never run. The report says the succession 'could not reach' it, but a simultaneous five-name ban is a single prompt condition that needs no greedy succession. (3) 'analyze the internals, all the runs that produced BFS vs all runs that produced DFS vs dijkstra'. Only forced-prompt centroids were analysed, although natural BFS and DFS runs under the ban exist with saved states (exp3: 300 per task). (4) Question 1's '(always same seed)'. Common random numbers across temperature cells were not used, and same-seed determinism failed in vLLM (39/64 identical texts; failed on the grid task in the decommitment experiment). The report lists SAE, thought anchors and the top-five ban as open, but not (3), (4), NLA or j-lens.
critiques.suggested_action: List every unaddressed request item in the open-questions paragraph with a planned artifact. Run the simultaneous ban of 5 of the 6 grid algorithms, leaving each survivor in turn, and of 4 of the 5 shortest-path algorithms, or extend the catalogue toward the ten algorithms the request imagines. Probe the BFS-labelled versus DFS-labelled natural ban runs from the exp3 states. Use a public SAE where one exists for the model, or switch the mechanistic arm to a model with released SAEs. Run thought-anchor resampling on the thinking-on traces that exp6 already has (raise the 2,048-token cap so traces complete). Expected impact: +0.5 to +1 on coverage.

critiques.description: No positive claim is compared with its nearest published neighbour, so none has earned novelty credit in this record. (a) 'Temperature is a phrasing knob' and the ideas-by-phrasings split sit next to Lee et al. 2026, 'Are We Measuring Strategy or Phrasing?' (arXiv 2606.29985, ICML 2026: diversity metrics capture surface variation, not approach), Peeperkorn et al. 2024 [37], and NoveltyBench (arXiv 2504.05228). (b) Generate-then-select is the SimpleStrat mechanism: model-proposed strata, then an external random choice (Wong et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2410.09038), which also shows that temperature does not buy coverage. Its diversity is imposed by the experimenter's random draw, so it is closer to forced implementation than to model choice and should not sit in the BUY column as a knob on equal footing. (c) The free-form and listing-control predictors and the 'sharpened by post-training' reading neighbour Verbalized Sampling (Zhang et al. 2025, arXiv 2510.01171: mode collapse from typicality bias in preference data, recovered by verbalised distributions), Kirk et al. (ICLR 2024) and West et al. 2025 [35]. (d) Approach-organised internal states neighbour Goudarzi et al. 2026 (arXiv 2609.27041), which the final hypothesis review flagged and the report omits. (e) Bans re-collapsing onto SPFA/Bellman-Ford were already seen in the inspiration repository, and constraint violation under denial prompting in Lu et al. [23].
critiques.suggested_action: For each positive claim add one line: the nearest neighbour, then what this run adds. Candidate additions: a five-draw replication with mechanism-level labels on an open model; within-model compliance driven by wording (0.09-0.72); the inversion of the mention twin against the sham-ban control; disguise counts (41/94, 58/100); and the read-position double dissociation for seeds. Where nothing is added (generate-then-select versus SimpleStrat, the temperature result versus Peeperkorn/Lee), say it is a replication on code. Expected impact: +0.25 to +0.5.

critiques.description: The read-position evidence on seeds, which bears directly on the request's hypothesis 2 ('only context pushes you into a different subspace'), is half-reported. The report says that on the grid task the semantic seed's displacement pointed toward the implied centroid (cos 0.493) while the output did not follow. It omits the other half from the same file (analysis.json, forecast_check P5): on the shortest-path task the displacement did NOT point toward the Bellman-Ford centroid (cos -0.087), yet behaviour moved +66.30 pp toward it. The report's '67 points toward Bellman-Ford/SPFA' is the Dijkstra-share drop (-67.39); the implied-mode gain is 66.30. Also omitted: the word seed shifted the grid probe-decoded distribution toward A* by +0.88 with zero behavioural change. The shortest-path entropy seed's 90% CI upper bound is 1.596, above the 1.5 bound, yet the report says it 'stayed within the paraphrase noise'. Together these are a double dissociation: displacement along the forced-prompt mode subspace predicts behavioural movement in neither direction.
critiques.suggested_action: Add both halves, the probe shifts and the entropy-seed interval to Section 1.10. Correct 67 -> 66.3 for the shift toward Bellman-Ford/SPFA. Revise established item 3 and the summary: read-position displacement in the mode subspace did not predict which algorithm the output moved to, on either task. Expected impact: +0.25. It is the run's most direct evidence on the user's subspace hypothesis.

critiques.description: The reasoning behind the iteration is only partly recorded. The report gives the hypothesis-review scores (verified: 5,6,6,7,7,7,7) but not what the final review objected to, or whether the screen answered it. Several objections are settled by this iteration's data and should be linked. (i) The review said S1's equivalence prediction was inconsistent with the negation-promotion mechanism: if processing a negation promotes an associate, bans of absent algorithms should still move mass toward a related algorithm. Two of nine sham bans did so (ban Floyd-Warshall -> Bellman-Ford/SPFA 23%; ban IDDFS -> DFS 12%). The report lists these shifts but files the sham control only as untestable, without saying what they mean for the mechanism. (ii) The review raised self-simulation (Binder et al., ICLR 2025) as a rival reason why the model's own stated alternative predicts its behaviour. That is exactly the free-form predictor's success. (iii) The review warned that point-cloud resampling would make geodesic stability uninformative. (iv) It flagged the missing Goudarzi et al. precedent and the unmapped j-lens.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short subsection to Section 1.1 or 1.12, 'What the hypothesis review asked for and what the screen showed', with one line per objection and the evidence that now answers it. In particular, re-read the sham-ban vs baseline shifts as a (weak, 2 of 9 events) test of negation-triggered promotion, and state self-simulation as a live account of the free-form result. Expected impact: +0.25 on contribution.

critiques.description: Executed outputs missing from the record. Association experiment: 11 forced-implementation conditions (N=10 each, e.g. forced IDDFS 0/10 pass, forced Dial 0/10, forced bidirectional Dijkstra written as plain Dijkstra 10/10), although Table 6 is captioned 'Every condition'; and the sharpness-matched in-sample scores (association -1.386 vs frequency -1.475). Forking token: summaries/next_token.json (next-token entropies at fork candidates vs controls), confirmation-threshold sensitivity (grid candidate T1|ban|0 confirms at TVD 0.10 and 0.15 but not 0.20), and engine tests (greedy prefix identity 0.14 at 10 tokens). Decommitment: the c=1 arms at layers 14 and 22 (N=10 each, pass 0). Geometry: Procrustes disparity 0.18/0.25 and the pre-declared components that were dropped (external-model elicitation, LOCO decoder). Decoding: the all-label composition of the shortest-path enumeration arm (Bellman-Ford/SPFA 33 written, 8 correct).
critiques.suggested_action: Add these as table rows or single sentences with their file names (data/samples.jsonl conditions 'forced:*'; summaries/next_token.json; forks.json 'confirmed_tvd0.10/0.15'; logs/test_engine.json; results/deviations.json). Expected impact: small, but it completes the record the paper step draws on.

critiques.description: Established item 8 ('Post-training sharpened an ordering the base model already had, rather than installing a new attractor') relabels a preregistered verdict, INSTALLED_BY_POST_TRAINING on the shortest-path task (MIXED on the grid task; MIXED on both at the planned N). Its support is thin: the base model under the chat template parses only 0.58/0.66 and yields 57/90 correct programs, the base arms are mostly judge-labelled (runtime vs AST kappa 0.20-0.50), and in plain completion the base model's shortest-path mode is Bellman-Ford/SPFA (16 of 25 correct), first rather than second.
critiques.suggested_action: Keep the preregistered verdict label beside the interpretation. Give the base-model counts with intervals. Say that the base model's ordering matches the instruct model's only under the chat template.

critiques.description: Bookkeeping and traceability gaps. GPU hours are missing for the forking token, decommitment and decoding experiments. Tables carry artifact markers but not the result file each was compiled from. The forking-token artifact has no README. Because 'compliant = correct' drives every grid number, the grid failure taxonomy belongs in the record. In the association experiment, 161 of 273 DFS programs fail (127 wrong answers, 81 of them on three_by_three_blocked and 35 on two_by_two_open; 31 timeouts; 3 runtime errors). My re-run shows this is not an I/O artefact: reading a None return as [] rescues only 2-3 programs per condition (ban BFS: DFS 38 -> 40).
critiques.suggested_action: Fill GPU hours from each artifact's logs (exp3 logs/throughput.log, exp4 and exp6 logs). Name the source file under each table. Add a one-line failure taxonomy per grid condition, so readers know that low grid compliance reflects DFS implementation bugs rather than test bias.

dimension_scores.justification: Set by the review rule. Two conclusions contradict the report's own tables. First, the grid-task claim that the substitute replicated in five draws is contradicted by the geometry draw: DFS 10 / unit-weight Dijkstra 8, which Section 1.6 calls no clear mode. Second, 'no grid knob at the 80% floor produced a second algorithm among compliant programs' is contradicted by Table 37's decommitment row (16 compliant: unit-weight Dijkstra 13, A* 3) and by Table 13 (18 compliant, unit-weight Dijkstra). The underlying measurements are sound and reproduce. Further soundness defects: the selection rule is misreported and misapplied (informative-event gate omitted, BUY tie decided on one task, mixed Hill statistics); the geodesic-neighbour claim is presented as established despite a failed grid gate and no k/layer robustness; and 'sharpened, not installed' relabels a preregistered INSTALLED_BY_POST_TRAINING verdict.

A researcher who was not on the run can follow the record in order. Each experiment has why / design / results / what it settled, each table is introduced by the question it answers, and the conventions (read position, compliant sample, realised mode, Hill_cc, log score) are defined once in Section 1.2. It loses a point on three counts. Table 37 mixes raw Hill_cc with rarefied delta-Hill against different references. Table 26 reports Hill without label composition, which hides a complete Dijkstra-to-Bellman-Ford flip. Tables are tied to artifacts but not to the result file each came from.

Almost the whole run is preserved: all seven artifacts, their tables with correct numbers, dead ends with evidence, spend and review scores. Missing: the association experiment's 11 forced-implementation conditions (N=10 each), although Table 6 claims 'every condition'; the geometry manipulation-sensitivity matrix, which changes the shortest-path rank; the forking-token next-token entropies and confirmation-threshold sensitivity; the decommitment layer-14/22 arms; the label compositions of the steering arms; the shortest-path semantic-seed direction result (cos -0.087); the cause of the empty probes.json; GPU hours for four experiments; and the content of the hypothesis review's objections.

review.overall_assessment: This is the iteration-1 record of a six-account screen of algorithm choice in Qwen3-8B on the request's two path-search tasks (seven artifacts: one dataset, six experiments). As a lab record it is unusually complete and accurate. Every executed artifact is written up with its tables, the dead ends are kept with the evidence that killed them, and the preregistration bookkeeping (hash-committed forecasts with commit times, spend, the hypothesis-review scores 5,6,6,7,7,7,7, which I checked) is preserved. I recomputed the sample-level tables from each artifact's per-sample rows and found no mismatch. This covers Table 3 (61,469 examples; inspiration-repo labels Dijkstra 132 / Bellman-Ford-SPFA 34 / ...), Table 4 (1,199/1,200 BFS; 1,174/1,200 Dijkstra), all 40 conditions of Table 6 including Hill_cc, Tables 11, 13 and 16 (geometry), the label counts of Table 22, Table 24, Tables 27 and 31, and Table 34. By hand I recomputed the Table 7 log scores (-2.817, -0.755, -1.630, -1.406, -0.112, -0.061) and the Table 14 geodesic score (-1.337, median centroid distance 71.06). I also re-ran the association experiment's grid hidden tests on 250 programs and reproduced the artifact's pass/fail labels on 250 of 250. Bootstrap intervals, slopes and activation statistics (Tables 15, 25, 29, 32, 33) were checked against the artifacts' result files (for example analysis.json subspace_test), not recomputed from raw activations, and I treat them as verified-by-file. No projected, illustrative or placeholder number was found, so results_reported is true. BLOCKING: two conclusions contradict the report's own tables, so by rule soundness is 1 and blocking is true. (1) The headline that the post-ban substitute 'replicated in five independent draws' ('landed on the same substitute every time', 'collapses again on one substitute') is false for the grid task. In the geometry draw the 18 compliant programs split DFS 10 / unit-weight Dijkstra 8, and Section 1.6 itself calls this 'no clear realised mode'. (2) Section 1.11 states 'On the grid task no knob that kept 80% of the pass rate produced a second algorithm among compliant programs'. Table 37's own decommitment row contradicts it (cumulative BFS+DFS ban, pass 0.88 of 1.00, 16 compliant programs: unit-weight Dijkstra 13, A* 3), and so does Table 13 (geometry BFS+DFS ban, pass 0.96, 18 compliant, all unit-weight Dijkstra). The measurements are sound. The fix is to rewrite these conclusions and to re-run the selection rule as preregistered. Section 1.1 omits the PREDICT gate that defines an informative event (compliance >= 50%, >= 2 survivors). Under either compliance definition, the geometry and instruction-tuning modal events and the decommitment shortest-path event fail that gate, yet Tables 14 and 36 score them, and the BUY tie is decided on one task although the rule asks for pooled tasks plus the same direction on each. Other major gaps: (a) the random-direction controls move the shortest-path task to the same substitute (exp5 random-2: 33/33 correct programs Bellman-Ford/SPFA, shown in Table 26 only as 'Hill 1.00, delta 0'). This is a generic-perturbation rival to ban-specific promotion, and the report never states it. (b) The geodesic-neighbour claim rests on a failed grid read-position gate. It is confounded with typicality, has no k/layer robustness check, and an unreported sensitivity file reverses the shortest-path rank. (c) The locus probe ran at 18:29, before its states were saved at 18:34, so it is a CPU-only re-run, but the report does not record this cause. (d) The read-position evidence on seeds is half-reported: on the shortest-path task the semantic seed's displacement points away from the implied centroid (cos -0.087) while behaviour moves 66 pp toward it. (e) The final hypothesis review's objections are not recorded. (f) No positive claim is compared with its nearest published neighbour (SimpleStrat, Verbalized Sampling, Lee et al. 2026, Goudarzi et al. 2026). (g) The iteration added forecasters (15 families) to two informative events instead of adding events. Coverage of the request is partial: SAE, thought anchors, NLA and j-lens are absent, the top-5 prohibition was never run, and the internals of natural BFS versus DFS runs were not analysed. Score 4: the descriptive behavioural findings are solid and reproducible (total collapse, temperature as a phrasing knob, bans that re-collapse onto a substitute, ban compliance driven by wording). The mechanistic hypothesis is untested, the scope is one model and two tasks, and the positive findings sit close to published work.
strengths: Completeness verified by recomputation, not taken on trust. Every one of the seven artifacts is written up, and the sample-level tables I rebuilt from the per-sample JSONL rows match the report to the last digit: Tables 3, 4, 6 (all 40 conditions, including Hill_cc), 11, 13, 16, 22 (label counts), 24, 27, 31 and 34. The Table 7 and Table 14 log scores also match when recomputed by hand. An independent re-run of the grid hidden tests reproduced the association experiment's pass/fail labels on 250 of 250 programs.

Dead ends are kept and labelled with the evidence that killed them. Affine ablation moved 0/50 at alpha <= 2 with 78-90% of texts byte-identical to alpha=0. Sharpening subtraction left 0/100 programs parseable. The forking-window temperature arms were 100% the default. The decommitment direction did no better than a random direction (+0.07 [-0.26, 0.39]). The Borda map was unstable across two elicitations. Typicality is uniform under total collapse. Mention twins act as recommendations. The locus probe failed and the reserved bench was never built. The paper step will know these were tried.

The preregistration bookkeeping is preserved in the record: commit times precede first generation in each experiment (for example 15:18:30 vs 15:20:05 UTC; sha256 186f7182... at 16:36:57), along with spend per artifact and the hypothesis-review score trajectory, which matches the review files (5,6,6,7,7,7,7; final soundness 3, presentation 3, contribution 3, fidelity 4).

The replicated-draw design yields a real, correctly drawn finding. Five independent draws of the same modal ban (Table 34, which I recomputed) show that compliance depends on the ban sentence: banned share 0.09-0.72, with per-paraphrase counts from 0/10 to 10/10. The report states the right consequence: any ladder-limit analysis must hold wording fixed or model it.

Limits are stated without selling. The section on what iteration 1 established is explicitly descriptive. The labeller gate failures are disclosed with their numbers (Table 2). The Hill_cc flaw (correct banned programs count as a second idea) is admitted. The two conflicting 'compliance' definitions are neutralised by reporting banned share and compliant counts recomputed from rows. The central quantitative hypothesis is declared untested rather than confirmed.

Direct, data-backed answers to the request's literal questions 1a-c and 2. The BFS share is 797/800 (thinking off) and 800/800 (thinking on) across 4 temperatures x 2 samplers. A full ideas-by-phrasings table is given at three Jaccard thresholds with bootstrap slopes. The seed equivalence tests sit within +/-15 pp. The requested activation-space manifold plot with centroids coloured by implemented count exists (geometry artifact figures/manifold_t1.png).

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration the pool holds, on the same two path-search tasks and the same Qwen3-8B ban events: (1) hash-committed predictions and realised post-ban distributions for five predictor families (association, frequency, geodesic, de-committed survivor, base-model survivor) with per-sample rows in one schema; (2) BUY rows for eight knobs (single and cumulative prompt bans, affine removal, de-commitment addition, sharpening subtraction, fork-only temperature, global temperature and top-k, seeds and creativity instructions), each with pass rate and correctness-conditioned Hill number at matched correctness; (3) the LOCUS diagnostic (decoder accuracy at R versus at forks and the pre-commitment token); (4) the request's literal figures (BFS fraction by temperature, the manifold with centroids coloured by implemented count, the prohibition landing table, the ideas-by-phrasings table); and (5) the reserved bench of 8-14 tasks with gate verdicts and frozen pre-ban nominations. NEXT ITERATION: an evaluation artifact compiles the scorecard under the selection rule stated in the rationale (PREDICT survivor: highest mean log score on discordant events with a >= 0.10 nat margin over >= 3 events; BUY survivor: highest Hill number at >= 80% of baseline pass rate with a >= 0.5 margin; LOCUS: >= 20 points over R moves geometry to trajectory states) and checks that independent draws of the same ban event across experiments agree on the realised mode; the surviving account (or the top two) is then confirmed as a DEEP TEST on the reserved tasks using the dataset artifact's frozen nominations, with one reserve task held out as the H1 forecast, before anything is claimed. Nothing in this iteration is inferential; every contest is descriptive with intervals and effective N.
strategies.objective: A pre-registered, coarse, head-to-head screen of five rival accounts of why an instruction-tuned LLM re-collapses on one algorithm and what moves it: substitution by association (main), the typicality ladder, manifold geometry at the read position, fork-token decisions during generation, the de-commitment frame direction, and instruction-tuning sharpening; all screened on the same Qwen3-8B events on the request's two path-search tasks with one two-column scorecard, PREDICT (log score and top-1 hit of each account's hash-committed prediction of the post-ban distribution) and BUY (correctness-conditioned effective number of algorithms at >= 80% of the baseline pass rate for each account's knob), plus a reserved 12-task bench with validated labellers and frozen pre-ban nominations on which the survivor is confirmed next iteration. The literal deliverables of the request (BFS fraction by temperature, the path-search manifold with centroids coloured by implemented count, the prohibition landing test, the ideas-by-phrasings table) come out of the same screen.
strategies.rationale: This is the first iteration and the hypothesis carries four alternates that disagree with it about the answer: whether the post-ban mode is set by the model's textbook association (main), by baseline typicality (alt 2), by manifold proximity (the geometric predictor inside the main design), by a decision made at fork tokens during generation rather than before it (alt 3), by a single commitment direction (alt 1), or by a post-training sharpening the base model lacks (alt 4). Only one of these has ever been in play. The right first move is a wide screen, not a deep test: run all of them cheaply on the same evidence, with the same measure and a selection rule stated now, and confirm the survivor on reserved tasks. SELECTION RULE (fixed before any artifact runs). Shared evidence: the ban events of tasks T1 and T2 on Qwen3-8B thinking-off under the shared protocol (every named single ban, the mention twin, the list-all control, greedy succession), scored by the shared labeller. PREDICT column: for each predictor family that can name a post-ban distribution (association Borda map [main], latent frequency [typicality], geodesic kernel [geometry], de-committed survivor distribution [de-commitment], base-model survivor distribution [instruction tuning]) the raw log score of the realised compliant samples with the same 5% uniform mix over survivors and the same 2% 'other' floor, plus the top-1 hit, on every informative event (banned mode present at >= 10% of the latent baseline, compliance >= 50%, >= 2 survivors). The PREDICT survivor is the family with the highest mean log score on the events where the families' top-1 nominations disagree, if its margin over the runner-up is >= 0.10 nats and there are >= 3 such events; otherwise the top two both advance. BUY column: for each knob (prompt ban single and cumulative; affine removal; de-commitment addition; sharpening subtraction; fork-only temperature; global temperature and top-k; seeds and creativity instructions) the correctness-conditioned Hill number at the strongest setting that keeps the pass rate >= 80% of baseline, with a sample-bootstrap 90% interval; the BUY survivor is the knob with the highest such Hill number if it beats the runner-up by >= 0.5 effective algorithms on the pooled tasks and in direction on each task; otherwise the top two advance. LOCUS diagnostic: if the decoder of the final mode from generated-token states at the detected fork or the pre-commitment token beats the read-position decoder by >= 20 points over shuffled, the confirmation iteration builds every geometric contest on trajectory states, as the hypothesis's own gate prescribes. Because the six experiments run in parallel, each computes its candidate's column on its own draw of the shared events and publishes per-sample rows in one schema; the cross-candidate scorecard and the cross-experiment replication check (do independent draws of the same ban event agree on the realised mode?) are compiled by an evaluation artifact next iteration, before the deep test on the reserved bench. POSITIVE TARGET: the screen is built so that at least one row comes out positive on two tasks where the collapse is strongest (the Invisible Lottery prior gives Dijkstra at 94% with no cue): a predictor that names the post-ban algorithm where its rivals do not, or a knob that buys a second correct algorithm at under 20 points of pass rate. The screen's two tasks also produce, first, the request's literal figures, so the minimum publishable result exists after this iteration. SHARED SCREEN PROTOCOL (identical in every experiment of this iteration; deviations must be logged in method_out.json under 'deviations'). MODEL: Qwen/Qwen3-8B in bf16 with thinking OFF (chat template with enable_thinking=False), generation through vLLM (gpu_memory_utilization about 0.92, max_model_len 2048, max_num_seqs 16, fixed seed); the GPU is one RTX A4500 with 20 GB, so load vLLM and HF-transformers hooks SEQUENTIALLY (free one before the other), never both; if Qwen3-8B does not fit, fall back to Qwen/Qwen3-4B and write the model id into every output row (results are pooled per model next iteration). TASKS (the request's two path-search tasks): T1 unweighted grid path search (grid rows of '.' and '#', start and goal cells; return any valid 4-neighbour path as a list of (r,c) or [] if unreachable; catalogue: BFS, DFS, bidirectional BFS, iterative-deepening DFS, A*/greedy best-first with Manhattan heuristic, unit-weight Dijkstra; grids at most 30x30 so every catalogue algorithm passes); T2 weighted shortest path (directed graph, n <= 100 nodes, non-negative integer weights <= 100, cycles allowed; return the shortest distance s->t or -1; catalogue: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford/SPFA, bidirectional Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall, Dial's bucket queue; sizes chosen so Floyd-Warshall passes). Hidden tests: at least 40 cases per task incl. edge cases, written by the executor, with a wall-clock limit of 10x the reference solution (minimum 1 s) in a subprocess; every catalogue reference implementation must pass before any model sample is scored. PROMPT SCAFFOLD: [condition segment] + [fixed shared task specification and I/O format, >= 50 tokens, identical across conditions: 'Write a Python function solve(...) ...; return only one ```python code block'] + chat-template assistant header; the read position R is the last prompt token, so no condition-specific token sits at or near R. Conditions share these names: baseline; ban:X = 'Do not use X.'; mention:X = 'X is one well-known approach to this task; implement any correct algorithm.'; listall = 'Known approaches include <all catalogue names>; implement any correct algorithm.'; succession:k = cumulative ban of the realised modes of steps < k. Condition segments get 10 paraphrases (the task spec is never paraphrased); N=100 per condition means 10 paraphrases x 10 samples. DECODING: T=1.0, top-p=1.0, max_new_tokens 1024 for the screen arms unless an arm says otherwise. LABELLING: label in catalogue + {'other'} by (1) a runtime-signature tracer (run the program on crafted inputs with heapq, collections.deque, dict/set/list/sorted/bisect wrapped to record usage, node expansion order, and negative-weight handling) and (2) AST rules; disagreements or no match go to a blind LLM judge via OpenRouter (a cheap model, <= 1 USD per artifact, rationale stored); recursion vs iteration is never a separate mode; correct := passes the hidden tests within the limit. Compliant := correct and not labelled with a banned mode. Realised mode := modal compliant label if it leads the runner-up by >= 15 points, else 'no clear mode'. Hill number := exp(Shannon entropy) of the label distribution over correct samples. OUTPUT SCHEMA (so a single evaluation can pool all experiments): per-sample JSONL rows {task, condition, paraphrase_id, sample_id, model, decoding, label, labeller_source, passed, wall_s, code_sha256, code}; per-condition summaries {label_counts, pass_rate, hill_cc, wilson_ci}; any prediction file is written and its sha256 logged BEFORE the corresponding samples are generated (hash-committed forecast). Every arm scales in stages (10 -> 100 -> full) with a time-per-sample extrapolation logged before the full run.

artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_7
artifacts.summary: FRLP output-space screen of claim C1 (do prompt-level algorithm bans on Qwen3-8B pick a specific substitute or move mass along a generic ladder?) on the two iteration-1 path-search tasks (T1 grid, 6 algorithms; T2 weighted shortest path, 5). (3) FRLP cells (yield-corrected mixture-proposal importance sampling, ESS per cell; results/frlp_cells.jsonl, 6 variants). (4) FRLP gate vs 19 exp1 sampled events: primary FAIL on calibration (a) (m=0.83<0.9: scrubbed programs give DFS mass under the T1 baseline), PASS on (b) 0.92 nats and (c) 16/19; 98% of gate cells have ESS<5. Diagnostic: the UNSCRUBBED variant passes all three (S=0.95, m=1.00; 1.18 nats; 17/19), so the failure is a name-scrubbing artifact; single-proposal also passes (reported, not adopted). (5) C1 (descriptive): pooled X-specific SHARE 0.55 [0.25, 0.67] (neutral twins), 0.66 [0.49, 0.87] (mention twins) -> pooled branch UNDETERMINED, robust across both references and the ESS-weighted variant; T1 is X-SPECIFIC-UNAIMED under the mention reference. Residuals are not aimed at the prime-and-veto profile (AIM -0.10, null p95 0.20, p=0.80) or free-form association (p=0.77); the 8 generic profiles do not form a coherent ladder (mean centred cosine 0.34 T1, -0.02 T2). Unscrubbed W1-only sensitivity: SHARE 0.69 [0.51, 0.84] (X-specific). Bans of absent algorithms raise their own FRLP (priming, +2.5 to +27 nats). artifacts.layman_summary: We tested how a 'do not use BFS / Dijkstra' instruction reaches a code-writing AI model's choice by swapping parts of its memory between banned and neutral prompts.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_8
artifacts.summary: Causal route test (C2) and compliance-at-R test (C5) for prompt-level algorithm bans in Qwen/Qwen3-8B (bf16, thinking off, Hub revision b968826d) on iteration 1's canonical tasks: T1 grid path with 'ban BFS' and T2 weighted shortest path with 'ban Dijkstra'. Each of 5 frozen ban templates has a token-length-matched neutral twin (irrelevant nouns in the same prohibition frame; identical ids from 'Task:' on), so the KV caches of the two prompts are spliced position by position. Arms: a full ban, b neutral (baseline), c PROMPT ROUTE (neutral condition span plus ban task-spec/R states), d DIRECT ROUTE (ban condition span plus neutral task-spec/R states), R-only, task-spec-only, placebo splice, condition-span attention knockouts (all generated tokens; first 16; after 16; layers 0-11/12-23/24-35) and a neutral-prompt knockout control. PRIMARY readout (FRLP drop of the banned algorithm over 30 self-written, name-scrubbed programs; decision rule sha256-committed before scoring): DECIDED BEFORE WRITING, carried by the prompt route, ROBUST across both tasks. Pooled F_prompt = 0.85 [0.61, 1.20] and F_direct = 0.00 [-0.08, 0.12]. Per task F_prompt is 0.87 (T1) and 0.82 (T2). R alone carries nothing (F_R about 0); the task-spec states carry it (F_spec 0.86/0.81). Placebo splice: about 1% of the effect. All four pre-declared sensitivities agree. BEHAVIOUR (common random numbers, N = 100 per arm) qualifies T1. Banned share for a/b/c/d is 0.14/1.00/0.57/0.70 in T1 and 0.11/0.99/0.13/0.95 in T2. A supplementary full-knockout arm restores T1 BFS to 0.47 but leaves T2 at 0.06. Mechanism: the ban suppresses the default first line ('from collections import deque' / 'import heapq'), and this opening veto is fully prompt-carried (0% import openings under a, c and the knockouts; 85% under d). In T1 the in-body algorithm choice also needs direct reads of the ban. A supplementary natural-proposal readout gives pooled F_prompt 0.57 and F_direct 0.16 (super-additive). FRLP weights are degenerate for T1 (ESS 1-3), so likelihood readouts measure the opening veto, not calibrated probability ratios. Lens: the fork precedes the signature token (no veto layer at it); the substitute set rises from about layer 28. C5: on 110 wordings (exp1-exp5 plus 10 new cells), the combined within-cell Spearman of banned share against the h_R projection on a leave-one-experiment-out ban direction is -0.41 [-0.69, -0.17], p = 0.0003 (Holm 0.0006). That is PARTIAL against the -0.5 bar; the ceiling is 0.77 and 98.5% of random directions are weaker. The decommitment axis is NULL; the substitute is not decodable beyond the projection. FILES: method_out.json and its full/mini/preview variants (1,400 behaviour samples, 110 C5 wordings, 130 FRLP route cells, every analysis in metadata); results/analysis.json, supplementary.json, c5.json, lens.json, natural_frlp.json, prereg.json, tests.json; data/samples.jsonl, frlp_programs.jsonl, frlp_scores.jsonl, token_lp/*.npz; figures fig1-fig6; reproducibility.md. Audits: 59 + 49 numbers re-derived independently with 0 mismatches, and every placebo/shuffle test fails. OpenRouter spend USD 0.32.

artifacts.layman_summary: Tests what Qwen3-8B writes when told not to use its usual path-finding algorithms: with four or five names banned at once it mostly writes the banned ones anyway, often without naming them.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_9
artifacts.summary: Qwen3-8B (thinking off, vLLM 0.11, T=1.0) multi-name ban study on the iteration-1 grid-path (T1) and weighted-shortest-path (T2) suite, with mechanism-level labels (runtime tracer + AST + blind judge). The grid catalogue was extended to 10 algorithms (greedy split from A*, IDA*, JPS4, bidirectional A*) with new references (25/25 runtime and AST) and unit probes (4/4). The canonical labeller re-check gave 135/144 and 22/22. The 40-program gold gate was missed (33/40, then 32/40 after one revision; kappa 0.53), excluding unit-weight Dijkstra, JPS and bidirectional A*. KEEP RULE (>=70% of 40 forced programs labelled as requested): only BFS, DFS, IDDFS, greedy and IDA* pass, so the extension failed (F4). The analysis catalogue (K=7) adds A* and BiBFS (flagged), giving 4-name TOP/ARC/SCATTER bans plus the literal five-name TOP5. FRLP cells (about 17k teacher-forced passes: ban, mention and neutral twins, nonce, LOS, tier 3) and six landing forecasts per set (LADDER, PRIME_AND_VETO, PROXIMITY, FRLP_BAN, GENERIC, CORPUS) were sha256 hash-chained before sampling; the chain verifies and the commit precedes session 2. RESULTS (N=100 per condition, 5 templates x 20): single bans work (T1 ban BFS: DFS 86, avoidance 0.86; T2 ban Dijkstra: BF/SPFA 83, avoidance 0.84). Every multi-ban fails its gate: TOP (BFS, DFS, greedy, IDDFS) avoidance 0.13; ARC (BFS, BiBFS, A*, greedy) 0.37 (DFS 37 survivor); SCATTER (BFS, DFS, greedy, IDA*) 0.04; TOP5 (adds A*) 0.00 (BFS 63, DFS 36). The banned BFS/DFS is re-implemented, 41-92% of the time without naming it ('backtracking'). FRLP-implied avoidance foresaw the failure (<1e-8 for TOP, SCATTER and TOP5) but not ARC (0.9995 vs 0.37). Ban prompts raise the likelihood of the banned programs relative to neutral twins (priming). Landing rank tests are degenerate (survivor mass only in ARC and SCATTER; exact permutation p >= 0.33 per set, >= 0.11 pooled). On ARC the ladder-type forecasts hit DFS (+1.06 nats/program over uniform) and PROXIMITY missed. T2 leave-one-survivor: 'will' Dijkstra 0.95, BF/SPFA 0.51, BiDijkstra/Floyd/Dial 0.00, despite 'can' 0.35/1.0/0.9 when forced. Geometry: centroid MDS stress-1 0.025/0.006; neighbours BFS-BiBFS, DFS-IDDFS, A*-greedy; no persistent H1 loop. Within-ban probes at g16 are near chance on T1 and 0.69 balanced accuracy on T2 LOS(BF/SPFA) (p=0.03); 'pre' probes are a position artefact. POST HOC (not pre-registered): the BFS/DFS mix is the same across the four multi-bans (BFS share 0.63-0.72, chi-square p=0.48) whether or not DFS is on the list. A long ban list therefore acts like a generic perturbation of the default (about 1/3 DFS) rather than a list-specific veto, while a single BFS ban moves the model to 86% DFS. Every method_out example carries predict_default (no change) and predict_ladder. Multi-ban rows also carry the committed top-1 forecasts: on multi-bans the default is right 64% of the time versus at most 10% for any survivor forecast. Caveats: FRLP ESS < 5 in 97% of cells; bf16 scoring noise of about 1 nat per program; T2 sum exp(L) is 0.17. FILES: method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out, 1,950 programs with labels, tests and predict_* top-1 forecasts), data/samples.jsonl, results/*.json (landing, los, frlp_cells.jsonl, sets_and_geometry, manifold, persistence, catalogue_keep, labeller validation, checks, deviations, independent_rederivation), predictions/, commitments.log and figures/. The states/ activations (0.95 GB) are kept on the run volume and not published. Cost: about 1 GPU-hour on an RTX 4090 and USD 0.42 of judge calls.

artifacts.layman_summary: Tests on a second AI model (Llama) whether telling it 'do not use algorithm X' pushes it toward one specific replacement or just a generic fallback, using the same frozen prompts and analysis as the main study.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_10
artifacts.summary: Second-model-family replication of the iteration-2 ban screen on meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (bf16, default chat template, revision 0e9e39f). It uses the frozen SHARED PROTOCOL v2 (templates W1-W5, v2 display names, nonce ban, novelty instruction), exp1's canonical task suite and labeller (copied into canon/ with SHA256SUMS), and the 718-noun bank of art_j3Rm_lr2nzR6 re-tokenised under Llama (nouns 'man'/'guy'). PROVIDES: (1) 1,780 seeded vLLM generations with mechanism labels (data/samples.jsonl, data/labelled.jsonl): baselines, modal bans, mention twins, listall, two non-default bans and two-step bans per task (14 events), 880 forced programs and 220 free-form association answers. (2) 248 name-scrubbed self-written forced programs and 39,768 HF program scores (frlp/parts, frlp/scores_<task>.parquet), with FRLP cells and ESS in 5 variants (frlp/cells.jsonl). (3) Results in results/*.json and figures/. KEY FINDINGS (all descriptive: two tasks, one model). Llama's T1 baseline is NOT collapsed (BFS 77, DFS 20) and its pass rate is low (0.20). T2 is collapsed (Dijkstra 92, pass 0.59). Ban BFS -> DFS 63/100; ban Dijkstra -> Dijkstra 43, other 37, BF/SPFA 18. Both two-step bans fail (avoidance 0.16 and 0.44). On T2, bidirectional Dijkstra and Dial were unwritable (M <= 2 after 120 attempts), so K = 3 and no T2 row has 3 survivors: C1 is T1-only. The FRLP gate FAILS: (a) T1 implied BFS 0.43 vs sampled 0.77; (b) passes at 0.59 nats/sample; (c) 7/10. Median cell ESS is 2.5. C1 under the neutral reference: SHARE 0.80 (95% percentile CI 0.28-0.94) -> 'not resolved at this N'; no aim (prime-and-veto AIM 0.067 vs exact-null q95 0.258; association -0.08); no ladder (mean generic cosine 0.14). Under the mention reference: X-SPECIFIC BUT UNAIMED. Not robust. Post hoc: program-level importance-sampling noise dominates (bootstrap variance of gbar 5-11x the replicate Sigma; the basic interval for V_tot covers 0), and SHARE is fragile (0.41 without 5 audit-disputed programs). Naming an absent algorithm in a ban RAISES its FRLP in 5 of 6 cases (+1.8 to +7.6 nats; mention prime +6.7 to +14.4, veto -4.9 to -10.1). Route test (FRLP-only): the modal ban's own-drop travels mainly by the prompt route (F_prompt 0.84, CI 0.62-1.46; F_direct -0.21). Per-sample top-1 accuracy over 743 samples: the empirical sampled ladder (0.70) beats FRLP (0.59; paired p < 1e-4); on single bans they tie (0.67 vs 0.67). Labeller re-check reproduces exp1 (22/22, 0.966); the Llama label audit agrees at 0.78 (flagged). Tests T2-T11 are in results/; 97 numbers are independently re-derived (audit/). Deviations (30) are in results/deviations.json, including bf16 T4/T7 tolerance failures and the crossed-design noise bias. Cost: USD 0.49 OpenRouter, about 0.64 logged GPU-hours on one RTX 4090.

All 13 passed the labeller gate (kappa runtime-vs-AST 0.84-1.00, refs 100%, runtime vs adjudicated >= 0.91; T03/T13 after one revision round with holdout); 12 frozen in Stage-A order (bench/commitment.json + commitments.log hash chain), R2 excluded by the 12-task cap. Model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 via vLLM 0.11 FP8 Marlin, eager (16 GB GPU, no C compiler); T=1.0, top_p=1, thinking off. Pilot (data/samples_pilot.jsonl, 50/task): fully collapsed on all 13 tasks (modal share 1.00, R6 0.98; Wilson [0.929,1.0]); pass rate >= 0.92. Optional Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 pilot (data/samples_llama_pilot.jsonl) is far more diverse (e.g. T03 modal 0.34). Association: 20 free-form 'standard alternative to X' answers per mode (data/association.jsonl), near-deterministic. Forced programs: >=40 attempts/mode from exp1's paraphrases ids 0-4 (+ top-ups and a descriptive variant for low-adherence modes), name-scrubbed and verified (same tests, same runtime label), data/samples_forced.jsonl with labels and adherence (45/54 modes >= 0.5; R3 layering/source_removal, T13 interval_tree, R1 DP variants, T06 index_marking, T10 label_propagation low). Baseline FRLP cells (data/frlp_cells.jsonl; method_out dataset frlp_baseline_cells): log q = mixture over generating prompts, w = l(base) - log q, L_corr = logmeanexp(w) + log adherence, with Kish ESS (34/54 cells < 5), halves, generating-paraphrase-only and correct-only sensitivities; argmax(pi) = pilot mode 13/13, beats uniform log score 13/13 (placebos 0/13), S in [0.3,3] for 11/13. Stage-A order (assoc/proximity/ladder disagreement): T03,T04,T06,T05,T10,R1,T08,R3,T13,R6,T14,T11,R2; Stage-B (FRLP-broken ladder, forced-program proximity): Kendall tau 0.54. method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out): bench_candidates (13 rows with predict_ladder baseline vs predict_association / predict_proximity nominations, pilot stats, gate, FRLP, validity) + 54 FRLP cells.
