artifacts.layman_summary: Looks inside an AI model while it writes code under a ban on its favourite algorithm, comparing sparse-feature readouts with simple baselines, attention, and repeated sampling.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_12
artifacts.summary: Descriptive readout artifact on Qwen3-8B (bf16 states; FP8 twin for vLLM generation) for the iteration-1 path-search tasks under a ban on the modal algorithm (T1 grid: BFS banned; T2 weighted: Dijkstra banned). Provides method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out, 4 datasets, 1,122 examples: 200-run protocol-v2 fresh ban pool with per-run exp3-fitted readout predictions (SAE top-1/top-20 latents vs DiM / raw logistic / top-20-neuron baselines), 480 same-seed CRN rows, 10 thinking traces, 432 thought-anchor continuations) and per-readout JSON in results/. KEY RESULTS: (1) Fresh pool banned share T1 0.15 (W4 template 15/20 BFS, others 0/20), T2 0.13; labeller re-check 0.965; commit locator 20/20. (2) Qwen-Scope SAE (W64K, k=50) base->instruct transfer test FAILS at L15/L20/L27 (dCE ratio 3.29/1.95/1.59 > 1.5) -> all latent results flagged out-of-distribution; DiM leads. (3) Discovery on exp3 states (nested LOPO + 200 within-paraphrase permutations + max-stat null): T2 decodable at k_pre/k16 by every method (within-paraphrase AUC 0.67-0.86, p<=0.025); T1 not decodable within paraphrase; SAE latents never beat DiM/neurons beyond CIs. Positive control weak: exp3's commit token is the ' deque' import for most rows of both classes. (4) Replication on the fresh pool: exp3-fitted DiM transfers best (T1 within-template AUC 0.93-1.00, only W4 has both classes; T2 0.66-0.76); single top latent fails (0.27-0.80); shuffled-label placebo ~0.50. (5) Attention: same ban-specific heads on both tasks (L21H17, L26H21, L26H25; +0.21/+0.10 attention mass to the ban segment vs the token-matched neutral twin), focused on the banned name tokens; T1 compliant runs attend more (p=0.0025, within W4). (6) Prime-veto pattern absent in 6/6 configs; at L27 NAME(X) and IMPL(X) latents are lower at k_pre under the ban than under both twins for the same text. (7) Thought anchors: T1 thinking runs 8.4-9.3k tokens (0/5 within the 8,192 cap) and DFS is fixed at the first resample point (D_0=1.0 in 4/4); T2 1 anchor in 32 sentences; early-label validity 13/16. (8) Same-seed CRN: ideas do not change with temperature (0/30 in 10/12 cells), so same- vs different-seed idea agreement is identical; phrasing changes less within a seed (e.g. 0.55 vs 0.76). (9) J-lens (community lens) fails its gate vs the logit lens (L27 top-1 0.104 vs 0.291); NLA not available for Qwen3-8B (dated 2026-10-20). Headlines re-derived independently (69 checks, 0 mismatches; float64 sensitivity noted). Kept on the run volume: results/tensors/ (E2 states, attention masses, SAE context codes). Deviations: results/deviations.json; not run: Gumbel-max sensitivity, E6, NLA.
artifacts.title: Reading a coding ban inside Qwen3-8B

hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: Iteration 3 answers what decides the algorithm a prohibition installs and where it acts, how far any knob can push, and whether anything yields a correct novel algorithm, with manifold, SAE and lens readouts.
key_changes: Title and predicted branch flipped to the evidence's lean: a ban removes the default and the model falls to its next rung, forecastable with no ban text; X-specific substitution stays the reportable rival and reclaims the title if it wins.

C1 moved from FRLP variance shares (gate failed in both models; residuals point away from the realised substitutes) to SAMPLED landings scored by the gated PREDICT rule on events where forecast families disagree: ban-free SUBTRACT/LADDER vs ASSOCIATE and PROXIMITY.
New ban-free counterfactual, the SIGNATURE VETO: one-shot and persistent logit masks of the default's distinctive n-gram, with no ban text, to read the next rung in advance under total collapse.

New event generator, EXPOSURE BANS: show a correct program of a non-default algorithm Y and ban Y (named and unnamed), so association and ladder disagree wherever Y's stated alternative is not the default.

Claim 2 rebuilt on the route result: prompt states veto the default's signature before writing; behavioural route fractions are primary; a cross-task link to veto sufficiency; prefill arms; tokens 1-3 states as first extraction; an X-free prohibition direction added at task-spec positions; ban-attending head ablation.

Claim 3 added on reach and novelty: prompts reach one rung (FW 0/100 as sole survivor vs 40/40 forced); a cumulative TOKEN WALK of vetoes (incl. the request's top-five test); an audit of every correct out-of-catalogue program; the request's long-form novelty instruction with thinking on and off.
FRLP demoted to a descriptive mass-level forecast (unscrubbed or name-matched, fp32 path, >=1% mass and ESS>=5); M raised only if Step 0 arithmetic shows a decision is reachable.

Step 0 (CPU) answers every review item: mass-level C1 diagnostics and argmax tables, Qwen bootstrap variance, biased mention aims, the exp9 manifold figures recomputed at g16, Llama correct-only compositions, a declared knob-class rule, positioning rows, an SAE criterion fix and the factual slips.
The 12 frozen bench tasks in two models are the confirmation, with forecasts hash-committed inside the artifact that samples the bans; the two path tasks are screen only and never pooled.

Iteration-2 preregistered predictions recorded with outcomes (direct route >=2/3 FAILED; X-specific DFS gain FAILED; C5 bar MISSED; FRLP gate FAILED; PREDICT NOT RUN); closed bets extended (scrubbed FRLP, geodesic proximity, 10-algorithm catalogue, Jacobian lens, NLA, prime-veto latents).
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: Leads (prompt-route signature veto; one-rung reach; T2 pushes hit the ban's substitute) need decisive sampled events: bench modal and exposure bans, 2 models, vs ban-free forecasts.
hypothesis_update.title: Bans Remove the Default, Not Pick the Next

plans.title: Round-one audit: when is the algorithm chosen?
Do bans pick a substitute or a ladder?
Where an algorithm ban takes effect
Banning five path algorithms at once
Do algorithm bans work the same in Llama?
Coding-task bench with a baseline pilot
Reading a coding ban inside the model

critiques.description: The likelihood-based substitution test (C1) in [ARTIFACT:art_6zBfl3kDjeiP] and its Llama replication cannot settle where a ban sends the mass, and the record does not say so. (i) On the only rows where behaviour is known, the X-specific residual points away from the realised substitute. In results/c1.json (primary_neutral rows), the Dijkstra-ban row has residuals Bellman-Ford/SPFA -1.84, bidirectional Dijkstra -7.92, Floyd-Warshall +3.68 and Dial +6.07. Yet all 272 compliant programs in the five iteration-1 draws, and 255 of 260 non-banned programs in the three protocol-v2 draws, are Bellman-Ford/SPFA. The BFS-ban row's largest residual is IDDFS (+7.99; DFS +0.83), while DFS takes 257 of 257 non-banned programs and IDDFS none. The route experiment repeats the pattern: its full-ban survivor gains on the shortest path task (results/analysis.json#survivor_gains) are Bellman-Ford/SPFA +2.53, the smallest, against bidirectional Dijkstra +30.64, Floyd-Warshall +12.64 and Dial +6.79, and the Bellman-Ford/SPFA cells have median ESS 1.0 to 1.2. The generic ladder profile ranks Dial (6.55) above Bellman-Ford/SPFA (5.87), although every sampled perturbation lands on Bellman-Ford/SPFA. (ii) Log gains count a +18-nat move of an algorithm with negligible implied mass the same as the realised substitute's move, and those tail cells are the least reliable ones (median ESS 1.0 to 1.4, Table 61). 'Not pure subtraction' (F 16 to 22), 'not aimed' and 'no coherent ladder' therefore rest mainly on cells that are behaviourally irrelevant and close to unestimable. (iii) The Llama post hoc check found the bootstrap variance of the mean gain to be 5 to 11 times the replicate variance the frozen correction subtracts. It was never run on Qwen, whose intervals show the same upward skew: pooled V_tot is 1,069.5 inside [924.8, 2,106.7], and V_u is 483.9 inside [356.8, 1,406.8]. If the noise is underestimated by that factor, both F and SHARE are inflated. The ESS-weighted 'share' of 1.24 [0.57, 1.62] is impossible for a proportion and is given without comment. (iv) The Qwen aim under the mention reference (-0.595, p of about 1.0) is omitted from Tables 56, 57 and 78, while the Llama equivalent (-0.28) is reported. Neither is flagged as negative by construction: the mention twin enters both the gain and the prime-and-veto profile, with opposite signs.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a table for every sampled single-ban event in both models: the argmax of the full gain, the argmax of the X-specific residual, and the behavioural landing distribution. Recompute C1 on implied probability mass after renormalisation, or restrict it to survivors with at least 1% implied mass and ESS of at least 5, weighting rows by mass, and report whether the branch changes. Run the Llama bootstrap-versus-replicate variance diagnostic on the Qwen screen and report basic intervals for V_u, V_s and SHARE. Report both models' mention-reference aims with their built-in negative bias. Until these checks pass, rewrite 'not pure subtraction', 'not aimed' and 'no coherent ladder' in Sections 2.11 and 2.12 and the closing summary as 'not detectable with the current instrument'. Expected impact: +0.5 to +1. This decides whether the title claim can be tested with FRLP on the bench at all.

critiques.description: The record holds two verdicts on the rival account and never reconciles them. Section 2.11 item 2 and the closing summary say the generic-perturbation rival holds on the shortest path task. Every nonsemantic perturbation with at least 10 correct programs other than Dijkstra (8 of 8 rows, random directions included; Table 45) landed mostly on Bellman-Ford/SPFA, so 'a ban behaves like an arbitrary push'. In Llama, the empirical sampled ladder is the best per-sample predictor of the mechanism written (top-1 0.70 against 0.59 for FRLP, paired p < 1e-4; Table 72). Yet the same section lists 'A coherent latent ladder' under 'Ruled out, or not supported'. That verdict rests on mean cosines among FRLP generic-perturbation profiles (0.34 and -0.02 for Qwen, 0.14 for Llama), computed mostly over survivors with ESS near 1, from an instrument that failed its own gate in both models. The closing summary states both in consecutive sentences ('lands on the same second choice as the ban' and 'the generic perturbations do not form a coherent ladder either'). The behavioural evidence supports at least a shared top rung on the shortest path task. The likelihood evidence cannot resolve the order below it.
critiques.suggested_action: Add one reconciling paragraph to Section 2.11. Behaviour shows a shared top rung (Bellman-Ford/SPFA on the shortest path task; DFS only under bans on the grid task). The order below the top rung is unmeasured, because it is behaviourally unobservable and FRLP is unreliable there. Move 'a coherent latent ladder' out of 'ruled out' or qualify it as 'not detected by an uncalibrated instrument'. Plan a behavioural discriminating test: sampled landings under matched-norm random edits at the ban's own displacement, plus second-step bans after a random edit, on bench tasks (using Llama where present-minor events exist) where the runner-up and the associate differ. Expected impact: +0.25 to +0.5.

critiques.description: An executed output that answers the user's literal request is missing, and the report says it does not exist. The ban-list artifact [ARTIFACT:art_IVZc3TWCeE9f] drew 14 activation-space manifold figures (figures/fig_manifold_t1_{baseline, single_bfs, multi_TOP, multi_ARC, multi_SCATTER, multi_TOP5} and fig_manifold_t2_{baseline, single_dijkstra, los_*}, plus fig_kstab_*; results/manifold.json). Each is an Isomap of teacher-forced states at layer 24, position 'pre', k = 10, with centroids sized and coloured by implemented count, banned centroids crossed out and natural programs overlaid. That is the request's 'manifold, colour each centroid by implemented count, then prohibit the top 5'. Section 2.12 nonetheless lists 'the activation space manifold plots with centroids coloured by implemented count' as still open, and Section 2.6 carries only [FIGURE:fig_multiban] beside the landing and disguise tables. The geometry claims of Section 2.6 also rest on the 'pre' position, which the same artifact calls a label-dependent position artefact for probes. At that position the BFS and bidirectional BFS centroids coincide (centroid distance 0.0147; Isomap coordinates (-100.99, -118.52) and (-100.92, -118.52)), so 'BFS with bidirectional BFS' as nearest neighbours may be a position effect. results/persistence.json labels its own null 'weakly powered', yet the report says it 'answers the request's question about a circle in the negative'.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the exp9 manifold figures to Section 2.6 with a table of implemented counts per centroid for each condition (baseline, single ban, TOP, ARC, SCATTER, TOP5, and the shortest path bans that leave one survivor). State plainly that the counts stay on the banned BFS and DFS centroids under TOP5. Recompute nearest neighbours and persistence at a position that does not depend on the label (the g16 sweep already in manifold.json) and report whether the order holds. Rephrase the circle result as 'no evidence of a loop at weak power, at a label-dependent position'. Correct Section 2.12 to say the plots exist, but not at a validated locus. Expected impact: +0.5 on coverage and contribution.

critiques.description: The cross-model contrast rests on failing programs. In [ARTIFACT:art_-QPYRaFERCBX] data/labelled.jsonl, Llama's grid baseline is BFS 77, DFS 20 and other 3 among attempted programs, but its 20 correct programs are BFS 20 of 20. All 20 DFS attempts fail, so the correctness-conditioned Hill number that the run used throughout iteration 1 is 1.0: collapsed. Under the BFS ban Llama's correct programs are DFS 7, BFS 4 and other 1 (8 compliant), and under the Dijkstra ban Dijkstra 20, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 4 and other 1. The bench pilot's Llama 'diversity' is also largely failed attempts. On kth smallest the attempted programs are heapify-and-pop 16, size-k heap 11 and full sort 7, but the 10 correct ones are full sort 6, heapify 2, quickselect 1 and size-k 1, so the correct mode equals Qwen's mode. Section 2.7's heading ('Llama's baseline is not collapsed on the grid task') and the closing summary ('Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is not collapsed on the grid task ... so the collapse is a property of the model as well as the task') report attempts only. For a request about creative solutions that work, that distinction is the result.
critiques.suggested_action: Add correct-program compositions beside the attempted ones in Tables 70 and 73. Restate the cross-model claim: 'Llama attempts more algorithms, but its correct grid output is as collapsed as Qwen's (BFS 20 of 20). On the bench, correct-only diversity appears on substring search (naive 18, KMP 5, Rabin-Karp 1), connected components (union-find 30, DFS 5), cycle detection and top-k at small N.' Compute Hill_cc for every Llama event so it is comparable to the Qwen tables. Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description: Where samples were the binding constraint, the iteration again added variants and readouts instead of samples, and the PREDICT contest of the four frozen families was never run on any new event. FRLP precision is limited by the number of proposal programs. The screen fixed M = 20 programs per algorithm at the GPU deadline (bidirectional Dijkstra 11; 211 programs in all), leaving median ESS of 1.0 to 1.4 outside the forced cells (Table 61) and 98% of gate cells below 5. Instead of raising M, the run added 12 sensitivity variants over the same 211 programs (Table 59) and a Llama replication with the same problem (median ESS 2.5). The route, ban-list and readout experiments spent three more draws on the same two modal-ban events. The bench was frozen, but no ban event was run on it, so the event count behind the title claim is still 11 single-ban rows in Qwen and 6 in Llama, on two tasks. The four families frozen in Section 2.1 (ladder, association, prime and veto, proximity) were never scored together under the preregistered rule (0.10 nats on at least 3 disagreeing gated events). Table 72 is per-sample top-1 accuracy, not that rule, and the ban-list landing forecasts were degenerate. The iteration's PREDICT outcome is not stated anywhere.
critiques.suggested_action: State the iteration-2 PREDICT outcome explicitly: either a gated log-score table for the four frozen families on every iteration-2 event (Llama's 14 events include present-minor bans), or 'not run'. Add to Section 2.12 the arithmetic for the next budget: the M needed for median ESS of at least 5, given the observed weight dispersion per algorithm, and the number of bench ban events needed to separate SHARE from 0.5. Commit the budget to M and to bench ban events, not further variants. Expected impact: +0.5 on the contribution of the next record.

critiques.description: The iteration-2 positive claims are not set against their nearest published neighbours. Table 52 positions only iteration-1 claims. (a) The claim that the read position knows how hard a wording will be obeyed (C5, rho -0.41) neighbours Heo et al. 2024, 'Do LLMs "know" internally when they follow instructions?' (arXiv 2410.14516). That paper finds a pre-generation dimension in input-embedding space that predicts instruction-following success, is driven by prompt phrasing, and raises success when intervened along. This run adds a wording-level correlation for prohibitions in code, but its own route test finds the read position alone causally inert (F_R of about 0), a contrast with Heo's intervention that should be recorded. (b) The SAE dead end neighbours Kissane et al. 2024, 'SAEs (usually) transfer between base and chat models' (Alignment Forum; Mistral-7B and Qwen1.5-0.5B transfer, Gemma v1 2B does not). Here the fraction of variance unexplained is lower on instruct than on base at layers 20 and 27 (0.094 vs 0.243; 0.153 vs 0.325; results/transfer_summary.json). The failure comes from the CE-increase ratio, with the instruct model's clean CE nine times lower (0.030 vs 0.260), so the dead end may be an artefact of the criterion. The remedy Section 2.12 proposes, fine-tuning the base SAE on instruct activations, is Kissane et al.'s, and they are not cited. (c) The prompt-route, knockout and priming results neighbour Rana 2026 [7] (activation patching of negative constraints; naming primes the forbidden item) and Mann et al. [53]. Both are cited inline, without a line on what this run adds. (d) Ban lists failing by reimplementation and disguise neighbour denial prompting [23].
critiques.suggested_action: Extend Table 52 with one row per iteration-2 positive claim: compliance predictable at the read position (Heo et al. 2024), the opening-line veto and prompt route (Rana 2026; Geva et al. 2023 for the knockout method), priming by naming (Rana 2026; Mann et al.), ban-list reimplementation (Lu et al.), and SAE transfer (Kissane et al. 2024). For each, give the neighbour's finding, then what this run adds or 'replication'. Rerun or rephrase the SAE transfer verdict with a criterion that does not penalise the instruct model's lower clean CE (for example, the fraction of CE loss recovered against a zero-ablation baseline, computed per model on its own outputs). Expected impact: +0.25 to +0.5.

critiques.description: The headline route claim is stated more strongly in the summary than its evidence allows. 'In Qwen3-8B the prompt route carries 0.85 of the banned algorithm's likelihood drop and the direct route none, and Llama agrees (0.84)' rests on the preregistered FRLP readout. Section 2.5 itself says that readout is degenerate on the grid task (ESS 1 to 3 of 30; exp(D) 3e-7 against a behavioural ratio of 0.14) and measures the opening-line veto. Two other readouts in the same artifact show a direct route. The natural-proposal readout gives F_direct 0.16 [0.11, 0.21], an interval that excludes 0, with superadditive routes. Grid behaviour gives direct 0.35 [0.25, 0.45], and the full knockout restores BFS to 0.47, which I recomputed from data/samples.jsonl (condition K0): about 38% of the grid ban's behavioural effect needs generated tokens to read the ban. The Llama number is FRLP-only, on an instrument that failed its gate there (median ESS 2.5). C5 ('the read position carries part of how strongly a wording will be obeyed') sits next to F_R of about 0, so that site is decodable but carries none of the ban's effect causally. This is the decodability-versus-actionability gap the field now tests for routinely.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite item 3 of Section 2.11 and the summary per task and per readout. Shortest path: the prompt route carries the ban in likelihood (0.82) and in behaviour (0.98). Grid: the likelihood readout is dominated by the opening fork (0.87), behaviour is mixed (prompt 0.50, direct 0.35), and the natural readout puts the direct route at 0.16. Llama: likelihood only. Remove 'none'. Add 'splicing the read position alone carries none of the effect (F_R of about 0)' to every C5 statement, and list a causal test of the shared ban direction (add or subtract it at the task-specification positions and measure compliance) as next work. Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description: The core request ('can we make llms give truly creative and novel solutions?') is answered only inside a fixed catalogue, and the run never looks at the one place a novel solution could appear. Across the per-sample files of exp1, exp4, exp5 and exp6 (iteration 1), and exp8, exp9, exp10 and exp12 (iteration 2), about 22,000 programs, I count roughly 25 correct programs labelled 'other', i.e. outside the catalogue: exp9 13 (mostly forced conditions), iteration-1 decommitment steering 6, Llama 5 and association 1. None came from the creativity, new-algorithm or novelty instructions, whose correct programs are all catalogue algorithms (for example novelty, grid: BFS 81, unit-weight Dijkstra 2, DFS 1, A* 1). The 'other' programs are never inspected. Under the TOP ban, the 13 'not banned' programs that make its avoidance 0.13 are 12 failing programs labelled 'other' that are visibly DFS or BFS reimplementations ('def dfs(r, c)', '# Use a queue to perform BFS (but we av...') plus 1 unit-weight Dijkstra. The request's long-form instruction ('Make a fully novel algorithm never seen before ... 2000 words ...') was run only as the one-line 'Make a fully novel algorithm never seen before.' (exp6 prompts.json), and never with thinking on. The same-seed arm with thinking on and an SAE readout that passes transfer remain open, as the report says.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a table of every correct out-of-catalogue program by condition and model, with a blind judge or manual characterisation (novel algorithm, variant of a catalogue algorithm, or labeller miss). State the result as the run's direct answer to the novelty question: across about 22,000 programs, no instruction produced a correct non-catalogue algorithm, if that holds. Run the request's long-form novelty prompt, with thinking on and off, as one cheap condition on both tasks. Report the 'other' share separately from avoidance in the ban-list tables. Expected impact: +0.25 to +0.5 on coverage.

critiques.description: The answer to the user's 'can we influence it?' is paraphrased past its metric. The summary says 'Under one statistic, no ban and no diversity knob buys a second correct algorithm for less than 20 points of pass rate on either task.' The operational target is rarefied Hill-1 of at least 2, which a 2:1 split can never reach. The semantic seed's correct output on the shortest path task is Bellman-Ford/SPFA 61, Dijkstra 30 and Floyd-Warshall 1 at 7 pass points (Table 47). It moves the mode and plainly buys a second correct algorithm, and its Hill-1 interval [1.534, 2.076] includes 2 (I recomputed 1.934 by rarefaction). The BUY-rule outcome also depends on an unregistered class rule. The A* mention on the grid task (Hill-1 2.69 at 11 points, 88% of the reference pass rate) beats the next row by more than the 0.5 margin, but is excluded as a 'named mode cue', while sham bans, which are also controls, are ranked as knobs (Table 47, IDDFS sham 1.205).
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite the verdict in Sections 2.3.6 and 2.11 and the summary as: 'No knob reaches an even two-algorithm split (Hill-1 of at least 2) under 20 points. The semantic seed (Bellman-Ford/SPFA 61, Dijkstra 30 at 7 points; interval includes 2) and the A* mention (2.69 at 11 points) are the two conditions that buy a second correct algorithm, and both name or describe it.' Declare the knob-class rule (which controls count as knobs) and apply it consistently to mention twins and sham bans. Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description: The strategy's two positive targets failed, and the record never says so in those terms. The strategy predicted (1) an X-specific gain for DFS under the BFS ban that the ladder cannot match, but Table 58's largest residual for that row is IDDFS and DFS's residual is +0.83; and (2) that the direct generation-time route would carry at least two thirds of the ban's effect, but F_direct is 0.00 in likelihood, 0.35 in grid behaviour and 0.05 in shortest path behaviour. Section 2.5 says the update 'predicted ... a direct route', but Section 2.11 lists no failed predictions. Separately, the readout experiment ran about 11 hours after the audit had named generated tokens 1 to 3 as the extraction target (results/locus.json written 02:40 UTC; readout results/e2_meta.json 13:31 UTC), yet saved only R, k16, k_pre, k_post and meangen (results/tensors/e2_states.npz pos_keys). The record does not say why: presumably the plan was frozen before the audit.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a 'preregistered predictions and outcomes' list to Section 2.11 with both positive targets marked failed and their numbers. Add one line to Section 2.9 or 2.12 explaining why tokens 1 to 3 were not saved in this iteration, so the next strategy treats them as the first extraction.

critiques.description: The confirmation bench inherits an instrument that is not commensurable with the screen. The bench's frozen baseline likelihoods [ARTIFACT:art_0ndRfWKBWclR] come from FP8 weights through vLLM prompt log-probabilities, and batched and single-request scoring disagreed by 0.62 nats on 1 of 5 checked programs. The screen had to move to fp32 activations because bf16 moved per-program log-likelihoods by up to 2.1 nats, comparable to the between-survivor SDs being measured (1.5 to 7.8 nats, Table 58). The recommendation to score unscrubbed programs is validated only on baseline, mention and listing events. On ban rows, the algorithm names left in identifiers and comments interact with the ban's own naming, which is the mechanism scrubbing was introduced to remove.
critiques.suggested_action: Before forecasts are committed, rescore the bench baselines on the screen's fp32-activation path, and validate the unscrubbed variant, or a name-matched one (names replaced by neutral identifiers of equal token length), on the iteration-1 ban rows against their sampled landings. Record both checks in the bench section.

critiques.description: Several small factual slips. (1) Table 66 labels the bidirectional Dijkstra and Dial rows 'plain', but the 14 of 40 and 36 of 40 counts come from the descriptive prompts. In exp9 data/samples.jsonl, forced:bidijkstra has 10 samples (Dijkstra 9) and forced_desc:bidijkstra 40; forced:dial has 10 and forced_desc:dial 40. (2) Section 2.11 item 2 says no nonsemantic perturbation left BFS among correct programs on the grid task, but Table 46's T = 1.3, top-k = 10 row has DFS 1. (3) Item 6 says the model 'can write ... Dial when told to', but forced Dial passes 7 of 40 (0.175). (4) TOP's avoidance of 0.13 is labeller residue: 12 failing BFS/DFS variants labelled 'other' plus 1 unit-weight Dijkstra. (5) The clause added to item 6 of Section 1.12 ('which is consistent with geodesic proximity and with typicality ... not separated on these events') is not marked as an insertion; its correction note covers only the layer-24 instability.
critiques.suggested_action: Correct the five items in place, with iteration-3 markers where they touch earlier sections.

dimension_scores.justification: The previous internal contradictions are resolved and the behavioural numbers reproduce from raw rows. But the iteration's central instrument failed its preregistered validity gate in both models. The C1 decomposition built on it is dominated by negligible-mass survivors with ESS near 1, and its residuals disagree with the observed landing on both modal-ban rows. Four summary claims outrun the evidence beside them (direct route 'none', Llama 'not collapsed', 'no second correct algorithm', ladder 'ruled out').

A researcher not on the run can follow the record in order. Each iteration-2 section opens with why it ran, the protocol is defined once (Section 2.2), and tables are introduced by what they settle and name their source. Weaknesses: summary paraphrases sometimes drift from the defined metrics (Hill of at least 2 becomes 'buys a second correct algorithm'), a few rows are mislabelled (Table 66), and one inserted clause in the iteration-1 section is not marked.

Nearly every executed output of the seven iteration-2 artifacts is written up with its tables, and dead ends are kept with evidence. Missing: the ban-list artifact's 14 manifold figures, coloured by implemented count (the user's requested plot), which the report says do not exist; the Qwen mention-reference aim (-0.595); correct-only compositions for Llama; an explicit record that both of the strategy's positive targets failed; and any look at the roughly 25 correct out-of-catalogue programs.

review.overall_assessment:
This record is much sounder than the iteration-1 version. All eleven must-fix items of the previous review were addressed. The iteration-1 section was changed only through corrections marked in place: I diffed it against the iteration-1 draft, and the only unmarked change is one inserted clause in item 6 of Section 1.12. Every iteration-2 artifact is written up with full tables and named source files. I recomputed the behavioural headlines from the raw per-sample rows and they match exactly: route arms a/b/c/d/K0/K1/K2 (banned share 0.14/1.00/0.57/0.70/0.47/0.16/0.19 on the grid task, 0.11/0.99/0.13/0.95/0.06/0.11/0.11 on the shortest path task), per-template counts (0,0,0,14,0), import first lines (Table 64), the ban lists (TOP BFS 59, DFS 26; ARC 63/37; SCATTER 69/27; TOP5 63/36), the post hoc chi-square p of 0.48, the leave-one-survivor 'will' shares (0.95/0.51/0/0/0), the 14 Llama events, the 13-task Qwen pilot (all collapsed), the route fractions from the per-arm drops (0.87, 0.82, pooled 0.85) and rarefied Hill-1 for nine knob rows (within Monte Carlo error). The locus numbers in results/locus.json and the C1 shares in results/c1.json match the report. I did not recompute the importance-sampling cells or the geometry subsampling from raw scores; those numbers are traceable to result files, but I have not independently verified them.

What the record now supports. On two path-search tasks Qwen3-8B is collapsed (BFS, Dijkstra). Temperature, sampler, thinking mode and coupled seeds change phrasing, not the algorithm. A single ban is obeyed at a rate set by its wording: with five frozen templates, three draws on different engines gave 0.14/0.14/0.15 and 0.11/0.16/0.13, and one template caused every grid failure. An obeyed ban recollapses onto one substitute. Four- and five-name bans fail by reimplementing BFS and DFS. On the shortest path task, generic perturbations land on the same substitute as the ban. KV-cache patching shows the shortest path ban carried by the prompt states, via a veto on the default program's opening import line. These are careful, replicated, mostly behavioural findings.

What it does not yet support. The title claim, substitution against a latent ladder, is undetermined in both models, and the instrument behind it (the forced-ratio latent probability, FRLP) failed its preregistered gate in both. Its X-specific residuals point away from the realised substitute on the only rows where behaviour is known: on the Dijkstra-ban row, Bellman-Ford/SPFA has residual -1.84 while 272 of 272 compliant programs are Bellman-Ford/SPFA. The decomposition is dominated by survivors with negligible mass and ESS near 1. Several summary sentences outrun their evidence: 'the direct route none' ignores the natural-proposal readout (0.16 [0.11, 0.21]) and the grid behaviour (0.35); 'Llama is not collapsed on the grid task' ignores that all 20 correct Llama baseline programs are BFS; 'no knob buys a second correct algorithm' ignores that the semantic seed's correct output is Bellman-Ford/SPFA 61 and Dijkstra 30 at 7 pass points; and 'a coherent latent ladder' is listed as ruled out while the behavioural evidence supports a shared top rung. The record also omits executed outputs that answer the request directly. The ban-list artifact drew 14 activation-space manifold figures with centroids coloured by implemented count under the top-five ban, which is exactly the user's requested plot, and the report calls that item still open. The roughly 25 correct out-of-catalogue programs, the only candidates for 'truly novel' output, were never inspected. No contradiction of the kind that blocked the last record remains, so soundness is 2, not 1. The record is not blocking. Its score is held at 4 by the undetermined central claim, the failed instrument, two tasks and the overstatements listed below. Fixing critiques 1, 2, 3 and 7 would make the record a sound basis for the bench confirmation.
strengths: Every blocking and must-fix item of the previous review was repaired. Corrections in the iteration-1 section are marked in place with what changed and why. The five-draw substitute claim now carries per-draw counts (Table 43), the cumulative ban gets its three draws (Table 44), the selection rule is quoted in full and applied to gated events (Table 48), the knob table uses one statistic (Table 47), and the locus probe's cause is recorded with timestamps and the probe re-run.

Traceability is strong. Iteration-2 tables name their source files (results/c1.json, results/analysis.json#behaviour, tables/knob_table.csv, ...), every artifact carries an [ARTIFACT:id] marker, and the raw-row recomputations I ran reproduced the reported counts exactly.

The route experiment is a real causal test. Token-length-matched neutral twins allow position-by-position KV splicing, attention knockouts include a generic-damage control, and sampling uses common random numbers. The opening-line veto is concretely supported: 0 of 100 import first lines under the ban and the prompt route, against 99 of 100 under the neutral twin. The record also says where behaviour qualifies the likelihood readout on the grid task.

Fixed-wording replication across three engines (0.14/0.14/0.15 and 0.11/0.16/0.13), with every grid failure traced to one template, converts iteration 1's unexplained compliance spread into a measured wording effect. It is the cleanest behavioural result in the run.

Dead ends are kept with their numbers: the FRLP gate failure and its scrubbing diagnosis, the failed catalogue extension (5 of 10 kept), the SAE transfer test (ratios 3.29/1.95/1.59), the Jacobian-lens gate (0.104 vs 0.291), the unavailable NLA, and a presence pilot showing Qwen collapsed on all 13 bench tasks.
Bookkeeping is thorough: GPU hours from phase logs, OpenRouter spend per artifact, deviations, labeller rechecks, and independent rederivations with placebos.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration the pool holds: (1) a repaired record with per-draw substitute counts, a single-statistic knob table, gated PREDICT scores, the cross-experiment perturbation table that states the generic-perturbation rival per task, geodesic k x layer robustness, and the locus verdict from the saved states (artifact 1); (2) the FRLP validity gate and the full single-ban gain matrices on both path-search tasks for Qwen3-8B (artifact 2) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (artifact 5), each with the C1 share, the aim correlations and the branch under both references, so the title claim is either supported (X-specific share above one half), replaced by the ladder, or reported as pure subtraction, per model; (3) the route fractions F_direct and F_prompt with the temporal and layer-band knockouts, the veto layer, and C5 over about 110 wordings (artifact 3); (4) the top-five, ARC-5, SCATTER-5 and leave-one-survivor landings with manifold plots in activation coordinates (artifact 4); (5) a frozen confirmation bench of 6-12 gated tasks with pilot data, stated alternatives and forced programs, and no ban prompt run on it (artifact 6); (6) SAE, thought-anchor, same-seed and NLA/j-lens readouts (artifact 7). NEXT ITERATION: hash-commit every family's forecast on the bench, then run the confirmation (FRLP matrices and C1 on both models, sampled single, present-minor and two-step bans for the behavioural contest C3, the route test on modal bans with avoidance >= 0.5) under the frozen templates and code; the screen tasks are never pooled into confirmation statistics. If FRLP fails its gate, C1 falls back to sampled events and the bench's present-minor bans carry the contest.
strategies.objective: Decide, with instruments that work under a fully collapsed baseline, what a 'do not use X' instruction does to an instruction-tuned code model's algorithm choice and where it acts: (C1) whether ban-induced gains of the surviving algorithms are X-specific (substitution, aimed by X's prime-and-veto neighbourhood or its stated replacement) or a fixed latent ladder that any perturbation reveals, measured with forced-ratio latent probabilities on every single, sham and multi-ban; (C2) whether the ban travels by the direct generation-time route or through the prompt states, by cache patching and attention knockout; (C4) where the mass lands when the top five are banned at once; replicated on a second model family, with a presence-piloted confirmation bench frozen for the next iteration and the iteration-1 record repaired.
strategies.rationale: WHY DEEPEN, AND WHAT THE OBJECT IS. Iteration 1's live result is behavioural: when Qwen3-8B obeys a ban it re-collapses on one substitute (shortest path: Bellman-Ford/SPFA in 5/5 draws, 272/272 compliant; grid: DFS the realised mode in 4/5 draws, 116/128 pooled), and that substitute was predictable before the ban. But every ban event so far had the associate equal to the runner-up, and on the shortest-path task every perturbation, random directions included, landed on the same runner-up. So the object of this iteration is fixed: does a ban SUBSTITUTE (promote X-specific survivors beyond renormalisation) or only SUBTRACT and expose a fixed latent ladder, and does the ban act through the prompt states or directly at generation time? Every slot attacks that object from a different side. THE SIDEWAYS MOVE (aiming at a positive result). The read-position geometry is closed (share test null, ablation moved 0/50, decoder equal to random). The strategy moves to the two places the iteration-1 evidence points to: (i) the model's own output likelihoods, read by forward passes (FRLP), which are not degenerate under a collapsed baseline and turn every single ban, sham ban and multi-ban into a measured event (about 55 C1 rows per model on the two tasks alone, against 2 sampled events before); and (ii) generation time, where the evidence already leans: under a ban only 4-8 of 10 paths are decided at R against 10/10 at baseline, and the confirmed forking tokens sit at the import token and at algorithm names. Two positive targets are therefore realistic. On the grid task only bans produced DFS (29-90 per 100) while random directions, novelty and temperature produced it at most 1-2 times, which predicts an X-specific gain for DFS under ban-BFS that the ladder cannot match; and the route test predicts that the direct generation-time route carries at least two thirds of the ban's effect. If instead the ladder wins, the paper leads with 'bans subtract and expose a fixed ladder readable before any ban', which is equally publishable and is measured, not inferred. HOW THE SEVEN SLOTS MAP. FIX and CLEANER MEASURE: artifact 1 repairs the record (every blocking and major reviewer item) and runs the CPU-only diagnostics, including the locus probe that failed only because it ran before its inputs were written (probes.json written 18:29, states saved 18:34). CONFOUND: artifact 2 tests the generic-perturbation rival head-on with the FRLP gain matrices against an external ladder built from matched-norm random edits, a nonce ban and the novelty instruction. MECHANISM: artifact 3 is the 2 x 2 cache-patching route test with temporal and layer-band knockouts and the logit/tuned-lens veto layer, plus C5 (R encodes how strongly, not what). BOUNDARY: artifact 4 is the request's literal top-five prohibition with ARC-5 and SCATTER-5 controls and leave-one-survivor bans, where the ladder runs out. REPLICATION (second family): artifact 5 runs the frozen protocol on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. MORE POWER (events, not predictors): artifact 6 builds the confirmation bench behind a cheap presence pilot, with no ban prompt run on it. MECHANISM at the model's own units: artifact 7 reads the veto with SAEs, thought anchors and a same-seed common-random-number test, and resolves 'NLA' and 'j-lens'. REVIEWER MUST-FIX MAP. Contradictions 1-2, the misapplied selection rule, the seeds half-report, the geometry overreach, the locus cause, the missing outputs, the base-model caveats, the review objections (sham bans as weak negation-promotion, self-simulation) and the nearest-neighbour positioning: artifact 1. 'Events, not predictors': the predictor set is frozen at four families (ladder, association, prime-and-veto, proximity), wording at five templates, and the budget goes to events (artifacts 2, 5, 6). The generic-perturbation rival: artifacts 1 (cross-experiment table), 2 and 5 (ladder profile). Request coverage: top-five (artifact 4), natural BFS versus DFS internals (artifacts 1 and 4), logit and tuned lens (artifact 3), SAE, thought anchors, same seed, NLA and j-lens (artifact 7). PRE-REGISTRATION DISCIPLINE. The five templates, neutral-noun rule, FRLP definition, C1 code and decision branches are frozen in the shared protocol that every artifact quotes; nothing is retuned after data arrive. The screen tasks are never pooled into confirmation statistics, and the bench sees no ban prompt this iteration. Budget: about 16 A4500 GPU-hours across artifacts 2-7, OpenRouter at most about USD 4 in total.

artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_13
artifacts.summary: Iteration-3 confirmation experiment on Qwen3-8B (bf16, rev b968826d, thinking off) over the 12 frozen bench tasks of exp11 (art_0ndRfWKBWclR). Ban-free forecasts of where each task's modal 'do not use X' ban lands were built and hash-sealed (commitments.log, SEAL_BEFORE_BANS) before any ban sample: SUBTRACT (token vetoes of the default's distinctive n-gram, coupled to neutral-twin samples by exact rejection + masked redraw via vLLM logit_bias; one-shot, persistent, 3 iterated rounds), LADDER (nonce ban, novelty instruction, 3 matched-norm isotropic random directions patched into task-spec states at layers 12-23), ASSOCIATE (exp11 association answers) and PROXIMITY (AST Zhang-Shasha distance). Then 1,200 ban samples (5 templates x 20 per task) were labelled by the gated exp11 labellers (re-check matched gate.json on 12/12). RESULTS: only 5/12 bans pass the gate (T03, T06, T05, T10, T13; R1, R3, R6, T11 keep the default almost always). The frozen C1 rule returns 'SUBTRACTION/LADDER (LADDER)' (wins LADDER 3, PROXIMITY 2), but 2 of LADDER's wins come from an undefined forecast scored as uniform; counting defined forecasts only, no family advances, and no family beats the uniform reference on average (mean log score minus uniform over gated events: LADDER +0.06, SUBTRACT -0.69, PROXIMITY -1.53, ASSOCIATE -1.78). Landings are X-specific but largely unforeseen (T06 -> index_marking, T10 -> bfs, T13 -> 'other'; only T03 quickselect and T05 brute_force were hit by a top-1). C2b is UNDETERMINED: one-shot vetoes never reach 0.5 avoidance on a gated task; descriptively the last iterated veto round lands elsewhere on T06 and T10. Token vetoes move the surface, not the algorithm: the default re-emerges in every veto round on 9/12 tasks, with text-level leaks of the vetoed n-gram in 23% (one-shot) to 54% (round 2) of samples; a sham veto breaks programs without moving the algorithm. Band-patching the ban's own task-spec states into the twin reproduces avoidance only on T03 and T10. Wording matters: template LR 374 (df 4, p ~ 1e-79; shuffled placebo p 0.39), W4 'X is not allowed here.' fails on 10/12 tasks. FRLP fp32 rescoring: median |dL_corr| 0.88 nats vs FP8, argmax unchanged 12/12. It is within the random range on 5/6 tasks; on T03 it beats random but lands on a size-k heap, not the ban's quickselect. Projecting it out of the ban never restores the default (pooled delta -0.026, CI [-0.07, 0.03]). With 15 random directions (exploratory), v is at the 80th percentile on T2. C2e: no within-ban locus on any testable task (batch-1 teacher-forced states, blocks 8-28, tokens 1-8/16, 500 within-template permutations, text controls). The class is set by the template (W4 keeps the default 20/20 on bench, all 61 T1 BFS) or by tokens after 16 (T2 fork median ~29 tokens). States of identical prefixes are bit-identical. FP8 caveat: 20-row teacher-forcing batches add 4-10% row-position noise, so states were re-extracted at batch 1; the batch-20 sensitivity run gives the same verdict. C2f NOT SUPPORTED: mean-ablating L21H17/L26H21/L26H25 gives T1 delta +0.06 over layer-matched random heads (any head ablation breaks the fragile W4 ban); T2 unchanged. 0g: Qwen-Scope base SAEs pass the frozen FR_zero rule (instruct 0.989-0.994 vs base 0.991-0.993, own text, 2x2 model x text). The rule also passes on placebo input, so it is lenient. The SAEs keep only cos ~0.3 of the ban-minus-twin displacement; 5a latents never beat DiM (1/63 trivial cells). Outputs: results/*.json, figures fig1-fig9, method_out.json (datasets c2d_arms, c2f_heads, c2e_locus, sae_transfer; one CRN slot per example with predict_<arm>=label|pass), directions/ (v per task, random dirs), states/ (fp16, kept on the run volume), and an audit with independent re-derivation and placebo tests.

The veto is exact (0 banned-sequence occurrences in 1,450 vetoed generations) but the walk STALLED on all 6 tasks: at step 1 on T1, T2, T03, T04, T10 and at step 2 on T06 (rung 2 = sort+adjacent). The default returned by renaming (current_row/current_col; current_distinct), non-canonical spellings ((parent, parents, \tparent; leak up to 0.86) or near-miss syntax (T1 66-86% invalid). A matched SHAM veto kept the default (T1 50/50, T2 50/50, T04 49/50, T10 44/44 valid) while the distinctive veto cut T2 pass from 50/50 to 19/46 (Fisher p~8e-12). hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: Iteration 4 answers whether temperature is the creativity knob and whether creativity can be influenced: same-seed temperature versus plan noise on ideas and phrasings, where the choice lives (plan subspace, geometry plots), the top-five prohibition at the plan, and the novelty boundary.
key_changes: Title and object re-framed (embedding): from where a ban sends the mass to plan noise as the knob that moves ideas; a ban becomes one large plan-site displacement plus generated tokens reading it (Claim 3b).

New primary C1: per-sample random displacement of the task-specification states at layers 12-23 (plan noise) against every token- and prompt-level knob on H5 (best correct-only Hill-1 within 5 pass points), with matched-norm site controls and a plain-prompt control.
The request's 1a-c is asked as a same-seed 2x2 (temperature x plan-noise draw, token seed coupled), with the twice-dropped thinking-on same-seed arm made non-droppable.

New primary C2a: a ban-free plan subspace (forced and name-masked prompts at the task-specification states) must predict which random directions diversify; targeted default-to-runner-up pushes and cross-knob projections are secondary; geometry plots move to this causal site.

New primary C3a: movability predicts ban compliance. Screen rule frozen from iteration 3 (all 6 push-movable tasks obey the ban; none of 8 ban-failing tasks was moved); confirmed in a never-run family (gemma-2-9b-it, fallback Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct) with predictions committed before its bans.

C3b replaces signature vetoes with ban-free forecasts defined on every event (push-landing, opening ladder) and carries the route-landing lead: on connected components each route alone lands DFS like random pushes, both together land BFS.
C3c and C3d: a norm sweep (alpha up to 8) with a full novelty audit, and the request's top-five prohibition asked as an activation push at the plan, scored edge versus opposite side.

Old title claim recorded as not confirmed in its forecastable-next-rung form (no family beats uniform on Qwen modal bans; vetoes undefined on 10/12 and 29/33 events); snap-back kept as descriptive with its wording caveat.

Closed: signature vetoes and the token walk, the shared prohibition direction, head ablation, the tokens 1-16 locus, base SAEs as ban readouts, the counting rule, exposure bans and long-form novelty instructions.

Step 0 answers every reviewer must-fix item: full knob table with all 15 random directions and the alpha-2 rows; landing by route; the Llama hit rule with hits recomputed excluding 'other'; the 'other' audit with catalogue-only avoidance; figure markers for existing Isomaps; Table 92b.
Step 0 also fixes the minor items: defined-only hit rates; Table 82 per distinct likelihood row; Section 3.10 wording.

Screen and confirmation are explicit: iteration-3 push data are the screen, frozen in (0i). Confirmation uses fresh per-sample noise, R2 as a held-out task, new directions and a never-run family; Llama is demoted to a second screen body because its bans were already seen.

critiques.description:
The record's answer to the request's 'can we influence it?' contradicts its own evidence. The closing section says: 'No knob opens the repertoire cheaply. No knob reaches an even two-algorithm split under 20 points of pass rate; the semantic seed ... and the A* mention are the two conditions that buy a second correct algorithm, and both name or describe it.' Section 3.2.5 and the iteration-3 correction in 2.3.6 say the same.
(a) Table 91 contradicts this. The decommitment direction at c = 0.25 (Bellman-Ford/SPFA 54, Dijkstra 23; Hill-1 1.913 [1.705, 2.088] at 17 points) and random direction 1 (Dijkstra 53, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 26; 1.858 at 16 points) also buy a second correct algorithm, and neither names or describes one. The decommitment interval includes 2, the criterion the record uses to single out the semantic seed.
(b) No iteration-3 arm was entered into the knob table, although the class rule of Section 3.2.5 counts activation interventions as knobs. I recomputed rarefied Hill-1 (depth 25, correct programs) from [ARTIFACT:art_pVlCZ272hDV7] data/labels.jsonl; see verify_iter3.log.
- Kth smallest: random direction 9002 at alpha 1 gives quickselect 16, full sort 15, size-k heap 19 at pass 1.00 (2.92, 0 points). Random 9014 gives 2.42 (0 points), random 9003 2.32 (4 points), random 9010 2.11 (0 points). The shared-prohibition ADD at alpha 2 gives full sort 15, size-k heap 31, quickselect 4 at pass 1.00 (2.32).
- Two sum: random 9002 at alpha 2 gives hash map 26, brute force 23 at pass 1.00 (2.12, 0 points).
- Shortest path: random 9004 at alpha 1 gives Dijkstra 26, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 22 at 4 points (1.97). That is as diverse as the semantic seed at a lower pass cost.
- [ARTIFACT:art_1AYTO1Epb_7t]: the novelty instruction on substring search gives naive 37, KMP 11, Boyer-Moore-Horspool 1, built-in 1 at pass 1.00 (1.99).
Table 110 hides this. It reports avoidance only, without compositions or pass rates, and omits the three random directions at alpha 2. Those moved kth smallest (0.96), find duplicate (0.86, to sort and adjacent check) and two sum (0.48 and 0.36). On find duplicate and two sum, ADD at alpha 2 moved nothing (0.00). 'Every activation edit ... acted like a random direction' therefore hides that, on kth smallest and two sum, the random directions are the cheapest diversity knob the run found.

An executed result that bears directly on the record's main open question is missing. Section 3.11 says what decides the replacement under a modal ban 'remains open'. [ARTIFACT:art__5akZ9W9iZM4] results/landing_by_route.json gives the composition of the programs that left the default under every route arm.
- Connected components: the full ban lands BFS 75, DFS 25. The prompt route lands DFS 56, BFS 44; the direct route DFS 70, BFS 10; the full knockout DFS 57, BFS 43. Every Jensen-Shannon divergence against the full ban is outside the artifact's null. Union find is removed redundantly by either route, but BFS is chosen only when both routes act. Either route alone picks DFS, which is second in the baseline likelihood order and is Qwen's association answer.
- Kth smallest: the direct route alone almost eliminates size-k heap (quickselect 74, size-k heap 1, against 70 and 28 under the full ban).
- Find duplicate: the knockout lands on Floyd cycle detection 3 of 5 times.
Section 3.6 reports only the default's shares (Table 106) and the full-ban landing.
critiques.suggested_action:
1. Add a table of landing compositions per arm (a, c, d, knockout, one-shot veto) for the five gated tasks, with the JS divergence against the full ban and its null.
2. State the reading: on connected components, the routes together choose the substitute, which neither route chooses alone.
3. Compare each single-route landing with the frozen families (association, baseline likelihood order, proximity), and carry the result into Section 3.11 as a lead.
Expected impact: +0.5.

critiques.description:
The Llama contest scores top-1 hits against a label the report never defines, and Table 102 mislabels it.
- Definition: in [ARTIFACT:art_Q-qh-9HhPoWo] src/scoring.py (realised_hit), present-minor events are scored against the survivor with the largest excess over the renormalised baseline, not against the modal landing.
- Mislabelled rows: three entries of Table 102's 'Modal landing' column are not modal.
  - Top-k frequent, ban of sort by count: modal is heap, 54 of 75 attempts not banned; reported 'quickselect on counts', 12.
  - Substring search, ban of KMP: modal is naive, 48 of 66; reported Boyer-Moore-Horspool, 5.
  - Connected components, ban of DFS: modal is union find, 79 of 85; reported BFS, 4.
  Under this rule the ladder, which nominates the default, is scored a miss on events where the default is what the model writes.
- The 'other' label: the ladder's 7 of 13 hits include find duplicate, where both its top-1 and the landing are 'other' (50 of 94 attempts, 2 correct). The ladder nominated 'other' on 3 of the 13 gated events. With 'other' excluded as a nominee and as a landing, the ladder hits 6 of 13 (exact binomial p = 0.11 at chance 0.27). 'Ladder and association each named the landing above chance' therefore holds for association only (7 of 13, p = 0.037).
- Unstated replication: on these present-minor events Llama returns to its default (union find 0.93, heap 0.72, naive 0.73 of attempts not banned). That is the snap-back of the Qwen exposure experiment, replicated in a second model family, and the record does not say so.
critiques.suggested_action:
1. State the hit-label rule in Section 3.5.
2. In Table 102, report the modal landing and the largest-excess landing side by side.
3. Recompute hits and binomial tests with 'other' excluded.
4. Add one sentence, with the shares, noting that Llama's present-minor bans snap back to the default, and carry it into Section 3.10 as a cross-model replication.
Expected impact: +0.25 to +0.5.

critiques.description:
The bench event gate counts failing programs labelled 'other' as avoidance. Section 3.2.3 corrected exactly this for the TOP ban list, where catalogue-only avoidance is 0.00 against the reported 0.13.
- Merge intervals passes the gate in both the bench forecast and the bench route experiments only through 44 failing 'other' programs. Avoidance into the catalogue is 0.14 to 0.15 (union find 14 or 15).
- The record calls these programs 'a merge sweep without sorting'. A regex pass over the 44 programs in [ARTIFACT:art_1AYTO1Epb_7t] data/samples.jsonl finds about 32 that build a boolean coverage or point-marking array over the coordinate range, 10 unsorted sweeps and 2 others. All 44 fail.

Consequences:

Coverage of the original request is still partial.
The request requires 'actual geometry plots, actual activation space, not some summary bar charts', including a manifold with centroids coloured by implemented count, before and after prohibiting the top five. Those plots exist:
- [ARTIFACT:art_IVZc3TWCeE9f] figures/fig_manifold_t1_{baseline, single_bfs, multi_TOP, multi_ARC, multi_SCATTER, multi_TOP5} and fig_manifold_t2_*: 13 Isomaps with banned centroids crossed out and implemented counts on the centroids. Under TOP5 the counts sit on the banned BFS (63) and DFS (36) centroids.

critiques.description:
Iteration 3's positive claims are not set against their nearest published neighbours. Table 92 covers the iteration-2 claims only.
(a) Snap-back under exposure bans. The closest prior design is denial prompting in NeoCoder [23], which forbids, step by step, the techniques used in the model's previous solution. The record cites [23] only for ban lists.
(b) Wording dominates compliance (template SD 2.0 logits; one template is the weakest in every artifact). Nearest are Sclar et al. 2023 (FormatSpread, ICLR 2024: up to 76 accuracy points from formatting alone) and Heo et al. [58].
(c) Enforcement at the first body token. Qi et al. [63] is cited inline, but the prefill-depth result is not compared with prefilling attacks on refusals.
(d) Signature vetoes respelled around. Biagiola et al. [62] appears only as a contrast for an iteration-2 claim.
(e) No correct novel algorithm. Nearest are NoveltyBench [44] and NeoCoder [23].
(f) The random-push diversity of the first critique, once reported. Nearest are residual-stream noise steering (arXiv 2604.03380, 2026) and STARS (arXiv 2601.22010, ICLR 2026), which report that perturbing or steering residual-stream activations raises output diversity beyond what sampling randomness gives.
critiques.suggested_action:
Add a Table 92b with one row per iteration-3 positive claim: the neighbour's finding, then what this run adds, or 'replication'.
Expected impact: +0.25.

1. In all three contests, report defined-only hit rates together with the number of defined events.
2. If fractional tie credit is kept, report it separately.
3. Rewrite the exposure sentence in Section 3.4 and Table 120 accordingly.

critiques.description:
Table 82 treats behavioural replicates as independent events.
- The 17 Qwen 'events' are 11 distinct likelihood rows in [ARTIFACT:art_6zBfl3kDjeiP] results/c1.json.
- The 8 'modal bans' are 2 rows (BFS and Dijkstra), each scored four times against identical cells, so 8 of 8 [0.68, 1.00] is really 2 of 2.
- Per distinct row: the gain and residual argmax hit 0 of 11, and the implied mass hits 8 of 11. Six of those 8 are bans of absent algorithms, where the landing is the default and the argmax is trivially right.
The conclusion that the gains cannot decide the claim stands. The implied mass's track record is weaker than its interval suggests.
critiques.suggested_action:
1. Report Table 82 per distinct likelihood row, with modal and sham rows separated.
2. Drop the Wilson intervals computed over replicates.

critiques.description:
Several conclusions in Section 3.10 and the closing section say more than their tables show.
(a) Item 2: 'The ladder forecast wins the frozen contest (7 wins; top-1 0.77).' This omits what Section 3.4 shows: the counting rule advances some family in 85% of no-information simulations; the label-permutation placebo advances subtraction in 100% of draws and the ladder in 43%; and no paired test survives Holm on the named events. Wording changes the landing, not only compliance. In the template arm ([ARTIFACT:art_WiY4wqHLb9Gy] results/other_reports.json), the modal replacement is the default for 13 of 19 priority algorithms, against 15 of 19 under the fifth template. It flips to the associate for size-k heap (quickselect 13, full sort 2 under templates one to four; full sort 10 under the fifth) and for the Z algorithm (KMP 29, naive 11; against naive 44, KMP 6). Snap-back rests on a single wording.
(b) 'The ban gives way at the first body token' is resolved to one token only on kth smallest. On the other four gated tasks, the shortest prefix that undoes the ban is 10 to 30 tokens long.
(c) The reach experiment's disconfirmation on kth smallest uses the token walk's fallback rung. Three bench draws put the ban's landing on quickselect (59 to 79%), which makes quickselect the behavioural second rung; under that definition the cell confirms the claim (size-k heap, will 0.00). Connected components disconfirms under either definition.
(d) 'Generated tokens reading the ban carry more of the pooled effect than the prompt states (0.74 against 0.61)' compares point estimates whose jackknife intervals overlap, with a negative interaction.
critiques.suggested_action:
1. Add the calibration caveat and the template-arm landings to item 2 of Section 3.10.
2. Restate item 5 as 'at the opening of the body (to a single token on kth smallest)'.
3. Drop kth smallest from the one-rung disconfirmation, or label it as dependent on the rung definition.
4. Replace 'carry more' with both fractions and their intervals.

dimension_scores.justification: Most iteration-3 conclusions are proportionate and recompute exactly. One conclusion contradicts the run's own evidence: the closing knob verdict. Section 3.2.5, the 2.3.6 correction and the closing section say no knob reaches an even two-algorithm split under 20 points, and that only the semantic seed and the A* mention buy a second correct algorithm. Table 91's decommitment row (1.913 [1.705, 2.088] at 17 points, a 54:23 split) meets the same criterion. The iteration-3 locus artifact holds random-direction and ADD arms at rarefied Hill-1 2.1 to 2.9 for 0 to 4 points on kth smallest, and 2.12 for 0 points on two sum. Smaller overreaches: the Llama 'aimed above chance' claim depends on 'other' being scored as a hit; merge intervals is gated only through failing 'other' programs; the 8 of 8 modal-ban count is two likelihood rows repeated over four draws.

A reader who was not on the run can follow each iteration: why each artifact ran, what the review objected to, what each table settles. Corrections are marked and dated. The weaknesses are inconsistent conventions that a reader cannot detect from the text. Table 120 and fig_forecast_hits mix three rules for undefined forecasts. Table 102's 'Modal landing' column is a largest-excess label on three rows. Table 110 shows avoidance without compositions or pass rates, and only at alpha 1 for the random controls.

The report preserves almost all of a very large run, including every iteration-3 artifact with full tables, its dead ends and its bookkeeping. Executed outputs still missing: landing compositions per route arm (results/landing_by_route.json); the random-direction arms read as knobs, with the alpha-2 controls; a knob view of the bench forecast arms; template-specific exposure landings; an audit of the iteration-3 'other' landings; and figure markers for the activation-space manifolds the request demanded.

review.overall_assessment: This record has improved a great deal. All nine major and three minor items of the previous review are answered with new analysis, and Table 80 maps each item to where it is answered. The chronology holds: I diffed Sections 1 and 2 against the pre-iteration-3 draft, and every change carries an iteration-3 marker. The budget moved from likelihood variants to sampled events: 12 bench tasks in two models, 33 exposure algorithms and 13,030 route samples, with forecasts sealed by hash before any ban. I recomputed the iteration-3 headlines from raw files (verify_iter3.py/.log in this workspace) and all of them match. Exposure: 31 gated, 30 disagreeing, modal replacement equal to the default in 24 of 31 (14 of 18 priority), default share 0.72 (named) and 0.82 (unnamed), wins 7/2/2/0. Bench forecast: 5 of 12 tasks gated; mean log score minus uniform +0.06 (ladder), -0.69 (subtraction), -1.53 (proximity), -1.78 (association). Route fractions: per task and pooled 0.611/0.744/0.621. Llama contest: 13 gated, hits 7/7/4/3, exact Wilcoxon two-sided p 0.0029/0.0020/0.52/0.77. Likelihood argmax: 0 of 17 (gain) against 14 of 17 (implied mass). Reach novelty audit: 30/7/1 of 38. C2d: 0 of 5. results_reported is therefore true. Soundness is 1 for one reason. The record's answer to the request's 'can we influence it?' contradicts its own evidence. The closing section says no knob reaches an even two-algorithm split under 20 pass points, and that the semantic seed and the A* mention are the only conditions that buy a second correct algorithm. Two rows below in Table 91, the decommitment direction has an interval that includes 2. The iteration-3 locus artifact, which was never entered into the knob table, has matched-norm random directions on kth smallest at rarefied Hill-1 2.1 to 2.9 for 0 to 4 points, and on two sum one random direction reaches 2.12 for 0 points. Other gaps: route-specific landings that show the substitute flips with route on connected components are missing. The Llama hit label is undefined in the report and mislabelled in Table 102, and the ladder's above-chance claim depends on 'other'. Failing 'other' programs count as avoidance, which gates merge intervals. The request's activation-space plots exist but carry no figure marker. The iteration-3 claims are not set against their nearest neighbours. What the record does support, descriptively: a strong collapse in Qwen3-8B. Shown a solution and told not to use it, the model snaps back to its default. The frozen counting rule agrees, though its own null simulation shows the rule is weak, and Llama's present-minor bans show the same pattern without the record noticing. Whether a ban acts through the prompt states or through generated tokens depends on the task. The ban gives way once the default's opening is forced. Wording dominates compliance. Token vetoes are respelled around. No correct novel algorithm appeared on memorised tasks. The fixes are narrow, mostly re-analysis of data already on disk.
strengths: Every item of the previous review is answered with new analysis rather than rewording: likelihood diagnostics (Tables 81-84), reconciliation of the two verdicts on the rival account, implemented counts on the manifolds (Tables 85-86b), correct-only Llama compositions (Tables 89-90), the knob verdict restated in its own metric, positioning of the iteration-2 claims (Table 92), and the preregistered predictions and their outcomes (Section 3.1). Table 80 maps each item to where it is answered.

The chronology holds. A sentence-level diff of Sections 1 and 2 against work/paper_draft_before_iter3.md shows that every change, including deleted wording such as the 'circle answered in the negative' clause, is replaced by a correction marked 'iteration 3' that quotes or describes what changed.

The budget moved from estimator variants to sampled, preregistered events, as the last review asked. 1,200 Qwen and 1,800 Llama bench bans were sampled after forecasts were hash-sealed, alongside 33 exposure algorithms with copy, named and unnamed arms, 13,030 common-random-number route samples and a second independent route draw. The frozen counting rule was itself calibrated, with a no-information simulation (85% false advance) and a label permutation, and the record reports that the rule is weak.

Traceability is excellent. Each table names its source file, and every headline I recomputed from raw rows matched to the reported precision, including exposure, bench forecast, route fractions, Llama Wilcoxon and binomial tests, likelihood argmax counts and novelty-audit classes.

Dead ends and failures are kept with the evidence that closed them. The title claim of the hypothesis update is reported as not surviving in its stated form; FRLP, signature vetoes, the shared prohibition direction, head ablation and long-form novelty instructions are each listed with their numbers; and failed preregistered predictions are listed.

The request's novelty question gets a direct, audited answer. 0 of 78 correct out-of-catalogue programs from iterations 1 and 2 and 0 of 38 from iteration 3 were novel, under two blind judges, a tie-break and a full manual read, with rule-of-three bounds. The long-form 2,000-word instruction was finally run, with thinking on and off.

The controls are carefully designed: token-length-matched neutral twins, exact common-random-number coupling, placebo splices, matched-norm random directions, a fairer SAE transfer criterion together with a placebo that shows it is lenient, and fp32 rescoring of the bench likelihoods.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration the pool holds: (1) a repaired record (artifact 1). It contains implied-mass C1 tables and the variance diagnostic, which say whether likelihoods could ever decide C1 at affordable M; the 14 manifold figures with implemented-count tables and a g16 recomputation; Llama correct-only tables; the knob table under a declared class rule; an audit of every correct out-of-catalogue program, giving the run's direct answer to the novelty question; positioning rows; and a corrections file covering every reviewer item. (2) About 30 Qwen confirmation events (12 modal bans, 19 to 33 exposure bans) and about 15 Llama events (12 modal and 3-4 present-minor bans). Each has hash-committed SUBTRACT, LADDER, ASSOCIATE and PROXIMITY forecasts, sampled landings with correct-only compositions, and per-event log scores in one schema, so the advance rule is decided per artifact and the pooled Wilcoxon is mechanical. (3) On the bench: C2b (veto versus ban), and C2a and C2c (behavioural route fractions and their link to veto sufficiency) on gated bans, with prefill results. On both path tasks: screen vetoes. (4) C2d (the X-free direction, ADD and SUBTRACT), C2e (decoders at generated tokens 1-8, saved for the first time, with a causal patch if a locus appears), C2f (the heads), the corrected SAE verdict with an SAE readout if it passes, and a manifold at the tokens 1-3 states. (5) C3: will-versus-can on 4 bench and 2 path tasks, two-step bans, and the token walk with the rung and pass cost per step, including the top-five operation on the grid task; and the long-form novelty arm with judge audits. NEXT ITERATION: one CPU evaluation pools C1 across models and artifacts (Wilcoxon over disagreeing gated events, Holm, direction required in each model) and writes the verdict on the title. If subtraction holds, the account is generalised to held-out task families and a third model, and the token walk and the X-free direction become the knobs studied. If substitution wins, the winning family names the rule and is tested on new events.
strategies.objective: Decide whether a 'do not use X' prompt performs one operation: removing the named default, after which the model falls to the next rung of its own distribution, readable in advance with no ban text. The rival is that the prompt chooses its replacement, either the model's stated alternative to X or the survivor nearest X's code. The test runs on 12 coding tasks that have never seen a ban prompt, in two model families. The strategy then locates where the removal is applied (prompt states before the first token versus generated tokens reading the ban, a task-general prohibition direction, generated tokens 1-3), measures how far any knob can push the model (prompts versus cumulative token vetoes), and answers from data whether anything yields a correct novel algorithm. It also repairs every reviewer item on the record.
strategies.rationale: WHY DEEPEN, AND WHAT THE OBJECT IS. Every observation after two iterations fits 'remove, then fall one rung'. The substitute is fixed and is the runner-up: Bellman-Ford/SPFA in 272/272 and 255/260 programs, DFS in 257/257. Every push that leaves Dijkstra lands on Bellman-Ford/SPFA, random directions included (8 of 8). The ban acts through the prompt states as a veto of the default's opening: 0/100 grid-ban programs open with the default import, against 99/100 under the neutral twin. Prompts never reach past rung 2: Floyd-Warshall is written 0.00 as the sole allowed algorithm, though forced Floyd-Warshall is 40/40 correct. But the run has never sampled an event on which this account can lose, because on every event the model's stated alternative was also its runner-up. The object of this iteration is therefore fixed: the 'remove, then fall one rung' account. Every slot attacks it from a different side, on events where it and substitution make different predictions. THE SIDEWAYS MOVE. The likelihood instrument is demoted to descriptive. It failed its gate in both models, and its X-specific residuals pointed away from the realised substitutes. The strategy moves to an instrument that cannot be degenerate under collapse: SAMPLED landings under ban-free counterfactuals, committed before any ban is sampled. The counterfactuals are the signature veto (a decoding-time mask of the default's distinctive tokens) and generic pushes. It also moves to where the two accounts disagree. I computed this arithmetic from the frozen bench files of art_0ndRfWKBWclR before planning. Across the 12 frozen tasks, 33 non-default algorithms have at least one correct, correctly labelled forced program, and so are eligible exposure targets. For 19 of them the model's stated alternative is NOT its default: on substring search, Rabin-Karp's associate is KMP while the default is naive search; on k-th smallest, the size-k heap's associate is quickselect while the default is a full sort. Exposure bans on those 19 put the associate and the next rung in direct competition. If half pass the gate, Qwen alone clears the 10-event floor of the preregistered Wilcoxon. The 12 modal bans add events where the associate is unwritable or rare, so the veto and the associate are likely to split there too: forced matrix power on Fibonacci is correct in 4/40 programs, forced interval tree on merging in 0/40, and forced DP with bisect on interval scheduling in 0/40. HOW THE SEVEN SLOTS MAP. FIX and CLEANER MEASURE: artifact 1 (evaluation) repairs the record. It recomputes the likelihood claims on estimable mass, delivers the manifold figures, the Llama correct-only tables and the knob table under a declared class rule, and audits every out-of-catalogue program the run has produced. MORE POWER, on new events: artifact 2 runs the 12 bench modal bans in Qwen with committed ban-free forecasts, and also carries C2b, whether a one-shot veto reproduces the ban's landing. CONFOUND, tested head-on: artifact 3 runs the exposure bans, where substitution can win. REPLICATION in a second family: artifact 4 runs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on the same bench, with its present-minor bans and correct-only reporting. MECHANISM, the route: artifact 5 measures behavioural KV-splice route fractions on the bench, the cross-task link between veto sufficiency and the direct route, and prefill arms. MECHANISM, the internals: artifact 6 adds and removes the X-free prohibition direction at the task-specification positions, saves the first states at generated tokens 1-8, ablates the three ban-attending heads, and recomputes the SAE verdict under a corrected criterion. BOUNDARY: artifact 7 measures how far prompts and cumulative token vetoes push. It runs leave-one-survivor bans, two-step bans, and the token walk, which turns the request's top-five prohibition into an operation the model cannot ignore. It also runs the request's long-form novelty instruction with thinking on and off. POSITIVE TARGETS, which the paper leads with if they hold: ban-free forecasts beat the stated alternative on disagreeing events in both models; a one-shot veto reproduces the ban's landing; pooled behavioural F_prompt is at least 2/3 on the bench; an X-free direction leaves the default better than random and lands on the same rung; prompts reach one rung while token vetoes reach further. Each has a named disconfirming outcome that is still reported as a mechanism: substitution reclaims the title, the ban carries content beyond removal, there is no shared prohibition representation, or vetoes are bypassed. REVIEWER MAP. Artifact 1 covers the FRLP diagnostics, the ladder reconciliation, the manifold figures, Llama correct-only, the iteration-2 PREDICT outcome and M arithmetic, the positioning rows, the route wording, the novelty audit, the knob verdict, the preregistered-predictions list and the factual slips. Artifact 6 covers the SAE criterion. Artifact 7 covers the long-form novelty prompt. Artifacts 2-4 together supply the behavioural test of ladder against association on bench tasks where runner-up and associate differ. On 'samples, not variants': the budget goes to about 30,000 new labelled programs on events, and FRLP gets no new variants. BUDGET: about 15 A4500 GPU-hours across artifacts 2-7 (bench programs are short, 20-250 tokens); OpenRouter at most about USD 5 in total.

Corrections: Manifold Steering is an ICML 2026 MI-workshop spotlight, not main track; IFG is an ICML 2025 EXAIT workshop poster; the Invisible Lottery is confirmed as an ICML 2026 main-conference poster (keep); Tang's 'implementation priors' is VERIFIED in Sec. 5.3 of the v1/v2 PDF; Di Cicco's AUC is 0.931 (v1), 0.955 (v2) and 0.881 (v3, latest); 'self-decodable' appears only in Brewing v1; ICLR 2027 contemporaneity is two months and arXiv-only papers are exempt (the Reviewer Guide's 'September 16' conflicts with the Dates page's Sep 25). Contradicting evidence: temperature above 1 raises algorithmic diversity elsewhere (Lee et al., Findings EMNLP 2025); agents' H-creativity (2608.30047); FunSearch/AlphaEvolve; departure-matched decoding.
