hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: Iteration 5 answers how the algorithm choice manifests (a base repertoire narrowed by tuning at the plan site, tested by transplant) and how to influence it cheaply (nudges against text-level plan samplers), plus the literal 1a-c cell.
key_changes: Title and object deepened, not replaced: the plan-noise lead (plan-site nudges move ideas where temperature only moves words) gets a mechanism for its boundary. Post-training narrowed a base-model repertoire, and nudges reopen it.

New primary A1/A2: the base model's repertoire (beta = base correct-only non-default share; r = base runner-up) predicts which tasks a nudge moves and where it lands. It is confirmed on at least 12 new ban-free-screened tasks (the reviewer's steer to expand the panel), against rivals including the novelty instruction.

New primary B (causal, never run): transplant Qwen3-8B-Base task-specification states (blocks 12-23) into the instruct prefill, with read-position, late-block, matched-random and cross-task controls. A de-sharpening push along base-minus-instruct is secondary.

Price claim demoted to secondary C and attacked head-on: text-level plan samplers (IFG, PlanSearch-lite, enumerate-and-pick, base-intent), departure-matched decoding, plain-prompt plan noise, full-simplex hull.
Temperature carried as established (0/20 seeds, thinking off and on); the request's literal 1a-c cell (thinking on, top-k 10, same seed) is scheduled and never dropped.

Closed: forced-prompt plan subspace; further direction-level predictors on the old five tasks (signed progress); movability as a ban-compliance forecast (C3a: inconclusive primary, disconfirmed by default-drop, compromised positives); ban-landing contests beyond descriptive; top-five push at the plan; verbalized sampling; blocks 0-11 vs 12-23.

Instruments repaired: defaults only from twins at N>=50 with a NO DEFAULT rule; one ban-free dose unit everywhere (existing tasks re-measured); labeller style re-gate per family and unit; matched-event forecast rule; every best cell reported beside its per-direction distribution.

Step 0 answers every review item: held-out verdict per measure; site wording ('a prefill site at which noise is effective, not a locus'); landing claims on matched events with the find-duplicate counter-example; PNPLAIN, hull deviation, Llama block, units, GPU hours; distributions; Table 92c rows; exposure class; the Table 76 cross-reference.

Second family recast: gemma-3-4b pt/it, with pt-derived predictions committed before a fresh it push population. Labelled a replication on fresh samples, because Gemma's iteration-4 outcomes were seen.
Positioning: Step 5 runs a dated saturation search on base-vs-aligned diversity, base-aligned collaboration and base-to-instruct activation transplants before any novelty statement.
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: Leads only: plan-site noise moves ideas where temperature can't, on 5 of 15 tasks. Deepen: a causal mechanism for that boundary (base repertoire, transplant), new tasks, text-level baselines.

critiques.description:
The held-out test of the movability claim (Section 4.7, 4.10, closing) is reported as inconclusive under every sensitivity, but one preregistered sensitivity disconfirms it.
- Verdict. Section 4.7 says 'Every sensitivity stays inconclusive (Table 160)'. In art_k6nzFCDLOjQP results/c3a.json, 'compliance_as_default_share_drop' returns DISCONFIRMED (BA 0.568, Fisher p 1.0, rho 0.39). The experiment plan lists this sensitivity, and Table 160 itself labels the row 'disconfirmed'. The artifact README makes the same contradiction, and the report copied it.
- True positives. Two of the three true positives behind rho 0.54 are compromised, and the record discloses only one.
  - Grid task: the 'default' DFS was frozen from a 10-sample pilot (correct programs BFS 4, DFS 5; attempts 5 and 5; predictions/commit1.json). The 50-sample twin is BFS 25, DFS 25. 'Obeys' (avoidance 0.83) is therefore measured against a non-default baseline of 0.50. The grid escape (1 of 8 directions) measures BFS rising from 50%. Table 159 shows 'grid (DFS)' without the twin.
  - Shortest path task: the 'obey' rests on array-based Dijkstra labelled Bellman-Ford (disclosed). Without both tasks, BA is 0.61 and rho 0.31 (p 0.146).
- Same labelling failure elsewhere. It produces the top Gemma row of Table 163: plan noise 1.62 from 5 and 12 'bf_spfa' correct programs at alpha 1 and 2; the novelty instruction 1.96 from 29. The push-landing 4 of 4 (Table 162) includes both compromised tasks, and every family hits on both.

critiques.description:
Several landing conclusions generalise from one task or compare unmatched event sets.
(a) Route-landing lead. Sections 4.2.2 and 4.11 and the closing carry it forward: 'where a single route suffices to remove the default, it lands on the generic neighbour that pushes and the stated alternative agree on'. It comes from connected components. Table 127 contradicts it on find duplicate: the direct route alone removes the default (F_direct 0.99) and lands on index marking (74 of 78). That is neither the push landing (sort and adjacent check) nor the association answer (Floyd cycle detection). On two sum, pushes and association disagree, so there is no agreed neighbour.
(b) Item 6 of 4.10, 'that runner-up forecasts where a ban lands', is listed as established. It rests on:
  - 3 Qwen events, all seen before, with 2 top-1 hits (it misses connected components);
  - Gemma's 4 of 4, where only 2 events disagree and the other 2 are the tied grid task and the mislabelled shortest path task.
(c) Unmatched event sets. The closing and Table 157 compare the push forecast's mean over its 3 defined events (-0.76) with association's mean over 5 (-3.46). On the same 3 events association scores -3.11. With undefined forecasts scored as uniform, the push forecast scores -1.37 over all 5 (art_SHaWv77P1XCI results/c3b.json). This is the log-score form of the hit-rate defect the previous review raised.
(d) 'The landing is a property of the task, not of the direction' (4.6) holds across directions at one site, not across sites. On find duplicate, generated-token noise and the energy-matched read position land on Floyd cycle detection (5 and 6 correct programs). The plan-site screen escape landed on sort and adjacent check.
critiques.suggested_action:
1. Restate the route-landing lead as a single-task observation (connected components), with find duplicate as its counter-example.
2. Move item 6 from 'Established' to the descriptive results, with its counts: 2 of 3 seen Qwen events, 2 disagreeing Gemma events.
3. Report every forecast comparison on matched events, with the rule for undefined forecasts stated.
4. Qualify the 'property of the task' sentence with the site dependence on find duplicate.
Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description:
Executed results bearing on the iteration's primary claim are missing from the record.
(1) Plan noise without the twin frame. art_mWn-MQEnNelg ran plan noise on the plain prompt (PNPLAIN_a1, 350 programs): off-default share 0.16 on kth smallest (0.28 on the twin), 0.24 on connected components (0.12), 0.26 on the shortest path task (0.26), 0 on two sum and find duplicate. It is the only test that the knob works without the twin's 'Do not use <noun>' frame; that frame costs 18 pass points on the grid task. Section 4.3 reports the plain prompt without noise only.
(2) Hull deviation. Deviation D-hull-edges: the pre-registered hull search is restricted to edges. On random 5-vertex test cases it fell short of the full-simplex optimum by up to 0.19 Hill. Plan noise has 5 hull vertices against 2 or 3 for most comparison knobs, so any shortfall falls on it. On the real data the triangle_minus_edge check in results/prices.json shows at most +0.008 (connected components), so the verdict is unaffected. Neither the deviation nor the check is in the record.
(3) Llama knob verdict. The record audit priced 175 Llama cells but reports no Llama verdict. In tables/knob_table.csv, 0 of 36 Llama random-direction cells qualify, though they were three times the ban's displacement at layer 21. The 5 qualifying Llama knob cells are prompt bans and one veto (Fibonacci modal ban 2.43; substring one-shot veto 2.54). This cross-family check bears directly on 'random pushes buy correct diversity'.
(4) Dose units. The exp22 bench pushes used a unit 9 to 16% smaller than the screen's (its deviation 'ban_unit_scale'). Table 164 compares movability across experiments as if alpha meant the same push.
(5) Bookkeeping. Table 122 omits exp21's 2.74 GPU hours (results/gpu_hours.json).

critiques.description: Request item 1a to 1c asks what a tight temperature with top-k 10 and the same seed does to reasoning trajectories. The iteration-4 seed-coupled temperature block ran without top-k (top-p 1; top-k 10 only as one cell at T 0.7, thinking off). The thinking-on arm used Gumbel coupling without top-k. dimension_scores.justification: The experiments are sound and every headline number I recomputed matches. Four summary conclusions of the new section contradict the record's own tables. (a) Section 4.7 says 'Every sensitivity stays inconclusive (Table 160)'. The preregistered sensitivity 'compliance as the drop in default share' returns DISCONFIRMED (BA 0.568, Fisher p 1.0; art_k6nzFCDLOjQP results/c3a.json), and Table 160 itself labels the row 'disconfirmed'. (b) 4.10 item 3 and the closing say that the read position and the condition sentence change no algorithm 'at any dose'. The energy-matched read-position arm reported in Section 4.4 moved find duplicate (+0.23) and connected components (+0.18). (c) The closing calls the choice of algorithm 'located' in the task-specification states. The site rule returned PARTIAL, 4.10 lists the site claim under 'Inconclusive', and generated-token noise flips find duplicate 12:0 over the plan site (Table 146). (d) The route-landing lead of 4.2.2, 4.11 and the closing is contradicted by find duplicate in Table 127. Under the rule, a conclusion that contradicts the run's own evidence scores 1.

A reader who was not on the run can follow iteration 4: why each claim was tested (Section 4.1), the review items and where each is answered (Table 121), and per experiment its design, results, committed predictions and checks. The weaknesses are conventions the text does not state: 4.10 lists the site claim as both established (item 3) and inconclusive; Table 147 reports Hill numbers rarefied to depths 20, 9, 5, 7, 6 and 1 at alpha 4 without saying so; Table 157 and the closing compare means over 3 events and over 5 events; Table 159 shows each Gemma default without the twin composition that defines it.

The report preserves nearly all of a very large run. Every iteration-4 artifact appears with its full tables, dead ends and bookkeeping, and the earlier gaps are filled. Executed outputs still missing: the plan-noise arm on the plain prompt (exp19 PNPLAIN_a1); the hull edge-restriction deviation and its triangle check (exp19 D-hull-edges; at most +0.008 on the real data); a Llama verdict from the 175 Llama knob cells; the Gemma grid pilot and twin compositions; the 10 to 16% weaker dose unit of the exp22 bench pushes; the 2.74 GPU hours of exp21. Several neighbour rows of the positioning artifact were dropped, among them the nearest method to plan noise (NC-GRPO) and a contradicting row for the novelty claim.

review.overall_assessment: The record has absorbed the previous review. Every must-fix and minor item is answered with new analysis, and Table 121 maps each to its section: a 1,120-cell knob table with per-task verdicts and random-direction counts; landings per route arm; the Llama hit rule; a two-judge audit of every 'other' landing with catalogue-only avoidance; activation-space Isomaps with the position caveat; a seed-coupled thinking-on arm; and positioning Tables 92b and 92c. The chronology holds: I diffed Sections 1 to 3 against the iteration-3 draft, and all 18 changed hunks carry an 'iteration 4' marker. I recomputed the iteration-4 headlines from raw files (verify_iter4.py, verify_iter4.log), and every one I checked matches. Plan noise (exp19): the alpha sweep (Table 141), flips (Table 140), per-template shares (Table 142c) and the price decision (PARTIAL; count1 2, count2 4; mean margin -0.22 [-0.89, 0.30]; per-task 5-point Hill-1 2.72, 1.29, 1.00, 2.09, 1.42, 1.35). Site (exp20): 0 of 526 and 0 of 527 correct programs off the default at the read position and the condition sentence, 6 of 521 at the late blocks; the boundary; the top-five push (BFS only); plan-site indicator +2.15 [1.79, 2.51]. Same seed (exp21): temperature changes the algorithm in 0 of 20 seeds on all three tasks; plan-noise counts 17.25, 4.55 and 2.5; pooled contrast 0.545. Plan subspace (exp22): escape counts (kth smallest 12/40 and 25/40, and so on); pooled rho 0.033 [-0.03, 0.09]. Held-out family (exp23): table [[3,3],[1,8]], BA 0.739, Fisher 0.235, rho 0.537. results_reported is true. Soundness is 1, because four conclusions of the new section contradict the record's own evidence. (1) 'Every sensitivity stays inconclusive' (Section 4.7). The preregistered sensitivity that measures compliance as the drop in default share returns DISCONFIRMED in c3a.json, and Table 160 labels that row 'disconfirmed'. (2) The read position and the condition sentence 'changed no algorithm at any dose' (4.10 item 3; closing). Section 4.4 reports that the energy-matched read-position arm moved two tasks. (3) The choice of algorithm is 'located' in the task-specification states (closing). The site rule returned PARTIAL, 4.10 lists the site claim as inconclusive, and generated-token noise flips find duplicate 12:0 over the plan site. (4) The route-landing lead carried into 4.11 and the closing. Find duplicate in Table 127 contradicts it. Two confounds of the held-out test are undisclosed. Gemma's grid 'default' was frozen from a 10-sample pilot, and its twin is BFS 25, DFS 25. Its shortest path 'obey' and its top price row rest on array Dijkstra labelled Bellman-Ford. Executed results missing from the record: plan noise on the plain prompt; a hull-search deviation and its check (harmless on the real data); the Llama knob verdict. What the record does support: with coupled seeds, temperature does not change the algorithm in Qwen3-8B, thinking off or on, and it buys no correct diversity in gemma-3-4b-it either; a random displacement of the task-specification prefill states changes it on 4 to 5 of 15 tasks, cheaply on kth smallest and connected components; per unit of downstream displacement, the read position, condition sentence and late blocks are far less effective; the forced-prompt subspace does not explain which directions work; no knob produced a correct novel algorithm. The fixes are restatements of conclusions, plus reporting arms that are already on disk.
strengths: Every item of the blocking iteration-3 review is answered with new analysis rather than wording: one knob table of 1,120 cells under a declared class rule with per-task verdicts and random-direction counts (Tables 123 to 126), landings per route arm (Table 127), the Llama hit rule under five labelling rules (Table 129), a two-judge audit of all 226 'other' programs plus catalogue-only avoidance (Tables 131 to 132b), defined-only hit rates (Table 134) and Table 82 per distinct row (Table 135). Table 121 maps each item to its answer.

The chronology is intact. Diffing Sections 1 to 3 against the iteration-3 draft gives 18 changed hunks, all marked 'Correction, iteration 4' or 'Added in iteration 4'; old wording is kept inside the marks.

Every iteration-4 headline I recomputed from raw rows matches the report exactly: Tables 137, 140, 141, 142c, the inert-site counts (0/526, 0/527, 6/521), the boundary and top-five rows, the seed counts of Table 150 and the 0.545 contrast, the escape counts of Table 154, the pooled subspace rho 0.033, and the Gemma confusion table, BA, Fisher p and Spearman rho.

The new experiments are well controlled. Decision rules were hash-committed before the decisive samples. Common random numbers turn site and temperature contrasts into exact paired flips (Tables 140, 146, 150). Downstream displacement is matched (indicator +2.15 [1.79, 2.51]; Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio 5.72). Every Qwen engine reproduced the iteration-3 screen byte for byte. Independent rederivations and placebos ran in every artifact.

Negative and partial verdicts are kept as such, with their evidence: the price claim is PARTIAL; the plan subspace is disconfirmed, with a decomposition showing the subspace is not needed (Table 155); the targeted push fails on 5 of 6 tasks; verbalized sampling is closed as a run-time dispatcher artifact; the frozen counting rule is abandoned because it fires on noise.

The request's temperature question (1a to 1c) now has an executed answer in both thinking modes, with an uncoupled check in gemma-3-4b-it. Under seed coupling the algorithm never changes while phrasings grow, and the thinking-on result is read against a measured repeat noise floor.

Novelty is audited in every artifact with two blind judges plus a manual read (0 novel among 14,206 correct programs of the site and subspace experiments alone). The positioning audit checked 112 verbatim quotes and records which lanes are partly occupied and which baselines are missing (text-level plan samplers, departure-matched decoding).

The bookkeeping is preserved: hardware departures (FP8 W8A8 on a 16 GB card; gemma-3-4b-it instead of gemma-2-9b-it), spend per artifact, unit changes made before commitment, and the dropped Llama screen body.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration the pool holds: (1) a repaired record with no internal contradiction: a single-statistic knob table for every iteration-3 arm (plus the new arms) with the number of qualifying random directions per task, the per-task diversity verdict rewritten, Table 110 with alpha-2 rows and compositions, landing by route for the five gated tasks with Jensen-Shannon divergences and nulls, the Llama hit rule stated and hits recomputed without 'other', catalogue-only avoidance beside avoidance with residue-gated events marked and audited, figure-ready activation-space manifolds with position captions, and the frozen screen file. (2) The C1 decision on the six movable tasks: H5, P15 and P20 for plan noise against temperature 1.3 and 1.6, top-k 10, the nonce ban, the novelty instruction, the semantic seed and the iteration-3 vetoes, on one hull convention with bootstrap intervals, plus R2 as a held-out task and the other 8 bench tasks reported. (3) Site specificity: price curves at six sites on six tasks, with the plan site best on at least 4 of 6 or the generic-perturbation reading stated. (4) The same-seed answer to 1a-c: seeds whose algorithm changes across temperature (thinking off and on) against across plan-noise draws, and phrasings per idea by temperature at three thresholds. (5) The plan subspace: C2a Spearman on 40 new directions per movable task, the causal decomposition of escaping directions, a targeted half-distance push against random at matched norm, cross-knob projections (C2b), plan-site Isomap and MDS figures with centroids coloured by implemented count, and Qwen's push-landing and opening-ladder forecasts scored against the iteration-3 landings. (6) The confirmation of C3a and C3b in a held-out family with hash-committed predictions, rival predictors and correct-only compositions, and C1 replicated there. (7) The novelty boundary to alpha 8 with a full judge audit, the top-five prohibition at the plan scored edge versus opposite side, and Tables 92b and 92c with verified quotes. NEXT ITERATION: if C1 and C3a hold, the paper leads with 'the plan moves ideas, temperature moves words, and ban compliance is a property of the plan basin', and the next round adds a second held-out family and the targeted push as a practical diversity knob; if the site test or the subspace test fails, the claim is restated as generic perturbation of the specification states and the mechanism question moves to what the escaping directions share.
strategies.objective: Decide, on fresh samples and in a held-out model family, whether nudging the task-specification states of the middle layers (plan noise) is the knob that moves the ALGORITHM while temperature moves only the WORDING, and what that implies. Four contributions: (1) a price table showing that plan noise buys correct algorithmic diversity (correct-only Hill-1 of 1.5 within 5 pass points) on screen-movable tasks where temperature, top-k, the nonce ban, the novelty instruction, the semantic seed and token vetoes do not, priced on one hull convention; (2) evidence that the effect is specific to the plan site and carried by a low-dimensional plan subspace read from forced prompts, shown causally and drawn in actual activation coordinates; (3) the same-seed answer to the request's question 1a-c, with thinking off and on; (4) a confirmed, ban-free forecast of ban compliance (movability) in a model family never run, plus the novelty boundary (no correct algorithm outside the catalogue up to breakage) and the top-five prohibition applied at the plan. The CPU repair of every blocking review item ships alongside, so the record stops contradicting its own evidence.
strategies.rationale: WHY DEEPEN, AND WHAT THE OBJECT IS. Three iterations of ban-landing contests produced no forecasting rule, but iteration 3 left one effect that no knob table had shown: matched-norm random pushes at the task-specification states of blocks 12-23 made Qwen3-8B write two or three different CORRECT algorithms for one prompt at almost no pass cost (kth smallest: 7 of 15 directions escape, five reach Hill-1 of 2 or more, best 2.92 at pass 1.00; two sum: 2 of 3 at alpha 2, Hill-1 2.13 at pass 1.00; shortest path: 3 of 15, best 1.97 at 4 points), and the tasks those pushes move are exactly the tasks on which bans are obeyed (6 of 6; 0 of 8 failing tasks moved). The object of this iteration is that result. Every slot attacks it from a different side, and the move is `deepen`, so no slot goes to a new candidate. THE SIDEWAYS SHIFT, STATED. The literal question 'where does a ban send the mass' came back unforecastable (no family beat uniform on Qwen's gated modal bans). The strategy moves, within the request's own question ('is temperature the creativity knob, and can creativity be influenced'), to the object that already came out positive: a knob that changes the idea, the place in the network where the idea is set, and the ban as one large displacement of that place. A ban's compliance becomes a prediction target (C3a) rather than the thing being forecast landing by landing. HOW THE SEVEN SLOTS MAP. FIX: artifact 1 repairs every blocking review item from data on disk (knob table for every iteration-3 arm with per-task counts of qualifying directions, landing by route, the Llama hit rule, the 'other' audit with catalogue-only avoidance, geometry figure markers, minor rigor, Section 3.10 wording) and freezes the screen file. MORE POWER and a CLEANER MEASURE: artifact 2 runs fresh per-sample plan noise against every decoding and prompt knob on 15 tasks at N = 50 per cell, priced on one hull convention, with an engine check that reproduces two screen rows in bf16. CONFOUND, head-on: artifact 3 asks whether noise of the same per-position size anywhere else (read position, condition segment, generated tokens, early or late layers) buys as much, which is the generic-perturbation reading that can make the plan reading lose; it also carries the BOUNDARY (alpha 8 to breakage, with a full novelty audit) and the request's top-five prohibition applied at the plan. The request's 1a-c, never dropped again: artifact 4 holds the token seed fixed and varies temperature (thinking off and on) or the plan-noise draw. MECHANISM: artifact 5 tests whether a plan subspace read from forced prompts predicts which random directions move the algorithm and whether it is causally needed (remove the component, keep only it, push half the centroid distance), and draws the geometry at this causal site. (i) Escape at N = 10 per direction is too noisy for C3a: a direction with a true 5% off-default rate passes 8.6% of the time, so 16 direction-alpha draws call a nearly immovable task movable 76% of the time; every N = 10 pass is now confirmed on 20 more samples with an exact test. (ii) Knob prices are read off a randomisation hull, because H5 of a one-setting instruction and of a four-setting alpha dial are otherwise not comparable, and the bootstrap includes the max over settings. (iii) With only 3 plan-noise draws, the same-seed test on shortest path (about 20% of directions escape) would fail half the time by lottery; artifact 4 runs 6 draws per alpha and scores every 3-draw subset, keeping the hypothesis's matched count of four conditions. (iv) The unsigned plan-subspace share of an isotropic direction is about (K-1)/4096 with large chance variation, so C2a also preregisters the signed component along the default-to-survivor axis and a causal decomposition test, so a null on the share alone cannot be mistaken for a null on the subspace. critiques.suggested_action:
(1) Report results/unit_ratio.json beside Table 174 and reconcile the two ratio definitions (mean of per-position ratios against ratio of mean norms). State that the dose unit cannot explain the drop.
(2) Mark iteration-4 'Established' items 2 to 4 and the frozen screen in place as FP8 W8A8 results that did not replicate in bf16 at the population level. Qualify the plan-sampler verdict and the movability half as bf16-conditional.
(3) Run the decisive control, about 1 GPU hour: on connected components and the shortest path task, apply the same 40 fresh directions and common-random-number slots at the same absolute displacement under (a) FP8 W8A8, (b) FP8 weights with bf16 activations, and (c) bf16.

critiques.description:
The landing half, the iteration's only 'Established' positive, is overstated and confounded.
(a) Selective tally. Section 5.10 says it 'replicates everywhere it could be measured' and counts 16 of 19 events, using the FP8 screen's 5 of 5 for the existing tasks. It omits the iteration's own bf16 remeasurement: panel A extra_arm_a.json lands kth smallest on size_k_heap and connected components on DFS, while the base runner-ups are quickselect and DFS. That is 1 of 2, and Section 5.4 itself calls it 'the landing check splits'. Section 5.12 ('when a nudge moves the instruct model, it moves it to the algorithm the base model writes next') and the closing repeat the universal, despite four iteration-5 misses: integer square root, Gemma kth smallest, Gemma connected components, and bf16 kth smallest.
(b) Unscored rival. The record never scores the instruct twin's own runner-up as a forecast, yet it explains half the hits.
- Qwen, by twin minority share: trapped rain water two pointers 0.36 (p0 0.363), single number XOR fold 4/50, MST Prim 17/50, all equal to the landing.
- Gemma, by twin attempts: grid BFS 19/50, substring built-in find 6/50, first-and-last binary search 4/50, all equal to the landing.
- On the 8 events where the twin wrote no alternative, the base runner-up hits 5: Qwen 3 of 4 (Poisson-binomial p 0.052), Gemma 2 of 4 (p 0.42), pooled p 0.053.
The record already used this explanation for the Gemma transplant ('amplified an existing minority mode') but not for the landing half.
(c) Thin base support for the Gemma forecasts, from predictors.json:
- the grid r_u (BFS) comes from 4 valid base attempts and 0 correct programs;
- kth smallest and connected components come from 6 attempts each;
- labels agree with an adjudication at 0.64.
(d) On trapped rain water and MST the instruct twin is more diverse than the base (0.36 against beta 0.23; 0.34 against 0.11), against the narrowing premise.
critiques.suggested_action:
(1) Restate the tally per set, including the bf16 existing-task check: 17 of 21 with the 1-of-2 added. Delete 'everywhere' and the universal sentences in 5.12 and the closing.
(2) Add a rival 'instruct twin's most frequent non-default program', defined where the twin wrote any. Score base runner-up against it on matched events. Report the hit rate and p on the subset where the twin wrote no alternative.
(3) Add per-event base support counts (valid and correct) to Tables 203, 214 and 217.
(4) Move 5.11 item 2 to the descriptive results unless the unconfounded subset reaches p < 0.05, and note the two units where instruct is more diverse than base.
Expected impact: removes the contradiction behind soundness 1 (+0.5 overall).

critiques.description:
The movability half is listed under 'Ruled out' without its power or interval, and its rival criterion was never evaluated on the pooled set.
Panel A's own README states that the design 'can only detect a strong relation (power about 0.46 at a true rho = 0.6 even when pooled with panel B)'. The pooled rho of 0.15 over 13 units has an approximate 95% interval of -0.44 to 0.65. The data therefore exclude a strong relation, not a moderate one. Neither statement is in the record.
Positive-control sensitivity was also low. In the bf16 regime, 2 of the 6 screen-movable tasks escape, and per-sample plan noise moves more than 10% of programs only on kth smallest (see the engine critique).
The preregistered criterion 'beta ahead of each rival' needs the frozen rivals on the pooled set. The two panels computed the runtime-merit rival differently: panel A uses a minimum runtime ratio with sign -, and panel B a runtime gap with values of either sign. Table 205 therefore omits rivals. Yet 5.12 names runtime merit as the leading lead from panel A alone, and panel B's values do not show the same pattern: MST moved with a slower alternative.
critiques.suggested_action:
(1) Report the pooled rho with a bootstrap or Fisher-z interval and the panels' power. Restate the verdict as 'beta is not a strong predictor; a moderate relation is not excluded at this n'.
(2) Recompute the frozen R6 (and R1, R4, R7, K) with one definition for all 13 units from the panels' files, and report the pooled rival comparison that the rule requires.
(3) Qualify the verdict as bf16-conditional, pending the engine control.
Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description:
Executed outputs are still missing or summarised without their table.
(a) The literal cell. results/literal_cell.json holds phrasing clusters per temperature, theta 0.8: 4, 3, 3 and 7 at T 0.3, 0.7, 1.0 and 1.3, with the repeat at 6 (theta 0.9: 8, 10, 9, 12). Table 206 omits them, though they are the 'phrasings' half of request item 1a-c in its literal form.
(b) The knob experiment's prices.json holds P15/P20 prices. Examples: base intent on connected components 0.005/0.011, enumerate and pick on the shortest path task 0.103/0.19, the novelty instruction on kth smallest P20 0.018. Tables 207-208 give only 5-point Hill-1, so the price comparison that iteration 4 made with P15/P20 cannot be repeated.
(c) The knob experiment's results/unit_ratio.json is not reported (see the engine critique).
(d) Panel B's per-unit knob rows are not tabulated, unlike panel A's Table 197; they cover the twin, PN alpha 1 and 2 and T1.3 compositions. On MST, T1.3 gives Prim 18/49, matching plan noise at 20/50, so temperature 'moves' an already-mixed twin. Panel B's repertoire_check (no support violations) is also unreported.
(e) Table 126c lists 3 of 5 Llama qualifying cells as 'not staged', though they sit in the iteration-4 record audit's tables/knob_table.csv. They are K0522-K0524, Llama kth smallest present-minor bans of heapify and pop, quickselect and size-k heap, at Hill-1 2.87, 2.96 and 2.92 and pass cost -12 to -27 points. A previous must-fix item is therefore incomplete.

critiques.description:
Coverage of the original request is partial on its central question, how creativity manifests inside the model. After five iterations the record has no representation of the choice: the plan subspace was disconfirmed, the SAE readout closed and NLA was unavailable. Its one internal positive, a prefill site at which noise changes the algorithm, rests on FP8 W8A8 runs that do not replicate in bf16 at the population level.
Iteration 5 moved to a behavioural base-against-instruct comparison. That is useful for 'can we influence it', but it leaves the internal account where iteration 4 left it.
The request's manifold-and-prohibition item has been run, but only at a label-dependent position (iteration 2) and at the plan site in FP8 (iteration 4). The record should say plainly which internal claims survive the engine change.
critiques.suggested_action:
In the next iteration, make an engine-robust internal account the precondition for any internal claim.
(1) Rerun the site comparison (plan site, read position, generated tokens) and the top-five plan push in bf16 on the two tasks that still move (kth smallest, connected components).
(2) If the site effect is FP8-specific, write in the closing that the internal account of the choice is open, and list the internal claims that survive.
Expected impact: +0.5 on coverage and contribution.

critiques.description: Item 4 of 5.11 ('Plan noise's effect is not its token-level departure from the twin') generalises from one task. The pooled 19 against 3 discordant slots at alpha 2 includes 13 against 0 on kth smallest. On the other four tasks it is 6 against 3, and on connected components matched decoding moved more (3 against 1). At alpha 1 there is no difference (4 against 3).

critiques.description: The undefined-forecast rule is unstated in Gemma's landing comparison, although the previous review asked for it everywhere. The '1.50 nats over association (Wilcoxon p 0.023)' includes first-and-last position, where association is undefined (q_assoc_defined false in e_a2.json) and is filled. The defined-only mean is 1.57.

critiques.description: The record does not say that collapse is not universal on the new tasks. Three of 15 new units are already mixed in the instruct twin at T = 1.0: trapped rain water at default share 0.64, MST at 0.66 and valid anagram at 0.76. On two of them the twin is more diverse than the base. The closing's opening paragraph and 5.11 item 3 ('the base model is more diverse than the instruct model on most tasks') are stated from the existing tasks only. This bears on the premise that Lee et al. contradict in part.

critiques.description: The zero-novelty count in the transplant experiment rests on the executor's manual override. dimension_scores.justification: The iteration's headline positive is stated more strongly than the record's own tables allow. 'The landing half replicates everywhere it could be measured' (5.10), the universal in 5.12 and the closing's '5 of 5 movable existing tasks' omit the bf16 remeasurement in Table 196 (kth smallest lands on size-k heap, not the base runner-up quickselect). Section 5.4 itself reports that as a miss. Half the hits are also predictable from the instruct twin's own minority mode, which the record never tests as a rival. Separately, the iteration-4 plan-noise effects collapse in bf16 at near-matched dose. The record keeps the dose unit as a possible cause, though its own unit_ratio.json rules that out, and it does not mark the iteration-4 'Established' items as engine-conditional. Under the rubric, a conclusion contradicting the record's own evidence scores 1.

A reader not on the run can follow the iteration: why it ran (5.1 with Table 166), what each artifact did, a table for each result with source files, and dead ends with their evidence. The main presentation defect is comparative. Section 5.10 and the fig_beta_escape data set FP8 existing-task escape fractions against bf16 new-task ones, while the like-for-like bf16 existing-task remeasurement (Table 196) sits in 5.4.

The record preserves nearly everything: seven artifacts, about 60 tables, every preregistered verdict and its sensitivities. A few executed outputs are still missing or summarised. The literal cell's phrasing clusters per temperature are missing, though they are the phrasing half of request item 1a-c. Also missing: the knob experiment's P15/P20 prices and unit ratios, panel B's knob rows, and three Llama qualifying cells left as 'not staged' though they are on disk. A previous must-fix (the Llama block) is therefore still incomplete.

review.overall_assessment:
Iteration 5 is a careful, well-bookkept record. Every must-fix item of the previous review was addressed with marked in-place corrections. A diff against work/paper_draft_before_iter5.md finds 27 changed blocks before the iteration-5 heading, all carrying iteration-5 markers, with the old wording quoted inside each marker. All seven iteration-5 artifacts are written up with source files per table. Three preregistered claims are reported as failures: the transplant (1 of 5), the plan sampler comparison (1 of 5) and the movability half (pooled Spearman 0.15).

I recomputed the headlines from the artifacts' own files (checks/recompute_iter5.py). Results:
- Movability half: panel A -0.030, panel B 0.206, pooled 13 units 0.146 (permutation p 0.315), 15 units 0.006.
- Landing half: pooled 6 of 7, Poisson-binomial p 0.0027; Wilcoxon p 0.055 against the corrected association.
- Gemma: A1 0.421 (p 0.060); A2 5 of 7 (p 0.025), Wilcoxon p 0.023.
- Plan sampler comparison: 1 win, D_bar -0.40 [-0.70, -0.24].
- Literal cell: 0 of 20.
- Transplant: top-k frequent 21 of 49, McNemar 19:0 against the matched random; kth smallest 2:20.
All match the report, so results_reported is true.

The record is blocked by two problems, both visible in its own files.
(1) The iteration's only 'Established' positive, the landing half, is stated as a universal that 'replicates everywhere it could be measured' (Section 5.10). Section 5.12 and the closing repeat it ('when a nudge moves the instruct model, it moves it to the algorithm the base model writes next'; '5 of 5 movable existing tasks'). The same section contradicts this. Under the iteration's own bf16 engine, kth smallest lands on size-k heap, while its base runner-up is quickselect (Table 196 against Table 182; Section 5.4 calls it a miss). Integer square root, Gemma kth smallest and Gemma connected components miss as well. In addition, 3 of the 6 Qwen hits and 3 of the 5 Gemma hits fall on units whose own instruct twin already writes the landing algorithm (8% to 38% of programs). On the 8 events where the twin wrote no alternative, the base runner-up hits 5 (p about 0.053).
(2) The run's main mechanistic positive, iteration 4's plan noise measured on an FP8 W8A8 engine, does not replicate in bf16 at near-matched dose. Off-default shares fall: connected components from 30/50 to 1/50 at alpha 2 (Fisher p 4e-11), shortest path from 27/50 to 2/50, and kth smallest from 14/50 at 1 ban unit to 4/50 at 1.39 units. The knob experiment's own results/unit_ratio.json measured the bf16 dose at 0.89 to 1.39 ban units per alpha. The record still leaves the cause 'not established' and still attributes it partly to the dose unit, so the iteration-4 'Established' items and two iteration-5 comparisons are engine-conditional without saying so.

Coverage of the request is partial. The behavioural questions are answered: temperature, top-k, the same seed, context seeds, instructions, bans and novelty. The internal question ('how does creativity manifest inside the model') still has no representation of the choice, and its one positive site effect may be an artefact of the quantised engine.
strengths: All five must-fix items and three minor items of the previous review are answered, with a review-item-to-location map (Table 166). The corrections are marked in place, and the diff confirms no unmarked edits to earlier sections. Examples: the held-out verdict per compliance measure (Tables 169-170); 'at any dose' corrected; landing comparisons on matched events (Table 171); PNPLAIN, hull deviation, dose units and GPU hours added; per-direction distributions, reliability on all six tasks, signed-progress closure and alpha-4 depths (Tables 175-178).

The next budget went to new tasks rather than another predictor, as asked: 15 new gated coding units in two panels, each with its base repertoire hash-committed before the first push (guard verified). This is the right fix for the underpowered five-task panel.

Negative results are reported with their rules and not softened: the transplant claim DISCONFIRMED (1 of 5), the push toward the base never escapes, and the plan sampler comparison DISCONFIRMED (base intent beats plan noise on 3 of 5). The movability half is reported against its disconfirming bound.
Every headline I recomputed matches the artifact files exactly, including the report author's own pooled computation (work/pooled_a1a2.json), which I re-derived independently.
The literal cell of request item 1a-c (thinking on, top-k 10, same seed) was run: 0 of 20 seeds change the algorithm, and 100 of 100 traces completed.
Plan noise against decoding at matched departure (19 vs 3 discordant slots at alpha 2) answers the main objection of the nearest published neighbour (ICLR 2027 submission oag3wgNLRh) on these tasks.

The positioning is thorough and honest: 137 verbatim quotes. 'First' is struck for the transplant. The premise row is marked 'contradicting in part' (Lee et al.), and the landing half is marked as having only stylised neighbours.
Novelty is audited everywhere: 130 correct out-of-catalogue programs in iteration 5, including base and transplant output, with no novel algorithm.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration the pool holds: (1) a repaired record: the held-out movability verdict per measure, the site wording 'a prefill site at which noise is effective, not a locus', every forecast comparison on matched events, the PNPLAIN, hull, Llama, dose-unit and GPU-hour rows, best cells beside their distributions, Table 92c rows, the exposure class, the Table 76 cross-reference, and a sha256-frozen rival set (human-solution diversity, merit gap, opening margin, modal share, novelty share, ban-unit ratio). (2) The base repertoire (beta, runner-up, Hill-1) of all 15 existing tasks, committed, and the first causal test of whether tuning's narrowing is carried by the plan states: the transplant at three lambdas against read-position, early, late, matched-random and cross-task controls on fresh slots, the reverse transplant, the de-sharpening push, and plan-site geometry in activation coordinates with centroids sized by implemented count under the base model, the twin and the transplant. (3) 12-14 new gated tasks (two panels) with committed base forecasts and escape populations, plus the 15 old tasks on one ban-free unit and up to 10 disguised variants, enough for the pooled A1 and A2 confirmation that the next round's Step 0 computes mechanically from both committed halves. (4) Plan noise priced against IFG, PlanSearch-lite, enumerate-and-pick, base-intent and departure-matched decoding on the full-simplex hull, and the literal thinking-on, top-k 10, same-seed temperature cell. (5) The gemma-3-4b pt/it replication on re-gated labels. (6) Table 92d with verified quotes and saturation flags. (7) A novelty count that now includes base and transplanted output. NEXT ITERATION: if A1, A2 and B hold, the paper leads with 'tuning narrowed a choice the base model makes evenly; the narrowing lives in the plan states; nudges and transplants reopen exactly the base alternatives, and nothing reaches beyond them', and the next round extends it to tuning stages (base, SFT, preference and RL checkpoints of an open family) and to a larger model. If B fails its controls, the narrowing is located downstream of the plan and the next round localises it by block band. If A1 fails, the report says tuning removed the alternatives from the plan, and the task-level account is closed.
strategies.objective: Test the NARROWED-REPERTOIRE account of where an LLM's algorithm choice comes from and how to influence it. (A) Across 12-14 new tasks built and gated this round, the base model's correct-only repertoire, committed before any instruct push, predicts which tasks a plan nudge moves (A1) and where it lands (A2), ahead of rivals including human-solution diversity, the merit gap and the novelty instruction. (B) Transplanting Qwen3-8B-Base's task-specification states into Qwen3-8B's prefill reopens the base alternatives on base-diverse tasks beyond matched-random and cross-task controls, does nothing at the read position or on base-collapsed tasks, and the reverse transplant narrows the base model. (C) Price plan noise head-on against text-level plan samplers and departure-matched decoding. Also: the request's literal 1a-c cell, a second-family replication, the novelty count, and a record cleared of every contradiction the blocking review found.
strategies.rationale: WHY DEEPEN, AND WHAT THE OBJECT IS. After four iterations one effect stands: a random nudge to the task-specification states changes which correct algorithm Qwen3-8B writes where temperature changes only the wording (17.25 of 20 seeds against 0 on the shortest path task), but only on 5 of 15 tasks. The move is `deepen`, so the object is that result, and every slot attacks it from a different side. THE SIDEWAYS SHIFT, STATED. Iteration 4's direction-level question (which property of a direction makes it move the algorithm) is closed: the plan subspace failed (rho 0.03) and the signed-progress lead rests mostly on one task. The review asks for the budget to go to more tasks rather than another predictor on the same five. The strategy therefore moves, within the request's own question ('how does creativity manifest, and can we influence it'), from a property of directions to a property of TASKS, and from correlation to a causal test: the base model's repertoire (does it write more than one algorithm?) as the predictor of where a nudge works, and the base model's plan states as the cause. Evidence already points there: on both path tasks every push landing and every ban landing (DFS; Bellman-Ford/SPFA) is exactly the base model's runner-up, and the base model is far less collapsed (Hill_cc 1.58 and 2.09 against 1.00 and 1.16). HOW THE SEVEN SLOTS MAP. FIX: the CPU evaluation clears every blocking review item from rows on disk and freezes the rival task predictors. MECHANISM (causal): the repertoire-and-transplant artifact runs the never-run base-to-instruct plan transplant with read-position, early-block, late-block, matched-random and cross-task controls, a de-sharpening push, and the reverse transplant. MORE POWER and a CLEANER MEASURE, as a held-out confirmation: two parallel panel artifacts each build and gate half of the new tasks from disjoint pre-registered lists, commit every unit's base-repertoire forecast before the first instruct push, and put every unit (the 15 old tasks re-measured too) on one ban-free dose unit. Two panels, not one, because building gated tasks is the bottleneck and A1's power is the number of tasks; panel B also carries disguised variants, a within-task test of the task-affordance confound. CONFOUND, head-on: the knob artifact runs the strongest competitors plan noise has never met (IFG, PlanSearch-lite, enumerate-and-pick, a base-written intent, decoding matched to plan noise's own departure), plus the request's literal 1a-c cell, never dropped. REPLICATION: gemma-3-4b pt/it with a style re-gate, a pt repertoire committed before a fresh it push population, and a pt-to-it transplant. POSITIONING: a dated saturation search on base-versus-aligned diversity, base-aligned collaboration, base-to-instruct transplants and reversibility of sharpening, before any novelty statement. REVIEWER MAP. Must-fix 1 (held-out verdict per measure), 2 (site wording), 3 (landings on matched events), 4 (missing executed results) and 5 (distributions, not best cells; budget on more tasks): the evaluation, with item 5's steer carried by the panels. Minor items (Table 92c rows, exposure class, the Table 76 cross-reference): the evaluation, plus the literal cell in the knob artifact. BUDGET. About 10.75 GPU-hours (repertoire and transplant about 2.5, panel A about 2.5 with the re-measurement, panel B about 2, knobs about 2.25, Gemma about 1.5), sized from iteration-4 throughput (10,100 programs in 2.53 GPU-hours on the FP8 engine; bf16 on an A4500 is expected to be slower, which the staged extrapolation absorbs). OpenRouter at most about USD 10.5 of the shared USD 20 (judges and audits only: evaluation 1, transplant 1.5, panels 2 each, knobs 1, Gemma 1.5, research a few cents).
strategies.title: Do nudges reopen what tuning narrowed?

STAGE A (method: full-state exchange of the full ban's residual states into the token-length-matched neutral twin; baselines: twin, matched-norm random exchange MR, placebo twin, identity and KV-splice tests). The ban is carried by the task-specification states at blocks 12-23 on prompt-route tasks: T2 Dijkstra->Bellman-Ford/SPFA transfer 0.80 (24:0, Holm p 7e-7), condition-span KV splice 0.00, read position 0.00. All 70 W4 ('X is not allowed here') programs use the banned default. The T2 semantic seed barely moves Dijkstra. INSTRUMENT (results/layer_convention.json, gate.json): the extraction convention is hidden_states[21], the output of block 20 (FVE_ref 0.695 vs 0.580 for [20]). The reference set reproduces the released 0.752 within 0.06; FineWeb and chat score 0.78-0.79. Code text is out of distribution (LeetCode 0.45, HumanEval+ 0.39). The task-state gate is FVE_ref 0.512, PARTIAL. READOUT (results/readout.json; blind judges Gemini-2.5-flash-lite + Mistral-small-3.2, DeepSeek resolver, kappa 0.82 on explanations): at end-of-prompt positions (SPEC-3..READ) the NLA never names the planned algorithm. N1 ban->Y* is 0/16 (only T05 eligible; fallback F4). N2 twin->default is 0/112 vs text-only 0/112. N8b (ban-failure default) is 0/96. The N3 positive control is 0.00 on all 7 tasks vs text-only 1.00; explanations mention the prompt's own algorithm name in 0.7% of cases. They describe the format line and confabulate the task. At generated tokens the NLA sometimes names the realised algorithm before the text does (up to 0.28), but the outside-reader PREDICT baseline beats it per sample (0.25 vs 0.07, McNemar 20:88, p=2e-11). EXPLORATORY local control (results/local_control.json): read AT the algorithm-name token, explanations mention it 80% (forced) and 89% (ban) of the time, and they respect the ban's negation (planned 0.48 vs 0.06). Identity fades within one sentence (27%/6%), so the null means 'not carried in verbalisable form at pre-code positions', not 'NLA blind'. CAUSAL (results/causal.json): the pre-registered difference-of-reconstructions edit at 4 prefill positions, x1/x2/x4, N=30 CRN pairs, FAILS on all 4 tasks (T10 union-find, T05 brute force, T06 Floyd, T04 KMP; T2/T1/T03 had no admissible Y). Edits are tiny (||delta||/||h|| 0.04) and the prefill site is inert even at x16. EXPLORATORY steering at READ + generated tokens 1-64 (results/causal_exploratory_followup.json): the NLA edit x8 moves T06 to Floyd 0.76 vs C0 0.28 (25:1 over 50 CRN pairs; fresh-slot replication 13:0). It beats matched random 28:1, an unrelated-word edit 12:1 and a norm-matched round trip 13:1. T05 brute force 10:0 at x8 and 23:0 at x16; T10 moves only with difference-in-means (15:1); T04 does not move. Prompting (forced adherence 0.90-1.00) remains the ceiling. Novelty audit: 10 correct 'other' programs, 0 novel. Every headline number is re-derived by audit/rederive.py (stdlib) and audit/rederive_headlines.py; placebos fail. FILES: method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out; datasets nla_behaviour 1,646, nla_readout_states 1,900 with predict_nla vs predict_text_only_name vs predict_outside_reader, nla_causal 2,314, nla_causal_exploratory 1,960, nla_local_control_exploratory 660; all analyses in metadata). Also data/explanations.jsonl (6,180 explanations), data/judgements.jsonl, figures F0-F9 (F6/F8 activation geometry). cache/*.npz (layer-20 states, recon, deltas) stay on the run volume. Caveats: one model and layer, one AV checkpoint, code is out of distribution for the NLA, and the steering results are exploratory.

artifacts.layman_summary: Checks each new claim of this run about a hidden 'plan' inside a code-writing AI model against published papers, and says which ideas are already taken and which remain open.

artifacts.summary: Dated (2026-10-22) positioning audit for the iteration-6 claims P1-P5, N, S and E. It provides paste-ready Table 92e in research_report.md: 8 claim blocks plus CTRL rows. It has 123 new verbatim, versioned quotes from 94 sources, all 123/123 matched against cached source text and 123/123 re-matched by an independent live fetch_grep pass. Statuses: 82 VERIFIED, 22 VERIFIED-ABSTRACT, 4 VERIFIED-BLOG, 15 VERIFIED-README. It cites Tables 92b/92c (art_kjrCpQnPaniY) and 92d (art_ObxQOIlAM9MS) by row id without re-verifying them. Saturation search: protocol frozen and sha256-stamped before the first call; 21 strings over 7 lanes on arXiv API, Semantic Scholar, the OpenReview ICLR 2027 pool, OpenAlex/Crossref and grey literature; 6 round-2 strings; snowballing; a round 3 that met the stop rule; 126 logged calls (incl. 3 supplementary full-text checks). 2,191 raw hits gave 1,820 unique records, 1,401 in the window and 67 papers scored on the O/I/C rubric (75 claim-rows: 3 occupy, 66 adjacent, 6 irrelevant). FLAGS: A (DAS localization of algorithm choice in code, validated by generation) NOT FIRED, narrowly. CDAS (ICLR 2026) does DAS steering validated by generation, but on refusal and a CoT backdoor. Algorithm choice in code is moved only by prompt cues (92c Invisible Lottery). Code attributes that are not the algorithm (language, library, coding habits) are moved by patching or difference-in-means vectors. The nearest same-model, same-site neighbour is the ICLR 2027 submission 'Before Reasoning Begins' (Qwen3-8B final-prompt SAE targets, code benchmarks, random nulls). B (activation quantization changes perturbation effects) PARTLY FIRED. Steering under quantization has been measured only with weight-only INT8/NF4 (2609.06473: activations stay FP16/BF16). Two ICLR 2027 submissions show effect changes across precision with aligned directions, but their abstracts do not say whether activations are quantized (PDFs 403). FP8 W8A8 appears only in a non-determinism study. No source found measures the effect size of random perturbations under activation rounding. C (editing verbaliser explanations to steer) FIRED. The NLA paper (Transformer Circuits, 7 May 2026; cite as Fraser-Taliente, Kantamneni, Ong et al.) edits a rhyme-plan explanation, reconstructs it with the AR and steers at the newline only (~50% success). LatentQA, SelfIE and Dreaming Vectors are kin. N is therefore a replication in a new setting. Cautions: about 2% claim-dependence of the AR (2607.20379), no newline plan in small open models (2609.18440), and published readout controls (ICLR 2027 'Auditing the Auditor'). D (resampling a fitted causal plan variable for diversity) PARTLY FIRED. Activation noise and latent-code sampling are occupied; the closest fitted-direction work is the ICLR 2027 'Random Choice in LMs'. Lane verdicts: P1 PARTLY OCCUPIED (method); P2, P3 and P4 ADJACENT-ONLY; P5 PARTLY OCCUPIED; N OCCUPIED (method); S PARTLY OCCUPIED (SAE-Steering, ACL 2026, beats prompt and activation baselines on reasoning strategies); E ADJACENT-ONLY in the published record but PARTLY OCCUPIED by contemporaneous submissions. Corrections: there is no official NLA for Qwen3-8B, but community NLAs exist at L24 (nanoNLA, EasyNLA); circuit-tracer has Qwen-3 PLTs including 8B (Hanna et al.), so justify Gemma for S; Gemma Scope 2 dates from 22 Dec 2025, with IT SAEs finetuned from PT; Sutter's 'any network to any algorithm' phrase is not in v2; Engels' v3 title. The report also gives permitted and forbidden wording per claim and reviewer baselines. Evidence files are in evidence/.

hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: Iteration 7 answers how the algorithm choice manifests inside Qwen3-8B (a DAS-fitted plan in the task states, the fork token it tilts, and why temperature acts only there), places the top-five ban causally, prices the activation knob, traces a circuit at Gemma's fork, and tests evaluator-guided search for novel algorithms.

direction_options.case_against: DAS is method-occupied and prone to illusions (Sutter, Makelov); iteration 4's prompt subspace failed to mediate (rho 0.03, removal kept effects); Gemma's DAS broke programs; the same run was lost at planning once. Three slots on one account leave fewer for novelty and circuits.
direction_options.case_for: Central question of the request. The engine control made the 40-direction bf16 escapes a stable target (rho 0.96) and Stage A gave full-state ceilings (SP 21/30, forced 30/30), so DAS and mediation are decisive now. The lost DAS run is untested, not refuted; review score rose 4 to 5 as this line got cleaner.
direction_options.target: Plan-and-fork account in Qwen3-8B: DAS at task states (multi-Y, Sutter controls), fork-margin and plan-axis mediation of the 40 bf16 directions, natural forks and temperature

direction_options.case_against: Memorised LeetCode tasks may leave no room for novel correct algorithms; judges over-call novelty and hybrids read as variants; search is engineering rather than interpretability and adds little to how creativity manifests inside.
direction_options.case_for: The request's layman headline; 0 novel after >25k correct programs and six iterations, and the documented route (search with an evaluator) was never tried. Either a confirmed novel program or a clean 'even search stays inside known algorithms' answers it, with 3 iterations left to deepen.
direction_options.target: Truly novel solutions: evaluator-guided search (FunSearch/MAP-Elites) with hidden tests and a novelty critic against 18,237 known solutions

direction_options.target: Circuits: attribution graph at Gemma's one-token fork with Gemma Scope 2 transcoders, plus DAS with random-init and shuffled-target controls and a valid-program dose

direction_options.case_against: Activation noise for diversity is an occupied lane; even if plan noise wins it is a random knob, and prompting stays the ceiling (forced adherence 0.90-1.00).
direction_options.case_for: Iteration 5's knob verdict (base intent beats plan noise) used a design where plan noise is nearly inert; at the absolute unit plan noise moves CC 25/50 in bf16. About 2.5 GPU hours re-decides the 'influence' answer and tests whether pushes act where bans write.

direction_options.case_against: It produces no new evidence on the request; one slot of seven.

direction_options.case_against: The main design already discriminates these (claims C, F, P1, P2, T); a separate screen would duplicate it at the cost of the novelty and circuit slots.
direction_options.case_for: Guards against tunnel vision after six rounds on one model.
direction_options.target: Screen of mechanism candidates for where the choice lives: categorical plan, 1-D margin plus ladder, fork token, distributed code, head routing, generic sensitivity

hypothesis_update.direction_plan: 7 slots. Main deepen 3: Q1 DAS plan with Sutter controls, routing, causal manifold (how it manifests, mean-answer subspace, manifold); Q2 fork-margin and plan-axis mediation of the 40 bf16 directions plus the in-manifold top-five push (influence, top-5); Q3 Qwen3 natural forks and temperature vs margin (question 1, BFS/DFS internals). Secondary 4: K plan-noise 2x2 and prices (influence); N evaluator search (novelty); G Gemma fork circuit and DAS controls (circuits); E0 CPU record repair (review).
key_changes: Main object widened from a prefill plan variable to the PLAN-AND-FORK account: a low-rank plan in the task-specification states sets the margin at one early fork token, where the program commits.

Engine claim closed: bf16 escapes on iteration 4's 40 directions (CC 0.65 vs 0.725, SP 0.15 vs 0.20; per-direction Spearman 0.96/0.87) and plan noise reproduces (25 vs 30 of 50), so the push target is a model property; activation rounding adds nothing.

Stage A carried as evidence with both metrics (attempted / correct Y): shortest path 24/21 of 30, forced Bellman-Ford exchange 30/30, read position 0 on six tasks; the committed localization rule is recorded as NOT SUPPORTED (two sum's task states carry 0.43).
New primary claim F: the teacher-forced fork margin mediates the 40 bf16 directions' effects and every other knob cell (Spearman >= 0.5 per task, 0.6 pooled).

P1 rebuilt with multi-algorithm sources so permuted-label DAS is informative, Sutter random-initialisation and dormant-subspace controls, held-out templates, and correct-Y as the primary generation outcome.
New claim C distinguishes a categorical plan (exchange routes the source's own Y) from a margin-and-ladder plan (every push lands on the runner-up); both branches are reportable.
P2 now uses the signed default-to-runner-up axis, fitted inside its own artifact, confirmed on 24 fresh kth-smallest directions.

New claim T answers question 1 mechanistically: temperature acts only through the fork margin, so it should change ideas on undecided units (MST, trapped rain water, valid anagram, Gemma grid) between T 0.3 and 1.0, and never on collapsed tasks.
Top-five prohibition re-posed at in-manifold doses (fractions of the banned-to-survivor centroid distance) and placed in causally fitted coordinates (claim M), answering the reviewer's dose critique.

Covers the request's open parts: circuits via an attribution graph at Gemma's one-token fork (G), and 'truly novel solutions' via evaluator-guided search with a novelty critic (N), never tried in six iterations.
K tests the unit-profile vs direction-seed 2x2 behind iteration 5's bf16 plan-noise null, then prices plan noise at the design that moves against base intent and enumerate-and-pick.

Step 0 answers every review item: Stage A metric, post-hoc site wording and CC discordance, Gemma DAS/SAE restatements, per-model synthesis, five [FIGURE] markers, top-five dose caveat, Table 238 correct-only, NLA clustered interval, unreported checks, Section 4.9 wrap, fork positioning row.

Newly closed: activation rounding and the FP8 engine, the noise-site grid, state-vs-token at matched KL, the layer-20 NLA as a pre-code readout, SAE features over difference in means, the read position.
Confidence increased modestly: the internal handle survived the engine control and Stage A localized instruction-driven choices, while the low-rank and mediation parts remain untested.
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: Engine control made the bf16 push target stable and Stage A gave exchange ceilings, so DAS and mediation now decide the central question; the lost DAS run is untested, not refuted.

Plan resampling (a DAS coordinate drawn per generation) as a diversity knob.
Plan extrapolation beyond catalogue values as a route to off-catalogue programs.
Top-five prohibition in a less-collapsed model (Llama-3.1-8B grid) where survivors could appear.
NLA edits at the generated-token site as a steering source on more tasks (exploratory lead, 2 of 4).
Plan noise as the mutation operator inside an evaluator-guided search loop.
