critiques.description: Stage A's outcome is misdescribed. Section 6.4.1 says 'The outcome is the share of correct programs implementing the substitute Y', but the preregistered metric (art_rMlbrjVB1c__ predictions/commit0.json: transfer = share(label == Y | cell) - share(label == Y | TWIN), 'all samples') and every Y share/transfer in Tables 244-250 count all attempted programs; correctness enters only through the pass-ratio clause. Recomputed from data/labels.jsonl: shortest path exchange at blocks 0-35 is 24/30 Bellman-Ford/SPFA attempts but 21/30 correct programs (0.70, not 0.80); blocks 12-23 is 18/30 attempts but 11/30 correct (0.37, not 0.60); kth smallest blocks 0-35 is 17 quickselect attempts, 16 correct; on the grid task the exchange at blocks 0-35 'transfers 0.47 toward DFS' with only 3/30 correct DFS programs and the condition-span splice '0.33' with 7/30. The 0.80 and 0.57 figures are carried into 6.9, 6.10 item 2 and the closing as if they were correct-program transfers; the paper step will publish a wrong metric definition.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite the definition to match commit0 ('share of all attempted programs labelled Y; invalid rows count as not-Y; correctness gated by pass ratio >= 0.8'), add a correct-Y column to Tables 244-250 (e.g. T2 blocks 0-35 21/30, blocks 12-23 11/30; T03 blocks 0-35 16/30; grid blocks 0-35 3/30, condition splice 7/30; forced Bellman-Ford exchange 30/30), and quote both numbers wherever 0.80/0.57/0.47/0.33 appear. Expected impact: +0.25 soundness.

critiques.description: The post-hoc site result is overstated. 6.4.2 ends 'withdrawn as preregistered, and its post-hoc form survives in bf16', and the closing lists 'the post-hoc ordering of noise sites' among bf16-robust internal results. The artifact's committed verdict (art_rMlbrjVB1c__ results/site_grid.json RULE) is 'WITHDRAWN as FP8-specific: the site of the choice is open', and the rule required BOTH the read-position and the condition-span coefficient below the task-spec site with intervals excluding 0. In the post-hoc alpha<=4 model only the read-position clause holds; the condition-span clause fails on both tasks (S2 -1.70, bootstrap [-3.96, 0.42] on kth smallest; -0.56, [-4.93, 2.91] on connected components). On connected components the early blocks beat the plan site (S4 +2.51 [1.39, 3.80]; paired flips 4:18; MH odds ratio plan site vs read position 0.82 [0.31, 2.18]), the artifact's ST x Stage A concordance check is false and unreported (noise acts at blocks 0-11, the exchange at 12-23), and the exchange at blocks 0-11 and 24-35 alone already moves 0.87 and 0.63 of attempts off union find. The rule's own label 'FP8-specific' is never discussed although the engine control contradicts it.
critiques.suggested_action: Replace 'its post-hoc form survives' with: 'post hoc (alpha<=4) the read position is below the task-spec site on both tasks; the condition-span clause fails post hoc as well, so the site of the choice remains open, as the artifact concludes'. Report the rule's 'FP8-specific' label and say why Section 6.3 makes it inapplicable. Add the ST x Stage A concordance (kth smallest concordant at blocks 12-23; connected components discordant) and the depth-redundant removal on connected components. Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description: Two Gemma claims outrun their controls. (a) 'The plan is close to one direction at one position' (6.5) and 'DAS finds it in essentially one direction' (closing) rest on a rank-1 DAS trained with forced-BFS prompts as sources. The shuffled-source control is uninformative by construction (deviation D9: it still imports a BFS state and moves y by 10.1 nats); no DAS was fitted on a randomly initialised model or with shuffled targets, which the run's own positioning audit (art_OUuQUYQn5voE permitted wording; Table 277 rows 14-15) makes a precondition for a DAS localization claim; and in generation the rank-4 interchange gives 50/50 BFS with 0/50 passing, an off-distribution intervention of the kind [122] warns about. Shifting a log-odds whose natural SD is 0.67 nats by 8.8 nats is not evidence of one-dimensionality. (b) The preregistered SAE readout margin (Lasso R2 0.66 vs text 0.18) did not reproduce under the artifact's own second estimator: standardized ridge on the same layer-29 SAE codes gives 0.15 against 0.086 for a template+noun-norm control (delta 0.064, below the 0.10 bar; results/rederive_headlines.json H1). The report quotes only the unstandardized '<=0.09' and keeps the Lasso result as 6.10 Established item 3. (c) 'Every edit at the fork lowered the pass rate' is contradicted by Table 262's own SAE top-5 row (pass 0.84, equal to the twin).
critiques.suggested_action: Restate (a) as 'a rank-1 DAS subspace fitted on forced-BFS sources moves the held-out fork log-odds by 8.8 nats (random subspaces about 0); without random-initialisation and target-shuffled controls, and with 0/50 valid programs under interchange, this does not show that the choice is one-dimensional'. If budget allows, fit DAS on a randomly initialised Gemma and with shuffled targets, and sweep the interchange scale to find a dose that keeps programs valid. Report (b) beside the Lasso result in 6.5 and 6.10 item 3, and fix (c). Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description: The closing and 6.9 merge three different quantities into one 'location of the choice' and assert an untested result. 'Where the choice is held has now been measured in three models' compares where an external instruction's effect is carried in Qwen3-8B (full-state exchange from another prompt; Qwen3-8B has no natural split on these tasks), where a natural within-prompt choice forks during generation in Gemma, and what a verbalizer says in Qwen2.5. 'In all three models the read position is inert as a carrier ... Gemma's readout there is no better than the text' is wrong for Gemma: its 'SPEC' site is the mean over task-spec positions (art_zNyBP6zieI5u src/cfg.py: from 'Task:' to the last user token), not the read position, which was never read or edited. The Gemma result is that task-spec edits and readouts do not reach the choice, the opposite of Qwen3-8B's task-spec states carrying a ban.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite the synthesis per model and per quantity: Qwen3-8B - task-spec states carry an external ban/instruction on prompt-route tasks; Gemma - the natural choice forks at a generated token and task-spec edits/readouts do not reach it; Qwen2.5 - no verbalisable plan at pre-code positions. Drop Gemma from the read-position sentence or test the read position in Gemma. Expected impact: +0.25.

critiques.description: Coverage of the original request is still partial on its central question, how creativity manifests inside the model. In the main model the record shows where a ban or instruction is carried, not how Qwen3-8B represents its own algorithm choice: the DAS/plan-subspace/causal-manifold experiment (experiment_iter6_dir4) was lost at planning (correctly recorded as not run). The request also demands 'actual geometry plots, actual activation space'. Iteration 6 produced them - art_rMlbrjVB1c__ figures/F5_top5_geometry, art_zNyBP6zieI5u figures/geometry_raw_L17/L22 and geometry_sae_L17/L22 (centroids with implemented counts and the top-five prompt states), art_dbUtqBjT0tPf figures/F6_geometry and F8_mds_centroids - but none has a [FIGURE] marker; 6.4.4, 6.5 (Table 266) and 6.6 describe them only in prose or tables, so the paper step will not know they exist.
critiques.suggested_action: Next iteration, run the lost experiment: DAS at the task-spec positions of shortest path and kth smallest with the Stage A full-state exchange as ceiling, held-out templates, declared map class and random-init/shuffled-label controls, then project iteration 4's 40 directions (now known to escape in bf16 at the absolute unit) onto the fitted subspace and draw the algorithm manifold and the top-five prohibition in it. Now: add [FIGURE] markers for the five geometry figures listed, each captioned with its position (task-spec mean vs read position) and any label-dependence caveat. Expected impact: +0.5 on coverage and contribution.

critiques.description: The bf16 top-five plan push (6.4.4) was tested only at doses far beyond the forced-prompt manifold, so 'the activation version of the prohibition breaks programs before it moves the algorithm' (6.9) is confounded with dose. In art_rMlbrjVB1c__ results/top5_push.json the ten centroids span about 0.24 on PC1 (-0.098 to 0.144) while the alpha-1 push already moves the state from about +0.09 to -0.44, over twice that spread; the pass rate falls 0.92 to 0.67 at alpha 1. Iteration 4's targeted push on connected components crossed to DFS at 0.15 ban units (half the centroid distance), so an in-manifold dose is the informative one.
critiques.suggested_action: Parameterise the top-five push by the fraction s of the banned-to-survivor centroid distance (s = 0.25, 0.5, 1) as the targeted pushes were, and until then restate 6.9 as 'at doses of 1 to 8 ban units, which overshoot the forced-prompt manifold, the push breaks programs before it moves the algorithm'.

critiques.description: The engine-control plan-noise comparison (Table 238) is given only as valid attempts off the default, while the iteration-5 null it explains and the audit's own reconciliation (Table 228) use correct programs. On correct programs (art_lpQalcAXMGr1 data/samples.jsonl) shortest path alpha 2 is 14 of 37 correct under W8A8 against 9 of 31 under bf16 (alpha 1: 9/43 vs 5/43), so 'reproduces' holds against iteration 5's 2/47 but the 22 = 22 equality is partly a definitional artefact. The T2 screen-level verdict in results/verdict.json is MIXED (W8A8 passes the screen on 15 of 40 directions vs 8-9 for the others) and is not mentioned.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a correct-only column to Table 238 and report the T2 screen-level verdict beside the literal one.

critiques.description: The NLA per-sample comparison is pseudoreplicated. 'An outside reader ... predicts the realised algorithm better, per sample (0.25 against 0.07; exact McNemar 20:88, p 2e-11)' treats 364 units drawn from 120 samples as independent; the artifact's own cluster bootstrap (art_dbUtqBjT0tPf results/readout.json N6, 5 clusters) gives an effect interval of [-0.35, 0.02], which includes 0.
critiques.suggested_action: Report the clustered interval beside the McNemar p, or test at the sample level (one unit per sample).

critiques.description: Executed checks and drops are missing from the record. Gemma: the sampler-calibration unit test U6 failed - continuations from the empty prefix give BFS 0.38 (n 192) against the natural 0.305 [0.245, 0.372] (results/fork.json) - although the fork analysis rests on resampled continuations; deviation D12 (T04/R6 forks and cross-prompt readouts, U4/U5 not run) is not mentioned. Engine control: 3 correct programs labelled other (one reused, one W16A8, one bf16) were classed only by nearest-known-solution Jaccard and never judged. Exchange experiment: the ST x Stage A concordance result.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short 'executed but not yet reported' paragraph to 6.9 listing these with their numbers and files.

critiques.description: Section 4.9 (iteration 4) carries an iteration-6 insertion that is not wrapped as a marked correction, and its claim that 'every correct program outside the catalogue that the run produced has been read by two blind judges and the executor' is contradicted by Table 278 (engine control: 'not judged') and by iteration 3's note that about 9,000 programs of the forking-token experiment were not audited.
critiques.suggested_action: Wrap the text as '(Correction, iteration 6: ...)' and restrict the claim to the pools actually audited.

critiques.description: The Gemma one-token fork is a positive result without a stated nearest-neighbour comparison. Forking-token analyses ([30], [31]) already locate outcome-deciding single tokens, and latent planning in Gemma/Qwen models is reported by Hanna et al. [123] and Nainani et al. (Table 277 rows 11, 33, 56), but the record does not say what the fork adds beyond them (an algorithm-level fork in code at a non-identifying token about 138 tokens before identifying code, readable across prompts).
critiques.suggested_action: Add a positioning row for the fork claim stating the nearest neighbour and what this run adds.

critiques.description: Two iteration-5 verdicts that bear on 'can we influence it' - plan sampler comparison DISCONFIRMED and the movability half - are now known to rest on a design (ban-free unit, its direction seeds) in which plan noise is nearly inert, while at the absolute unit plan noise moves connected components 25 of 50 in bf16. The record tags them as conditional but leaves the deciding comparison (unit profile vs seeds) untested.
critiques.suggested_action: Run a 2 x 2 (ban-free vs absolute unit x iteration-4 vs iteration-5 direction seeds) on connected components and shortest path, then repeat the plan-sampler price comparison at whichever design moves the model, about 1 GPU hour.

dimension_scores.justification: Headline numbers recompute exactly and the main conclusions (escapes are a model property; ban/instruction effects are carried by task-spec states on prompt-route tasks; Gemma's choice forks at one generated token; the NLA does not verbalise a pre-code plan; no novel algorithm) follow from the data. Several iteration-6 sentences overreach: the Stage A metric is misdescribed (attempts reported as correct programs), the post-hoc site model is said to 'survive' although it fails the condition-span clause, the Gemma DAS 'one direction' claim lacks its own required controls, and the read position is called inert in Gemma where it was not tested. None reverses a headline, so not 1, but they are more than polish.

A reader can follow the record in order: each iteration opens with the review it answers, the hypothesis update and the strategy, and each table is introduced by what it settles. The length is very large, and in iteration 6 a few synthesis sentences (6.9, closing) merge quantities that the sections keep apart.

The record preserves almost everything the run did, including nulls and the lost experiment, with tables in full. A few executed outputs are missing: the iteration-6 activation-space geometry figures (no markers), the exchange experiment's ST x Stage A concordance, the Gemma sampler-calibration check (U6) and dropped sub-analyses (D12), the NLA clustered interval, the T2 screen-level engine verdict, and correct-only counts for the engine control.

review.overall_assessment: Iteration 6 answers the previous blocking review almost item for item, and the record is traceable. I recomputed the headline numbers from the artifacts' own rows: (i) engine control (art_lpQalcAXMGr1, data/samples.jsonl, with an independent implementation of the two-stage escape rule): escape fraction at alpha 2 on connected components W8A8 0.725 / W16A8 0.600 / bf16 0.650 (W8A16 27 of 40 confirmed on top-ups of 22-26 rows, so 'incomplete' is right); shortest path 0.200 / 0.125 / 0.150 / 0.150; screen passes 30/28/27/27 and 15/8/8/9; per-slot flips W8A8 vs bf16 30:10 (p 0.0022), W16A8 vs bf16 9:23 (p 0.020); per-sample plan noise 30/27/22/25 and 22/19/18/22 of 50, block-12 displacement 13.75. (ii) Stage A (art_rMlbrjVB1c__ data/labels.jsonl): every cell count of Tables 244-250 matches. (iii) movability (art_aRTQM6CQ0Dre tables/movability_units.csv): Spearman 0.146, Bonett-Wright [-0.44, 0.65], permutation p 0.32, 0.035 with count inversions' correct-only beta, runtime merit 0.713. (iv) Landing contest, Gemma fork/readout/clamp/geometry and NLA readout/local-control values match their result JSONs. The not-run DAS/plan-coordinate experiment is correctly named as planned and not run (6.1, 6.8, 6.10, closing). The previous must-fix items are addressed with marked in-place corrections: the decisive engine control ran and shows the iteration-4 escapes are a property of Qwen3-8B; the landing tally is per set (17 of 21) with the twin-minority rival (6 vs 6) and moved to descriptive; movability has its interval, power and pooled rivals; the missing outputs are added; the site comparison and top-five push were rerun in bf16; the novelty zero was re-adjudicated by two new judge families. The remaining problems are new and concern iteration 6's own internal claims, several of which say more than their artifacts: (1) Stage A's outcome is described as the share of CORRECT programs implementing Y, but the preregistered and computed metric counts all attempts; correct-only transfers are lower (shortest path blocks 0-35: 21/30, not 24/30; blocks 12-23: 11/30, not 18/30; grid blocks 0-35: 3/30 correct DFS against a quoted 0.47). (2) 6.4.2 says the post-hoc site model 'survives', but the post-hoc alpha<=4 model fails the rule's condition-span clause on both tasks, the artifact's own verdict is 'WITHDRAWN ... the site of the choice is open', and on connected components the early blocks beat the plan site. (3) The Gemma 'one direction' DAS claim lacks the random-initialisation and label-shuffled controls that the run's own positioning audit makes a condition for that wording, the interchange leaves 0/50 programs passing, and the SAE-beyond-text readout margin did not reproduce under the artifact's own second estimator. (4) The closing synthesises 'where the choice is held' across three models from three different quantities and asserts that the read position is inert in Gemma, where the read position was never read or edited. Coverage of the request stays partial: the representation-level account in the main model was lost with the DAS experiment, and the iteration-6 activation-space geometry figures have no figure markers although the request demands actual activation-space plots. Research quality: technically careful, exceptionally reproducible and honest about nulls; the new internal positives (engine robustness, a ban/instruction carried by task-spec states, a one-token fork in Gemma, an NLA null) are modest and partly overstated, and the central internal question remains open. Score 5.
strengths: The previous blocking review is answered item by item (Table 224) with in-place, marked corrections (Table 226: 36 corrections, 78 MATCH / 1 CORRECTED / 18 NEW / 2 CARRIED), and the earlier sections keep their chronology.

The engine control is the right decisive experiment and is well executed: four numerics built from one bf16 snapshot, iteration-4 directions, slots and uniforms held fixed, the W8A8 engine reproducing iteration-4 rows byte for byte (400/400, 40/40), each engine scored against its own twin. Every headline cell recomputes exactly from data/samples.jsonl.

Traceability is strong: each table names its artifact and file, and my independent recomputations of the escape fractions, per-slot flips, plan-noise counts, Stage A cell counts and the movability Spearman/Bonett-Wright interval all matched.

The record now states what survives the engine change (Table 229 with a status-after-6.3 column; closing list of bf16-robust internal results) and tags iteration-4/5 verdicts as conditional on their design.

Stage A has good controls (matched-norm random exchange, placebo twin, read-position exchange, condition-span splice) and an informative extension: forced positive instructions are carried by the same task-spec states (shortest path 30/30, connected components 28/30).

Dead ends and nulls are kept with their evidence (activation-rounding account, preregistered Stage A rule, feature claim, verbal readout, state-noise vs temperature), and the lost DAS experiment is recorded as planned and not run, never as a null.

The Gemma natural BFS/DFS split is a clean within-prompt contrast the request asked for, and the NLA exploratory local control turns a null readout into an interpretable one (the algorithm is verbalisable at its name token and fades within a sentence).

The novelty question is handled conservatively: the 14 disputed programs were stress-tested and re-adjudicated blind by two new judge families with controls, and the closing scopes the novelty null to single-sample generation without search.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this round the pool holds: (1) a repaired record (engine label table, per-set landing tally with the twin-minority rival and support counts, movability with its interval and power, the missing tables, the second novelty adjudication); (2) the engine verdict on iteration 4's noise positives (activation rounding, weights, or not reproduced) on 40 directions x four engines plus a noise mimic, with a relabel table; (3) the bf16 site comparison at matched downstream displacement, the top-five push, state against token noise at matched KL, Stage A band exchange on eight tasks against frozen route-class predictions, and the three-way landing forecast with the instruct opening ranking; (4) the DAS plan variable on 2-4 tasks with random, shuffled, read-position, null-source and reverse controls, its mediation of random pushes, its interpolation, its temperature profile, plan resampling and the causal algorithm manifold with the top-five ban placed on it in actual activation coordinates; (5) the Gemma Scope 2 readout of Gemma's natural BFS/DFS split with the fork, feature steering against difference in means, and a transcoder attribution graph at the fork; (6) the NLA readout and edit-and-reconstruct test on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; (7) Table 92e with verified quotes and saturation flags. NEXT ROUND: if P1 and P2 hold, iteration 7 confirms the plan variable on held-out tasks and a second family (Gemma DAS, or the Gemma-3-12B-IT NLA at layer 32), uses its value space for P3-style extrapolation and novelty search, and writes the internal account as the paper's lead; if P1 fails, the next round reports the minimal rank and layer set and moves the locus question to generated tokens; if E finds activation rounding, the paper's caution about quantised engines becomes a contribution in its own right.
strategies.objective: Give the request's central question, how the choice of idea manifests inside the model, a mechanistic and engine-robust answer. Test the PLAN-VARIABLE account in bf16 Qwen3-8B: the algorithm a model will write is carried before the first code token by a low-rank causal variable in the task-specification states, which (P1) an interchange of a rank-k subspace (k <= 16) transfers between prompts with correct code, on held-out templates and an untrained source type; (P2) mediates which random pushes change the algorithm; (P3) takes discrete values; (P4) does not vary with temperature; and (P5) can be resampled as a diversity knob. Read the same choice in words (NLA on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and in features and circuits (Gemma Scope 2 SAEs and transcoders on gemma-3-4b-it's natural BFS-against-DFS split). Decide with a four-engine control whether iteration 4's noise positives are a property of the model or of FP8 W8A8 rounding, rerun the site comparison and the top-five push in bf16, score who forecasts the landing, and repair the record.
strategies.rationale: WHY THIS DIRECTION. After five iterations the request's central question has no internal answer: the plan subspace failed (rho 0.03), SAEs were closed, NLA was unavailable, and the one internal positive, noise at the task-specification states, is an FP8 W8A8 result that shrinks 10- to 30-fold in bf16 at near-matched dose (connected components 1/50 against 30/50; the dose ratio 0.89-1.39 cannot explain it). Pushing noise further cannot recover this; the sideways move WITHIN the question is to the sharper instrument: fit the variable to its causal effect (DAS) instead of perturbing at random, and read it with the instruments the request names and that now exist (released NLA checkpoints for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Gemma Scope 2 SAEs and transcoders trained on gemma-3-4b-it). WHY A POSITIVE IS LIKELY. The bf16 route results already show that the task-specification states carry the ban's substitute (path tasks: prompt route 0.13 banned share against 0.11 for the full ban; kth smallest and connected components: either route suffices; band patching of blocks 12-23 reproduces avoidance on both), so a causally sufficient state exists; the open question is only its rank. Token-level interventions failed and state-level ones worked, which is what a held variable predicts. And in bf16 few random directions act at about one unit while two pre-selected directions act in both engines, the signature of a readout sensitive to few directions. HOW THE SEVEN SLOTS MAP (the direction's split, with one sub-item moved for load). MAIN cover: (1) the plan variable in Qwen3-8B (DAS rank sweep with random, shuffled, read-position, null-source and reverse controls; noise mediation; interpolation; plan resampling; temperature; the causal manifold with the top-five ban placed on it); (2) Gemma Scope 2 SAEs and transcoders on Gemma's natural BFS/DFS split, with attribution at the fork; (3) NLA readout and edit-and-reconstruct on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; (4) positioning. FIX: (5) the four-engine control (must-fix 1); (6) the bf16 site rerun with the top-five push and state-against-token noise (must-fix 5), plus Stage A band exchange (moved here from slot 1 to balance load) and the opening-rank landing rival (must-fix 2 extended); (7) the CPU record repair of must-fixes 1-4 and every minor item. REVIEWER MAP: must-fix 1 = slots 5 and 7; must-fix 2 = slot 7 (tally, twin-minority rival, support counts) and slot 6 (opening-rank rival); must-fix 3 = slot 7; must-fix 4 = slot 7; must-fix 5 = slots 1, 2, 3 and 6; the minor items = slot 7 (with the second blind adjudication of the 14 over-called programs). WHAT EACH OUTCOME BUYS. A positive P1 with P2 gives the paper its lead: the idea is a small variable fixed before the code, temperature acts on the words after it, and the variable explains which pushes worked; a negative gives the minimal rank and the set of layers the choice needs. Either way claim E tells the field that FP8 W8A8 can multiply the apparent effect of activation perturbations, or clears the engine. BUDGET. About 15.5 GPU-hours on the planned 20 GB Ampere pods (E about 4, site about 2.5, plan variable about 3.5, Gemma about 2.5, NLA about 3), sized from iteration-5 bf16 throughput (14,600 programs in 1.74 GPU-hours on an RTX 4090, expected about half that rate on an A4500); OpenRouter at most about USD 7 of the shared USD 20 (evaluation 1, E 0.5, site 0.75, plan 1, Gemma 1, NLA 2.5, research 0.2).

Iteration 7, claim T, on Qwen/Qwen3-8B (rev b968826d, bf16 HF, thinking off; one RTX 4090; about 0.75 GPU-h; OpenRouter USD 0.022). Verdict: PARTIAL.
(1) WHERE THE ALGORITHM IS DECIDED (Test 1, pass 3/3). Prefix resampling (8 per prefix length, Bayesian change points, 20-continuation confirmation with control positions; sampler calibration passes on all units) finds a one-token fork right after the canonical opening (|O|+1):

artifacts.summary: This artifact contains the source code (method.py) and three JSON result files (full_method_out.json, mini_method_out.json, preview_method_out.json) for iteration 7 of the "Circuit and dose dial at Gemma's BFS‑vs‑DFS fork" experiment. The Python script defines a pipeline of stages (engine checks, G1 path‑patching, G2 dose‑response sweeps, G3 temperature sweeps, novelty audit, etc.) and can be invoked for each stage via command‑line arguments. The JSON outputs record metadata (method name, model identifier, BF16 precision), status flags for each analysis component (engine_check, g3_sweep, g1_generation, g2_dose, g2_decisions, g1_extras, timing, costs) all marked as "ok", and detailed cost accounting showing a total spend of $0.0437 (≈$0.0364 on OpenRouter labeller calls across 88 API calls, plus $0.0073 for novelty and regate). They also include toy DAS training metrics such as training/held‑out KL divergences and principal‑cosine similarity values for three configurations (standard, shuffled, and a low‑learning‑rate optimiser). No further quantitative results (e.g., fork‑margin values, dose‑response curves, or temperature sweep predictions) are present in the displayed excerpts. Consequently, the artifact primarily provides the reproducible pipeline code and a verification that all planned sub‑experiments completed successfully within a modest computational budget, enabling other researchers to rerun the same stages, examine the cost breakdown, and extend the analysis with deeper result extraction if desired.

hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: Iteration 8 answers how the idea manifests inside Qwen3-8B (decision tokens, the circuit that computes their odds, where a low-rank variable exists), whether temperature at the decision token alone is the creativity knob, the literal top-five prohibition question in a model that obeys it, and whether the decision token hides correct ideas that sampling never reaches.

direction_options.case_against: Internal deepening has been the main move since iteration 4 with flat review scores (4-5), and all three primary claims of iteration 7 failed. A fork-site variable may be close to a next-token readout, and K1 could be judged predictable from the forcing results already in hand.
direction_options.case_for: Fork localisation and the temperature law gained support in two families this round. K1 tests a mechanism-derived knob that could turn the run's temperature null into a positive answer; K3 and K2 say what computes the idea and where a low-rank variable lives. Serves the central questions (how it manifests, can we influence it) and the novelty tail at once.
direction_options.target: Decision-token account in Qwen3-8B: fork-dosed temperature knob and hidden repertoire (K1, HR), fork circuit (K3), one DAS protocol at decision vs task sites in both families (K2)

direction_options.case_against: Bookkeeping: it tests no claim of the request and moves no ledger row, and it costs a slot that could test something.
direction_options.case_for: The review is blocking: nothing publishes until these are fixed. All are CPU-only re-derivations from rows on disk, so one artifact answers them with certainty and restores novelty credit for the three iteration-7 claims.
direction_options.target: Step 0 record repair: every MUST-FIX and minor review item (counting-sort relabel, per-source recovery, Gemma prefill caveat, fork-margin restatement, controls comparability, positioning)

direction_options.case_against: It may show that the dial does not beat prompting and that the subspace is dormant, weakening Gemma's strongest internal result, and it adds little coverage of the request.
direction_options.case_for: Review items 3 and 5 require executed checks, about one GPU-hour on a 4B model. It also puts the dial into free generation, which turns a teacher-forced demonstration into a knob.
direction_options.target: Gemma dial matched and checked (G): forced-BFS prompt with the prefill, free-generation dial, reverse interchange, projected retention, natural variance at every rank

direction_options.case_against: The user called temperature a minor part. Given one-token concentration the law is close to an identity, so a pass adds generality more than surprise, and Llama's grid pass rate is only 0.20.
direction_options.case_for: Turns a 2-of-4 temperature law into a held-out, three-family claim with composed forks for second decisions. It also tests the request's 'mean answer' hypothesis as post-training sharpening of the decision token. Cheap: teacher-forced passes plus same-seed sweeps.
direction_options.target: Composed-fork temperature law on held-out units in three families (Qwen3-8B, Gemma, Llama-3.1-8B) plus base-vs-instruct decision margins (L)

direction_options.case_against: No tested model may obey (Qwen3-8B, Gemma and Llama all failed). Qwen3-32B needs an 80 GB GPU, and a model switch weakens comparability with the main model's mechanism.
direction_options.case_for: The request's edge-or-opposite question has never been answerable because no model obeyed a five-name ban. A stronger open model (Qwen3-14B or 32B, or thinking on) may obey, and the landing can then be scored in actual activation geometry against a random-survivor null.
direction_options.target: The literal top-five prohibition with survivors (TP): obedience screen across open models, then survivor landing by geodesic distance in actual activation space

direction_options.case_against: The method lane is crowded (FunSearch, EoH, ReEvo, AlphaEvolve). Internal knobs need task-specific units and sources that open-ended tasks lack. It is a large new build with three iterations left and a weak link to the request's path-search framing; HR probes the tail first.
direction_options.case_for: The one setting where 'novel' can be scored without the failing judge gates: beat known baselines on held-out instances. It addresses the layman question directly, and plan noise as a mutation operator is untried.
direction_options.target: Novelty on an open-ended scored design task (bin packing or path heuristics) with internal-knob mutation operators in the search loop

direction_options.case_against: Adjacent to Beyond the 80/20 Rule (RL updates concentrate on forking tokens), and it answers only one sub-question. Folded into L as a sub-arm instead.
direction_options.case_for: Cheap (teacher-forced margins of base vs instruct at the same positions) and gives the request's 'mean answer' hypothesis a mechanism.
direction_options.target: Make 'post-training sharpens the decision token' (the mean-answer hypothesis) the main object

direction_options.case_against: This round produced real leads, not nulls, and the request's named methods are already covered. A screen spreads seven slots across shallow tests and confirms nothing within three iterations.
direction_options.case_for: Several untried candidates could reveal where creativity lives under thinking or post-training, and a cheap screen might find an unexpected positive.
direction_options.target: Screen many candidate carriers of the idea (thinking-on traces, community NLA at Qwen3-8B layer 24, pt-vs-it crosscoders, base-instruct weight interpolation, BACo) with a held-out confirmation

hypothesis_update.direction_plan: 7 slots. Main deepen, 3: K1 fork-dosed temperature knob plus hidden repertoire (Qwen3-8B, Gemma grid); K3 Qwen3-8B fork circuit; K2 one DAS protocol at decision vs task sites in both families, with push mediation. These serve how creativity manifests, influence, and novelty. Fix, 2: Step 0 CPU record repair of every MUST-FIX item; G Gemma prefill-matched dial and dormancy checks. Extend, 1: L composed-fork law on held-out units in 3 families plus base margins (temperature, mean answer). Cover, 1: TP top-five ban with survivors, geodesic landing.
key_changes: Re-centred the account on the decision token: the idea is cashed out at 1-2 counterfactually located tokens whose odds the task states set (0.05-0.19 bits given the fork class; exchange 30/30, 5-22 nats).

New primary K1: temperature applied only at the decision token, dosed from its measured margin, should give alternative ideas at no correctness cost where global and entropy-adaptive temperature cannot (iteration 1's window used T 1.3, about 5x too little).

New primary K2: one DAS protocol (fork-margin objective, >=3-class sources, permutation, untrained-network, reverse-interchange, projection and variance checks) at decision vs task sites in both families, plus mediation and clamp of the 40 pushes.

New primary K3: a path-patching circuit at Qwen3-8B's decision tokens validated against matched random components and in generation, compared with Gemma's motif; circuit-tracer with Qwen-3 transcoders as the extension.

Iteration 7's primaries are recorded as failed: fork claim inconclusive, DAS claim not supported (handle, not variable), axis disconfirmed. The fork margin is re-labelled a readout of the outcome, not an explanation of pushes.

Evidence restated as the review requires: per-source DAS recovery (forced BF/SPFA 0.17-0.43, forced BFS 0.06-0.53); counting-sort 'other' = dictionary counting sort; untrained-network ratio 5.1 on shortest path only; Gemma dial prefilled; Gemma natural variance below random at ranks 1-4.
Step 0 answers all six MUST-FIX and five minor items in place (0a-0k), including the iteration-7 positioning table from positioning.json and the venue correction for A Tale of Two Temperatures.
Artifact G runs the review's executed checks on Gemma: forced-BFS prompt with the prefill on the same slots, the dial in free generation, reverse interchange and projected-map retention.

Secondary L extends the temperature law to held-out units in three families with composed forks for second decisions, and tests the mean-answer hypothesis as post-training sharpening of the decision token.
Secondary TP re-poses the literal top-five question in a model that obeys a five-name ban (obedience screen, then geodesic landing in actual activation space, confirmed on held-out templates).
Novelty: HR enumerates the top-64 branches at each decision token with blind adjudication; search's level b reported as rates and clusters (7.8x instruction-only, 12 vs 7 vs 1 clusters, 0 novel).

Newly closed: contrastive and whole-program-likelihood DAS objectives as certification, the axis as channel, discreteness, seeds as cause, temperature above 1 as an idea source, search on shortest path and rain water, in-manifold top-five push in Qwen3-8B.
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: Fork localisation and the temperature law gained support in two families; a fork-dosed knob, a Qwen circuit and one matched DAS test can turn these leads into the run's answer.

critiques.description: Section 7.3 claims the DAS subspace routes counting sort where the full state cannot. The claim appears in 7.3.4 ('the forced counting sort source transfers 30 of 30 at every rank while the full state exchange gives 0 (29 programs labelled other, read below)'), in 7.3.6 and Table 300 ('the full state exchange lands none ... on two tasks it carries it more cleanly than the whole state does'), and in 7.10 Established ('on two tasks it routes more cleanly than the full state'). The artifact contradicts it. In art_veI9l_Rb9wDY results/novelty_audit.json, all 29 FULL_F_counting_sort programs are classed CATALOGUE_VARIANT with catalogue_name counting_sort; the judges describe them as a frequency dictionary followed by sorted keys. data/labels.jsonl shows that the forced counting-sort prompts themselves are labelled 'other' in 6 of 12 samples (F1-F3). The labeller does not recognise counting sort written with a dictionary, a gap the record itself documented in iterations 3-4. The full-state exchange therefore transfers counting sort in 29 of 30 programs, and the DAS edit writes the array form that the labeller does read. The same cell drives Table 297. In p1.json this source's per-source recovery is undefined because its full-state transfer is 0, yet its 30 DAS programs still enter the pooled numerator: T03 rank-1 recovery is (21+30+30)/(22+29+0) = 1.59, and counting the 29 gives 81/80 = 1.01. The 7.3.4 explanation 'above 1 where a trained direction moves the model further than the full exchange' is therefore wrong for kth smallest. Section 7.3.9 reports '36 catalogue variants' without saying that 29 of them come from this cell.
critiques.suggested_action: Add an adjudicated-label column, or relabel, for FULL_F_counting_sort and the F1-F3 sources. Correct Table 300 (full state: 29/30 counting sort in dictionary form) and Table 297 (T03 pooled recovery about 1.0 at every rank). Restate 7.3.4, 7.3.6, 7.3.9 and 7.10 as 'more cleanly than the full state on one task (shortest path: Floyd-Warshall 28/28 against 8/20)', and say that on kth smallest the DAS edit changes the implementation form (array against dictionary), not the algorithm. Expected impact: removes one of the three contradictions that set soundness to 1.

critiques.description: Three passages say the DAS handle matches the full-state exchange: 7.3.4 opens 'A rank-1 or rank-2 edit moves the algorithm about as far as the full state exchange on all three tasks'; the closing says forced instructions transfer '24 to 30 of 30' and that 'a DAS subspace of rank 1 or 2 at blocks 12 to 23 matches that exchange in generation'; and 7.10 calls it a handle 'that matches the full state exchange'. Per source (art_veI9l_Rb9wDY p1.json per_source), this fails for half the forced sources. On shortest path the forced Bellman-Ford/SPFA source reaches 30/30 under the full exchange but only 13/30 at rank 1 (recovery 0.43), 9/30 at rank 4 and 5/30 at rank 16 (0.17). On connected components forced BFS reaches 17/30 under the full exchange against 1/30, 7/30 and 9/30 (0.06-0.53). The pooled rank-1 recovery of 1.00 on shortest path (48/48, Table 293) holds only because forced Floyd-Warshall over-recovers (28 against 8, recovery 3.5) and cancels the Bellman-Ford/SPFA deficit; pooled rank 16 is 0.73. Rank 2 was never generated for any forced source (deviation D-C-k), so 'rank 1 or 2' is untested there. The text names the forced-BFS deficit and the Floyd excess but not the Bellman-Ford/SPFA deficit, which is the forced form of the ban's own substitute. The untrained-network control has gaps of its own. It ran on shortest path only (random_init_control 'present': false for T10 and T03), and the report does not say so. The committed version compared against the diverged contrastive fit (ratio 0.013, 'not meaningful', deviation D-randinit) and was replaced post hoc by a matched fit. Under the matched fit's own objective the untrained network gains 43.6 nats against 8.6 for the trained one (ratio 5.1, randinit_ly_T2.json), which is also unreported.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a recovery table by source and rank, and stop using pooled recovery as the summary. Restate the claim as: 'matches the full-state exchange for ban sources and for the forced Floyd-Warshall, quickselect and DFS sources; recovers 0.17-0.43 of forced Bellman-Ford/SPFA and 0.06-0.53 of forced BFS; rank 2 untested for forced sources'. Correct the closing and 7.10 to match. State that the random-init control ran on shortest path only and was replaced post hoc, and report the 5.1 ratio on the likelihood objective. Expected impact: removes the second contradiction.

critiques.description: Section 7.8.4, Table 370 and the closing ('as a dose dial it raises correct BFS programs from 11 to 42 of 50, above the 35 of an explicit BFS instruction') present the Gemma DAS edit as beating prompting. The two arms are not comparable. In art_HY7uYZz-OjRW src/g2.py (stage_g2d), the twin, DAS, DiM and random cells all generate from the prompt with c*, the 32-token canonical opening, prefilled, and apply one edit at the fork. The forced-BFS 'prompting ceiling' instead calls run_cell(pfz['ids'], [], ...) and samples from index 0. The artifact README says so ('The prompt cell samples naturally from index 0, and the DAS cells from index 32 after the c* prefill'), but the report drops the caveat. The prefill matters: Table 363 shows that the ' queue' branch writes BFS that fails every hidden test (0/125 pass), an unprefilled instruction can take such openings, and the prefilled opening plus the fork edit avoids them. The dial is also demonstrated only with a teacher-forced 32-token opening and a known fork index, so it is not yet a knob for free generation.
critiques.suggested_action: Rerun the forced-BFS prompt with c* prefilled on the same CRN slots (N = 50, a few GPU-minutes), or apply the DAS edit during free generation at the generated fork. Until then, restate the result as: 'with the shared opening prefilled, the edit raises correct BFS from 11 to 42 of 50; the instruction, sampled without the prefill, gives 35, which is not comparable'. Remove the 'above the 35' clause from the closing and the comparison from Table 370, and state the prefill condition wherever the dial is called a knob. Expected impact: removes the third contradiction.

critiques.description: Section 7.4.3, 7.10 Established ('the fork margin under a random push predicts the effect of the push (Spearman 0.80)') and the closing ('The margin at the decision predicts what moves the algorithm') present the fork margin as an explanatory predictor. It is a teacher-forced readout of the outcome itself. On connected components the label given the token at index 11 has zero entropy (Table 315), so the margin is the model's own log odds of writing the default, measured one token before it does so. A high Spearman with the sampled share is therefore expected by construction; I recompute 0.804 from f_analysis.json cells. Three results in the artifact show this. The more direct readout, the log-likelihood ratio of the 48-token opening, predicts better (0.869). The token-map placebo reaches 0.80 in 18% of permutations. And on shortest path, which has no single fork, the margin falls to 0.149. T03's prospective 0.60 uses the same readout over a 20-token opening. The question the fork claim was meant to answer, which property of a direction makes it move the fork, was tested twice and failed both times: the axis projection gave 0.17 and 0.01, and in iteration 4 the plan-subspace share gave 0.03. The proportionate reading is a localisation result: a push's effect is fully expressed in the next-token distribution at the fork. That is worth having, but it does not explain the pushes.
critiques.suggested_action: Restate 7.4.3, 7.10 and the closing as: 'the effect of a push is already expressed at the fork token (a teacher-forced readout matches the sampled outcomes at 0.80, and the 48-token opening at 0.87)'. Add one sentence recording that no direction-level property predicted which pushes move the fork (axis 0.17/0.01 here; plan-subspace projection 0.03 in iteration 4). Expected impact: makes the established claims proportionate to the evidence.

critiques.description: Section 7.8.3 concludes that 'the controls that failed for Qwen3-8B in Section 7.3 pass here', and 7.10 says Gemma's subspace 'passes all three controls', which implicitly certifies it where Qwen's is 'not a certified variable'. Three problems undercut this. (a) Qwen's handle was also rejected on the dormancy checks of [122]: reverse interchange restored 0/30, and projected-map retention was 0.20-0.26. Neither check was run or reported for Gemma. The one dormancy check that was run shows Gemma's L17 subspaces holding no more natural variance than random (g2_decisions.json natural_variance): rank 1 holds 0.00093 against a random 95th percentile of 0.00098, rank 2 holds 0.00116 against 0.00185, and rank 4, the k* used for the dose dial, holds 0.00187 against 0.00275. Meanwhile DAS recovers 1.98-2.81 times the full-state counterfactual, the off-manifold signature [122] warns about. The report quotes only the rank-1 value, as 'at the random 95th percentile'. (b) The controls differ between the two models. Qwen's untrained-network ratio (0.92) is a teacher-forced likelihood gain on fixed whole programs, which an untrained network can raise freely. Gemma's ratio (at most 0.25) is the directional shift of a fork-class margin at a single token. Qwen's permutation changed 44-56% of labels within the off-default class, whereas Gemma's swapped BFS and DFS sources. (c) Gemma's three seeds share only one direction (cosine 0.50-0.52 at k* = 4). So the conclusion 'certified in Gemma, not in Qwen' is confounded by differences in objective, site and readout.
critiques.suggested_action: Run the reverse interchange and projected-map retention for Gemma's L17 rank-4 subspace; both are teacher-forced and cheap. Report all four natural-variance ranks against the random 95th percentile, and state that the dial's subspace lies below it. Add a sentence saying the Qwen and Gemma controls used different objectives and readouts, so their pass/fail outcomes are not directly comparable. Restate 7.10 as 'passes random-subspace, permuted-label and untrained-network controls; dormancy checks not run'.

critiques.description: Iteration 7 adds three positive claims: temperature acts on the algorithm through the fork logits (the record's answer to request question 1a-c); a DAS dose dial at Gemma's fork; and evolutionary search reaching known techniques outside the catalogue. Section 7 sets none of them against its nearest published neighbour, although the record audit produced the verdicts. art_LzP2qPwUrANz positioning.json holds three verdict groups. Under 'temperature_fork_margin' it lists Hot or Cold? [32] (AAAI 2024; 'closest in spirit'), Beyond the 80/20 Rule (NeurIPS 2025; high-entropy forking tokens), Control the Temperature (COLM 2025) and Entropy-informed Decoding. Under 'das_algorithm_choice_code' it lists CDAS [112], which validates DAS steering by generation on refusal and a backdoor, and MIB [52]. Under 'evaluator_search_novel_algorithms' it lists FunSearch [81], AlphaEvolve [82], DivAlgo, Beneath the Diff and arXiv 2504.05108 (evolutionary search with RL). dimension_scores.justification: Almost every number verifies, but three iteration-7 conclusions contradict the run's own evidence. First, counting-sort routing: the artifact's novelty audit classes the 29 full-state 'other' programs as counting sort. Second, the claim that DAS 'matches' the exchange for forced instructions: per-source recovery is 0.17-0.43 for forced Bellman-Ford/SPFA and 0.06-0.53 for forced BFS. Third, the dose dial against the instruction: the artifact itself states the prefill asymmetry. Two more claims overreach: the fork margin is a readout of its own outcome, and Gemma's control verdict skips the dormancy checks that sank Qwen's handle.

A reader not on the run can follow the record in order. Review items are mapped to answers, each experiment opens with why it ran, and tables carry their numbers and sources. But four in-place tags still read 'pending the 2x2 of Step K' after 7.6 resolved them, and 'Step K' is never defined. Several corrected captions lost the file names the audited text carried. And the DAS section leads with pooled recovery, which hides the source-level failures that a reader needs to see.

Nearly all executed work is preserved with full tables, including failures, deviations and dead ends; Section 7 alone carries Tables 280-372 with every generation cell. Four things are missing: the record audit's positioning verdicts for the three new positive claims; the DAS experiment's dropped items (plan resampling, and the top-five placement in fitted coordinates, which the request asks for); the fresh-slot profile replication of the dose-unit experiment; and level-b search results at the level of clusters.

review.overall_assessment: Iteration 7 answered every item of the previous review (Table 280) and ran the work the record lacked: a DAS experiment with the published control set, prefix-resampling fork location, a temperature-through-fork test in two families, the dose-unit by direction-seed 2x2, an evolutionary search with an executable evaluator, and a Gemma path-patching circuit validated in the real model. Sections 1-6 differ from the record audit's corrected text (art_LzP2qPwUrANz report_corrected.md) only by rewording inside iteration-7 corrections, so the chronology is intact. I re-derived the iteration-7 headlines from the artifacts' own row and result files (recompute_checks.py in this workspace), and every one I checked matches: DAS per-source counts and P1 clauses (art_veI9l_Rb9wDY p1.json, data/labels.jsonl); fork-margin Spearman 0.804 on connected components and 0.149 on shortest path, and axis 0.173/0.015 (art_pHL7LWNhpcCS f_analysis.json cells); unit effect +0.45 [0.35, 0.55] and seed effect +0.03 (art_8O5eaNc5gxJs s1_2x2.json); search classes, with T03 643 = 540 catalogue variants + 103 known-outside and level b at 78 (search), 23 (larger mutator) and 2 (instruction only) (art_VhaHGe7SxV95 program_classes.json); Gemma temperature MAE 0.0265 and 26 teacher-forced prediction gaps with max 0.099 and mean 0.029 (art_HY7uYZz-OjRW g3_sweep.json, g2_dose.json). Three iteration-7 conclusions nonetheless contradict the run's own evidence. (1) 'On two tasks [the DAS subspace] routes more cleanly than the full state': the artifact's own novelty audit classes all 29 'other' programs of the full-state counting-sort exchange as counting-sort catalogue variants. On kth smallest, then, the contrast comes from the labeller's blind spot for counting sort written with a dictionary, and the T03 pooled recovery of 1.59 becomes 1.01 once those programs are counted. (2) 'A DAS subspace of rank 1 or 2 ... matches that exchange in generation': per source, the forced Bellman-Ford/SPFA prompt is recovered at 13, 9 and 5 of 30 against 30 of 30, and forced BFS at 1 to 9 of 30 against 17. Pooled recovery hides this, and rank 2 was never generated for a forced source. (3) Gemma's dose dial 'above the 35 of an explicit BFS instruction': the DAS cells had the 32-token opening prefilled while the instruction cell sampled from index 0, a caveat the artifact README states and the report drops. Two further claims overreach. The fork-margin 'predictor' is a teacher-forced readout of the outcome it predicts. And Gemma's subspace is said to pass the controls that Qwen's failed, without the reverse-interchange and projected-map checks that sank Qwen's handle; Gemma's rank-4 dial subspace in fact holds less natural variance than the random 95th percentile. The record audit also produced positioning verdicts for the three new positive claims, and none of them reached Section 7. Under the rule, a conclusion that contradicts the run's own evidence sets soundness to 1 and makes the review blocking, but all three are text-level corrections that the artifacts already support. Apart from these, the research behind the record is substantial, honestly reported and traceable, and it now covers every item of the original request.
strengths: Every item of the previous review is answered and mapped in Table 280. Stage A now gives the first commitment's attempted share beside correct programs (Tables 244-250, 284-285). The site of the choice is stated as open, with a new concordance table of noise sites against exchanges (Table 254b). The Gemma claims are restated within their controls, and Table 279 keeps each quantity with its own model and site. The seven geometry figures carry captioned markers, Table 238 has correct-only columns, the NLA contrast is redone at one unit per sample, and the in-manifold top-five push was run.

The chronology holds. A diff of Sections 1-6 against the audited corrected report (art_LzP2qPwUrANz report_corrected.md) finds 24 changed hunks, all rewording inside text already marked as iteration-7 corrections; no number changed.

The lost DAS experiment ran with the field's full control set: random subspaces of matched rank, permuted labels, an untrained network, the reverse interchange, a projected map, natural-variance dormancy and a second initialisation seed. Its negative verdict is reported plainly: P1 is not supported on any task, and the handle is not a certified variable. The divergence of the committed contrastive objective and the amendment that replaced it are recorded.

The dose-unit by seed 2x2 resolves the iteration-5 plan-noise null with a committed rule: unit +0.45 [0.35, 0.55] and seed +0.03 [-0.07, 0.14] on connected components. Anchors reproduce earlier rows (26/50 against 25; 1/50 against 1), and the result is checked against a cell-level mechanism (top quartile against shuffled positions), fresh slots and a third task. The six conditional iteration-5 verdicts are retagged.

The temperature test was committed before sampling. It found single-token forks on three mixed units, with H(algorithm | fork class) of 0.05-0.19 bits, and replicated in Gemma (MAE 0.026). The fork margins of the collapsed tasks (4.85-17.04 nats) give a mechanistic account of six iterations of temperature nulls, and the misses on two Qwen units are reported with post-hoc readings marked as such.

Evolutionary search with an evaluator, the documented route to new programs, finally ran. It had no-evolution, instruction-only and larger-mutator controls, a disclosed judge-gate failure, an arm-blind rule replication (94.4% agreement) and rule-of-three bounds, so the novelty null is now scoped against search, not only against single samples.

The Gemma circuit was validated per node against 50 norm-matched random components and then tested in generation. The steering effect (16/30 against 8/30 correct BFS) and the null effect of ablation are both reported, and so are the three failed transcoder-graph attempts.
The numbers are traceable through [ARTIFACT:id] markers and named result files. Every iteration-7 number I recomputed from the raw files matched.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this round the pool holds seven things. (1) A repaired record: Stage A with both metrics, the site stated as open, Gemma's claims within their controls, a per-model synthesis, seven captioned geometry figure markers, the Table 238 correct-only column, the clustered NLA interval, the unreported checks, the Section 4.9 wrap, the fork positioning row, and the iteration-5 verdict tags. (2) DAS on Qwen3-8B's task-specification states for 2-4 tasks, with random, permuted-label, random-initialisation, read-position, null-source, reverse-interchange and natural-variance controls; the categorical-versus-margin routing verdict; the causal algorithm manifold with seeds, instructions, single bans and the top-five ban placed on it; and the discreteness curve. (3) The fork location on three collapsed tasks, the fork-margin mediation of 40 bf16 directions and every knob cell, a plan axis confirmed on 24 fresh directions, targeted pushes, and the top-five prohibition at in-manifold doses. (4) Natural forks, one-token concentration and the temperature-against-margin test on Qwen3-8B's mixed units, with the collapsed margins, the 1a-c table on undecided units, and the plan-to-fork links. (5) The unit-versus-seed 2x2, the profile split, and prices at the design that moves. (6) Evaluator-guided search against matched sampling on 2-3 tasks, with blind novelty adjudication. (7) A validated circuit (or path-patching graph) at Gemma's fork, a controlled DAS with a valid-program dose, and Gemma's temperature check. NEXT ROUND. If P1, F and P2 hold, iteration 8 confirms the plan and fork on held-out tasks and in a second family (Gemma DAS at task states, or Llama), and uses the plan's value space as a mutation operator inside the search loop. If P1 fails, it reports the rank and band needed and moves the account to the fork alone. If N finds a novel program, iteration 8 deepens the search; if not, the claim is scoped and closed.
strategies.objective: Give the request's central question (how does the choice of idea manifest inside the model, and can we influence it?) a mechanistic answer in bf16 Qwen3-8B by testing the PLAN-AND-FORK account from three sides at once: (Q1) a low-rank plan variable at the task-specification states, fitted by DAS with Sutter-style controls, that transfers which algorithm the model writes with correct code, and whether it is categorical or a default-versus-rest margin, drawn as the request's algorithm manifold in causal coordinates; (Q2) one early fork token whose prefill-set margin predicts which of iteration 4's 40 random pushes (now known to escape in bf16) and every ban, exchange and plan-noise cell change the algorithm, and a fitted default-to-runner-up axis that predicts which random directions escape, with the top-five prohibition re-run at in-manifold doses; (Q3) the same fork explaining temperature: an idea knob only where the model is undecided (fork margin under one nat), a phrasing knob where it is collapsed. Beside the account: price the activation knob at the design that moves (K), test the documented route to truly novel algorithms, evaluator-guided search with a novelty critic (N), build and validate a circuit at Gemma's one-token fork with a controlled DAS and a valid-program dose (G), and repair the record as the review asked (E0).
strategies.rationale: WHY THIS DIRECTION. The direction block chose 'deepen' on the plan-and-fork account, and the evidence now makes the decisive tests cheap and well posed: the engine control showed that iteration 4's 40 random directions escape in bf16 as in 8-bit (Spearman 0.96), so they are a stable target a fitted variable can be asked to explain; Stage A gave full-state ceilings (shortest path 24 attempts / 21 correct of 30; forced Bellman-Ford exchange 30/30; forced BFS on connected components 28/30, although random pushes land on DFS), so a DAS recovery ratio has a denominator and the categorical-versus-margin question has a sharp test case; Gemma showed a one-token fork 138 tokens before identifying code, and iteration 1 showed shortest path splitting at generated token 3, so the fork is where the plan is cashed out. The DAS experiment of iteration 6 was lost at planning, so it is untested, not refuted. THE SIDEWAYS MOVES (aiming at positives within the request's questions): from random perturbation and forced-prompt centroids (P_t, rho 0.03) to fitting the variable to its causal effect (DAS) and to the token where the plan is spent (fork margin); from temperature as a global knob, a settled null on collapsed tasks, to the undecided units where the account predicts temperature does change ideas; from 'novelty in single samples', a settled negative after more than 25,000 correct programs, to evaluator-guided search, the documented route; from a top-five push at 1-8 ban units that overshoots the manifold to in-manifold doses; from Gemma's under-controlled DAS to one with informative controls and a dose that keeps programs valid. HOW THE SEVEN SLOTS MAP (the direction's split). Main deepen, 3 slots: Q1 DAS plan, routing, causal manifold, discreteness (how it manifests; the 'mean answer' subspace; the manifold); Q2 fork-margin and plan-axis mediation of the 40 bf16 directions, targeted pushes, the in-manifold top-five push (why pushes work; influence; top-five); Q3 natural forks and temperature against margin (question 1 and the BFS/DFS/Dijkstra internals in Qwen3-8B's own choices). Secondary, 4 slots: K plan-noise 2x2 and prices (influence); N evaluator search (truly novel solutions); G Gemma fork circuit, controlled DAS and dose (circuits; usable knob); E0 CPU record repair (review). LESSON FROM THE LOST PLAN. Each experiment direction is self-contained (artifacts of one round cannot use each other), stages its core before its extensions, states the memory plan for the 20 GB A4500 explicitly (DAS trains only the blocks above its layer on cached inputs), and carries a compact shared protocol instead of a long one, so the planning agent can finish. REVIEWER MAP. Majors 1-4 and the wording parts of minors 1-6: E0 (0a)-(0k), applied in place. Major 5 (DAS on Qwen3-8B, projection of the 40 directions onto the fitted subspace, the manifold, the figure markers): Q1, Q2 and E0 (0e). Minor 1's dose test: Q2's in-manifold top-five push and Q1's placement of the top-five ban. Minor 7's 2x2 and the price comparison: K, with E0 (0l) tagging the iteration-5 verdicts until K reports. Major 3's optional actions (random-initialisation and shuffled-target DAS, a dose that keeps programs valid): G. WHAT EACH OUTCOME BUYS. P1 positive and categorical: the idea is a small causal variable written into the task description, with one value per known algorithm, and the run has a causal manifold of algorithms. P1 positive and margin-and-ladder: the model holds only 'default or not', explaining one substitute per ban, the top-five failure and the absence of novelty. P1 negative: the rank and band the choice needs. F and P2 positive: why some random directions switch the algorithm. T positive: why temperature is a phrasing knob here and an idea knob elsewhere. N positive: the first correct novel program of the run; N null after adjudication: a clean statement that even search stays inside known algorithms on memorised tasks. Every branch is reportable. BUDGET. About 17 GPU-hours on A4500 pods (Q1 about 4.5, Q2 about 3, Q3 about 2.5, K about 2.5, N about 2 plus CPU sandboxes, G about 2.5-3), sized from iteration 6's bf16 throughput (about 2 s per program at B = 7 on a 16 GB RTX 2000 Ada; the A4500 has about 2.9 times its memory bandwidth). OpenRouter at most about USD 7 of the shared USD 20 (E0 0.5, Q1 0.5, Q2 0.5, Q3 0.5, K 0.5, N 3.5, G 0.5).

Method: temperature applied ONLY at a located decision token (T = d over its top-20, T = 1 elsewhere; T10 also index 11 after ' def'), with doses d1/d2 committed in advance from teacher-forced node logits plus token maps of forced continuations (2,050 programs). Comparators share 50 CRN slot streams per unit: global T 1.3/1.6/2.0 with top-p 0.95, min-p 0.1 at T 3, EDT-style and AdapT-style temperature, the same dose at the highest-entropy or a random position, class-uniform forcing; boundary window arm on T1/T2/T03. artifacts.summary: Iteration-8 test of claim K2: is there a certified low-rank causal variable for the algorithm a code model picks? One DAS protocol was committed before any GPU use (commit #0, hash-chained, 8 commits verified): linear orthonormal map (ranks 1/2/4/8), bounded KL objective, class-margin readout at the decision token. It was applied at three sites: Qwen3-8B T10 connected components (BFS/DFS/union-find, token 11 after ' def'); gemma-3-4b-it T1 grid (BFS/DFS only; A* and IDDFS failed adherence); and the Qwen T10 task band (blocks 12-23, one shared map). There were seven committed controls (c1-c7). RESULT: K2 DISCONFIRMED (p_K2 = 0.037). T10 decision site (rule-chosen L* = 22, k* = 4): TF recovery 8.43, OFF-MANIFOLD (DAS Delta 17.4 vs full-state 2.1 nats). c2 label controls keep 0.87/0.63/0.77 of the effect (limit 0.10); c3 random-init 0.69 (limit 0.25); c4 and c5 fail; c1, c6 and c7 pass. In generation (CRN, N = 30, hidden tests), DAS writes 29/30 correct DFS (full-state 2, random 0), but BFS edits yield 29/30 BFS attempts with only 5 passing tests, so the pooled verdict is NO HANDLE. GRID decision site (L* = 16, k* = 4): TF 3.07, OFF-MANIFOLD; c2 0.11-0.20 (2-class shuffles), c3 0.41, c5 and c6 fail; generation BFS 22/30 vs full 10, random 5, base 6 (SUFFICIENT HANDLE). T10 band (k* = 2): TF 0.82, c3 passes (0.18), c4 passes, c2 fails (0.71-0.79), c5 fails on twins (passes c5b), c7 fails; generation BFS 28/30, but DFS sources are routed to BFS (24/30). Post hoc, block 24 (full state carries 16 nats): recovery 1.22, c4-c7 pass, yet c2 (0.50-0.61) and c3 (0.54) still fail, so the specificity failure is not an artifact of the rule-chosen block. Mediation of iteration 4's 40 random pushes: retrospective Spearman 0.39 (bar 0.5), prospective 0.09 on 24 new directions. Clamping the band subspace removes -0.01 of escapes (random clamp 0.02; decision-site clamp -0.05). Pushes act elsewhere. No novel algorithm: 0 'other' among 1,857 correct programs. Geometry figures plot actual R_8 activation coordinates (MDS/Isomap plus PCA). Placement prompts (seeds, novelty instruction, Gemma top-5 ban) stay inside the twin cluster. Provides: method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out; 8 datasets, 2,042 examples: per-slot generation labels, per-pair TF Deltas, mediation slots); results/*.json; results/summary.md; das_maps/ (all fitted maps); data/ (samples, labels, TF rows); figures F1-F5; audit/rederive.py (stdlib; 38 checks all match, placebos fail; c3 recomputed only from stored means); reproducibility.md. Departures: NVIDIA L4 instead of A4500; B3 and the Gemma band dropped; band fits 109 steps and 2 seeds; S2 engine check not run; judge not called on labeller disagreements.

artifacts.layman_summary: The artifact reports early results on identifying neural circuit components in Qwen‑3‑8B that predict whether the model picks Kruskal’s or Prim’s algorithm at a key token, showing contrast scores and example token pairs.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_41
artifacts.summary: This artifact contains the Python driver (method.py) and three JSON result files (full_method_out.json, mini_method_out.json, preview_method_out.json) documenting the initial stages of a circuit‑discovery experiment for Qwen‑3‑8B (bf16, thinking off). The method script outlines the experimental pipeline, including hardware setup, contrast generation for two decision tokens (C1: Kruskal vs. Prim after a 61‑token opening; C2: find vs. dfs at token 11), GPU‑based attribution screening, exact noising/denoising, path‑level patching, and validation via ablation and steering tests against matched random components. The JSON outputs share a common metadata block describing the model, timestamp, and baseline comparisons (matched random components, RAND5, and an unedited “twin” run). The core results section reports a contrast metric C1nat_sd_m_v = 0.3379592507008036 and provides a sample of token‑pair contrasts (e.g., "W1|guy" vs. "W1|mother") with measured token logits, total effect (TE) values, and the model's predicted probabilities for the Kruskal (p_kr) and Prim (p_prim) tokens in both clean and corrupted contexts. Aggregated statistics for the C1nat contrasts are included: mean TE ≈ 0.893, TE standard deviation ≈ 0.377, and the count of TE values exceeding a minimum threshold (n_TE_gt_min = 15). The preview and mini JSON files repeat the same top‑level data, offering truncated versions of the full output. No further analysis, figures, or final verdicts are present in the provided excerpts; the experiment appears incomplete, awaiting later stages such as top‑10 node validation, generation steering tests, motif comparison with Gemma, and final verdict compilation.

Interaction (dial - prompt | prefilled) - (dial - prompt | free) = 0.66 [0.50, 0.82]. artifacts.summary: Iteration-8 claim L (pre-registered, hash-chained): a frozen law over one or two blindly located decision tokens predicts, before any temperature sample, the attempted-algorithm distribution of sampled programs at T 0.3/0.7/1.0/1.3 (top-p 1 and top-k 10, N = 100 same-stream slots per cell). Units scored: Qwen3-8B A3 trapped rain water, B6 valid anagram, B3 MST weight (law-development); held-out gemma-3-4b-it T04 substring search and R6 first/last position, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct T1 grid path (Llama bench units T03/T06 selected then dropped under the plan's time box). Result: claim L PARTIAL. 5/6 units pass (MAE <= 0.10, H <= 0.3 bits): A3 0.029, B6 0.054, B3 0.043, G-T04 0.033, G-R6 0.014; L-T1 fails 0.142 (decision token ' visited'/' queue' exists but its openings cover ~2% of programs; at T 1.3 Llama programs degenerate, 72/100 hit the cap; adjudicated labels primary). Held-out 2/3 pass but only 3 held-out units scored (< 4 required), so the held-out criterion is underpowered; no disconfirmation. Rivals: flat B0 (fit-twin shares), algorithm-level tempering B1, single-decision B2, entropy-located BH; the law beats B0 on 4/6 (sign test p = 0.34), B1 5/6, BH 5/6; the second decision matters on R6 (B2 0.051 vs 0.014, bootstrap CI excludes 0) and A3. Per-slot replay names the algorithm of 0.87-1.00 of on-opening slots; top-k 10 is token-identical to top-p 1 on Qwen/Gemma (6/2,400 programs regenerated). B3's iteration-7 T-1 lean (0.40) was a stream artefact: fresh 25/100 vs predicted 0.23. Base sub-arm (Qwen3-8B vs Qwen3-8B-Base, identical ids): committed prediction holds - decision margins gain 3.27/13.41/2.11 nats on T1/T10/T2 while phrasing-position entropy differs by 0.23-0.31 nats; JS divergence 6-10x higher at decision than phrasing positions; the base fork would give Prim 0.68 on B3 (instruct Kruskal 0.78), so the default is not the base model's mean. artifacts.layman_summary: Tests whether open AI models can avoid five banned path-finding algorithms when told to, and maps where the compliant answers sit inside the model's internal representation space.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_44
artifacts.summary:
Iteration-8 top-five ban study (gen_plan_experiment_6_idx7) on the T1 grid-path task, with four hash-chained commits in commitments.log.

SCREEN: 8 new open-model configurations plus 2 carried rows. Each model's own baseline defines its banned set B_c, and for every configuration B_c = {BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy best-first}. The literal five-name ban (iteration-2 templates W1-W3) was sampled N=50 per configuration (N=30 for C1).
- Programs: scored on the 48-case hidden suite (plus the 41-case ITER1 suite) and labelled by the exp9 10-class runtime/AST labeller.
- Adjudication: gated judges deepseek-chat-v3.1 9/10 and kimi-k2 10/10, third judge mistral-medium-3.1 9/10, plus executor manual reads.
- Result: only C6, Qwen3-32B thinking on (DeepInfra fp8), clears the committed 0.20 bar, with 17/50 correct survivors = 0.34 (Wilson 0.22-0.48). The survivors are unit Dijkstra 6, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 7, random-priority search 2, random walk 1 and wavefront 1.
- Others: C4 Qwen3-14B thinking on 0.14; C5 Qwen3-32B thinking off 0.08. Qwen3-8B thinking on (local vLLM FP8), Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-14B thinking off, gemma-3-27b-it, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B and the carried Qwen3-8B thinking off and gemma-3-4b rows are all 0.00.
- Disobedience: banned BFS/DFS is re-implemented without naming it (55-100% name-free).
- Cost of obeying: the ban raises C6 reasoning from 6.9k to 9.1k tokens and truncation from 7% to 46%.
- Strictest reading: dropping BFS/DFS/SPFA-named 'other' survivors leaves C6 at 0.22. Catalogue-only survivors give 0.12.

GEOMETRY on m* = C6. States come from unsloth/Qwen3-32B-bnb-4bit (nf4) with a truncated decoder (exact): S-mean over task-spec tokens of 300 forced prompts.
- Layer: every block from 19 to 45 classifies the forced algorithm at CV accuracy 1.00, so L* = 31.
- Manifold: PCA 32.4%/12.0%; MDS stress-1 0.42 (points) and 0.28 (centroids); Isomap components 8/3/1 at k=5/10/15, so the primary k is 15. Split-half reliability is 0.58/0.95/0.98.
- Classes: unit Dijkstra is the farthest non-banned algorithm from the banned five (OPPOSITE, bootstrap-stable). Bidirectional BFS and bidirectional A* are EDGE.
- Landing: the 6/6 catalogue survivors are unit Dijkstra, giving the verdict OPPOSITE. p_opp is 1e-4 under the U and F nulls and 0.057 under C; the algorithm-level permutation P is 0.20 (floor). The verdict is NOT robust (10/15 cells), and the pre-registered EDGE prediction is not supported.
- Held-out confirmation (commit #4, frozen geometry, W4/W5/P6/P7, N=50): 21/50 survivors, 9/9 catalogue survivors are Dijkstra, verdict OPPOSITE, so CONFIRMED.
- Quantisation check on Qwen3-8B: int8 and nf4 vs bf16 geodesic Spearman 0.954 and 0.916, class agreement 5/5, so the geometry is not precision-sensitive.
- Ban-prompt states move toward the named banned IDDFS/greedy centroids, and Dijkstra is the farthest centroid from them.
- M2: the label is decodable at p* (0.97) but not at the label-independent g16 (0.53).
- Circle check: no loop at the centroid level.
- Novelty: 0 novel among 27 audited correct programs.

AUDIT: src/rederive.py (numpy only) finds 0 mismatches. audit_headlines.py reproduces every count, the Wilson intervals, g (1e-12), S and the exact uniform p (6.4e-5). In its placebos, random survivor labels reject at 5% (nominal), but shuffled point labels still reject 36% under the per-program null. The algorithm-level p = 0.20 is therefore the honest landing evidence. The landing is correlational only: iteration 7's pushes moved 0/300 programs.

FILES: method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out: tp_screen 1,109 rows, tp_geometry 300, tp_confirmation 50; metadata holds every analysis, commits and 20 deviations); data/samples.jsonl and data/raw_*/labelled_*.jsonl; results/*.json; figures F1-F8 in activation coordinates; predictions/commit1-4.json; cache/states/*.npz (kept on the run volume). OpenRouter spend: USD 1.53. Hardware: RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB.
