critiques.description:
Three passages state that Qwen3-8B's fork circuit matches Gemma's: Section 8.10 'Established' ('with a layer-0 MLP at the condition span injecting the instruction, the same shape as Gemma's circuit'), Table 414 ('The same shape, depth 0.69') and the closing ('have the same shape in both families').

The preregistered circuit claim included 'its shape matches the circuit of Gemma's fork'. Its committed motif test returned DIFFERENT MOTIF (art_18XvfcJJZi1O results/summary.json motif.primary_comparison): condition-span share 0.01 against the band [0.21, 0.51], and fork-stack depth 0.86 against [0.45, 0.80]. Table 400 marks it 'Not met', and Table 416 lists 'motif differs on condition share and depth'. Section 8.5's post hoc reading ('matches Gemma qualitatively', from the exhaustive sweep) does not rescue the claim: every minimum-spanning-tree row of Table 401, committed or sweep, has depth 0.86 to 0.96, and the primary forced-Prim sweep row still has condition share 0.17.

The node behind the 'injection' story is weaker than reported. In summary.json validation.C1forced, the layer-0 condition-span MLP scores exactly +/-0.0 on all 10 held-out prompts under both ablation and steering (mean_d_heldout 0.0, p_sign_flip_heldout 1.0), against 8.14 and 7.41 nats on the 20 pair prompts. Table 395's 5.429 and 4.938 are those means diluted by the ten zeros. The zeros are an artefact of the code. In src/k3circuit.py, MeanCache.get averages only pair prompts whose span has the same token count as the target prompt. No pair prompt matches the held-out paraphrases' condition span, so val_edit returns None and nothing is edited. No other node in the three contrasts has an exact-zero held-out effect. The node's only out-of-sample support is the descriptive natural contrast: held-out 0.28 nats on 5 prompts, p 0.031, the smallest p that five prompts allow.
critiques.suggested_action: Rewrite 8.10 'Established', Table 414's shape row and the closing to the committed result: 'a late stack of fork-position MLPs and heads carries the fork logit in both families; the committed motif test reads different motif (condition share 0.01, depth 0.86), and the post hoc sweep still misses the condition and depth bands'. In 8.5, add held-out columns to Tables 395 and 396, and state that condition-span edits were not applied to held-out prompts, and why. Rest the layer-0 node on the paired prompts plus the natural contrast. Optionally, rerun the held-out arm with span means aligned by position (one GPU pass over 10 prompts).

critiques.description:
The 8.4 verdict paragraph concludes: 'What the protocol finds in both families is a strong steering handle of low rank at the fork'. The closing says the protocol 'found a rank-4 handle in both families that writes the algorithm in generation (29 of 30 correct DFS on connected components; 22 of 30 correct BFS in Gemma against 6 unedited)'.

The committed verdict at Qwen3-8B's fork is NO HANDLE (art_e-_q5mSJGrSb results/analysis.json verdicts.T10-dec). V0 is false: tf_recovery, gen_recovery and the McNemar test pass, but pass_ratio fails. The report's own Table 391 prints 'No handle by the pooled rule'. The edit toward BFS writes BFS in 29 of 30 programs, but only 5 pass the hidden tests (pass rate 0.20 against 0.83; 5:0 against random, p 0.063). The closing quotes only the DFS direction. Table 414 gets this right ('toward BFS 29 of 30 written, 5 correct'), so the synthesis contradicts the record's own tables.
critiques.suggested_action: State in 8.4 and in the closing: 'a rank-4 edit at the fork moves the written algorithm in both families. Under the committed rule it is a sufficient handle in Gemma and NO HANDLE at Qwen3-8B's fork, where the edit toward BFS writes BFS in 29 of 30 programs but 24 fail. Neither passes the specificity controls.' Wherever the 29-of-30 DFS figure is quoted, report the BFS direction beside it.

critiques.description:
The closing says: 'The fork is the highest-entropy position of the near-deterministic code around it in every sample'. Section 8.3 (from art_vnyi0Fm5SyNH results/k1_verdict.json K1c) measures something weaker. The fork lies above the 90th percentile of per-token entropy in every sample. But it is the single highest-entropy position among the first 64 tokens on only some slots: 44/44 in Gemma, 32/39 on minimum spanning tree, 21/39 on valid anagram, 2/50 on connected components and 0/37 on trapped rain water. Table 416 repeats the '2 of 50'.

Two neighbouring closing sentences overreach in the same way:
- 'At most 0.004 bits under iteration 8's blind locator' omits Llama, where the same locator gives 0.63 bits (Table 408).
- 'Temperature acts on the algorithm only through those one or two tokens' goes beyond the evidence. The law passed on 5 of 6 units with an underpowered held-out criterion. The flat law beats it on valid anagram (0.030 against 0.054), algorithm-level tempering beats it on substring search (0.023 against 0.033), and every predictor fails on Llama.
critiques.suggested_action: Replace the superlative with Section 8.10's own wording plus the per-unit counts: 'above the 90th percentile in every sample; the single highest-entropy position on 44/44, 32/39 and 21/39 slots, but 2/50 and 0/37 on the two units where a highest-entropy rule misses it'. Write 'at most 0.004 bits on the five Qwen3-8B and Gemma units; 0.63 bits on Llama's grid task'. Write 'on 5 of 6 units the fork tokens predict temperature's effect on the algorithm mix', and name the units where the flat or tempered rival does as well.

critiques.description:
Section 8.7's base sub-arm appears in the closing as a key finding: 'Post-training made those margins ... the instruct default is the base model's second or third choice at the fork, sharpened, not its mean answer'. Its numbers: the fork margin gain is 2.11 to 13.41 nats; the Jensen-Shannon divergence between base and instruct is 6 to 10 times larger at the fork than at phrasing positions, and 1.5 to 1.9 times larger than at entropy-matched positions; random positions show no excess.

art_lzuosbrb34wB results/positioning.json marks this 'ADJACENT, PARTLY OCCUPIED' by Cantarero et al., 'The RLVR Policy Shift Is Sparse and Predictable from the Base Model' (NeurIPS 2026 workshop). It also lists 'Sparse but Critical: A Token-Level Analysis of Distributional Shifts in RLVR Fine-Tuning of LLMs' (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2603.22446). I confirmed that both exist. Cantarero et al. find the divergence between trained and base models concentrated at forks flagged by base entropy: 18.4 to 57.1 times higher inside them, a residual 1.06 to 1.70 times after adjusting for entropy, and no excess at random placement. Their Fork-Patched Decoding splices base logits at those forks and recovers about a third of the lost diversity. Sparse but Critical shows that swapping a small share of tokens between base and RL generations recovers or erases most of the RL gain. Neither paper appears anywhere in the report or its references, although 8.7's sub-arm closely parallels Cantarero et al. in design and result.

More generally, only 8.4 and 8.6 carry a positioning paragraph in iteration 8:
- Fork-dosed temperature (8.3) relies on iteration 7's Table 371b temperature row. The fork-dosing artifact's positioning file adds 'Embarrassingly Simple Self-Distillation Improves Code Generation' (arXiv 2604.01193: fork against lock tokens, and why one global temperature is a compromise), which is cited nowhere.
- The circuit (8.5) and prohibition (8.8) sections cite no neighbouring work.
critiques.suggested_action: Add an iteration-8 positioning table built from the six results/positioning.json files, with one row per claim: the nearest neighbour with venue and version, and what the run adds. For the base sub-arm, cite Cantarero et al. and Sparse but Critical, and narrow the claim to what is new: an algorithm-level outcome on code at a counterfactually located fork, and the reading that the default is the base model's second or third choice. The concentration of post-training shifts at forks is not new. Until this is done, the base result earns no novelty credit.

critiques.description:
Section 8.8 answers the request's literal question: the survivors land on the opposite side of the banned five, not at its edge. The answer rests on a manifold built from forced prompts that name each algorithm by an alias (art_R-HSmXq2t97f src/common.py ALIAS_TABLE). Each state is the mean over the task-specification tokens of those prompts.

The geodesic classes follow lexical overlap with the banned names:
- Bidirectional BFS (edge, 10.9): all three aliases contain 'BFS' or 'breadth-first'.
- Bidirectional A* (edge, 11.6): all three aliases contain 'A*'.
- IDA* (middle, 13.3): the aliases contain 'A*', 'iterative deepening' or 'Manhattan heuristic', all of which occur in banned aliases.
- JPS and unit-weight Dijkstra (opposite, 15.9 and 21.6): the aliases share no algorithm-specific term with any banned alias.
Mechanism points the other way. On a unit grid, Dijkstra expands nodes in BFS order, and JPS is a pruned A*, yet these two are the farthest from the banned set.

The run's own iteration-1 geometry experiment warned that 'Named probes reached 0.98-1.0 accuracy at every layer, which says only that the algorithm's name is in the context', and built a name-masked set for that reason. Iteration 8's manifold classifies the forced algorithm at 1.00 from block 19 to block 45 and has no name-masked control. The per-program states cannot stand in for one: they decode the label only at label-dependent positions (0.97 and 1.00), and at 0.53 at the label-independent 16th token (results/geometry_M2.json). 'Opposite' may therefore mean that, under a five-name ban, the model picks the algorithm whose name is farthest from the banned names.
critiques.suggested_action: Rebuild the ten-algorithm manifold from name-masked descriptive prompts (one 4-bit forward pass over 300 prompts; the CPU geometry code is unchanged), and recompute g, the classes and the landing nulls. Alternatively, report how g correlates with the lexical overlap between each algorithm's aliases and the banned aliases. Until then, state in 8.8, 8.10 and the closing that the manifold is alias-named and that 'opposite' may reflect distance between names.

critiques.description: Section 8.3 says Gemma's filtered dial 'beats global T by +0.08 (p 0.23) and min-p, entropy-triggered and block-start temperature with p 0.016 to 0.023'. Min-p (A4) and block-start temperature (A6) were never run on Gemma: its arms in results/k1_cells.json are A0, A1, A3g, A5, A7 to A11, A9f and A10f, and the README lists 'G (A1, A3g, A5, A7-A11)'. The committed comparator rule (src/analysis_k1.py) takes the best setting in a family whose pass cost is at most 5 points, and falls back to the twin's Hill-1 when no setting qualifies. In amendment.json, the min-p and block-start families therefore compare against the twin's 1.636 with no arm behind them (p 0.016). The entropy-triggered arm (A5) did run, but it cost 18 pass points, so its p of 0.023 is also a comparison with the twin.
critiques.suggested_action: Write: 'it beats the twin-level fallback of the entropy-triggered family (p 0.023) and ties global T (+0.08, p 0.23); min-p and block-start temperature were not run on Gemma'.
Add [FIGURE] markers with captions (position, block, projection, N, centroids sized by implemented count, caveat) for exp44 F3/F4, exp39 F8, exp40 F3/F3b and exp42 F4. Describe exp42 F4 in 8.6.

dimension_scores.justification: Iteration 8 is easy to audit. Table 373 maps every review item to its fix, the seven claims are stated with their committed rules, Table 374 gives each artifact's question, compute and spend, and each table is introduced by what it settles. Two weaknesses: Table 414 and the closing disagree with Table 416 of the same iteration, and the iteration-8 MDS, Isomap and handle-coordinate plots have no figure markers (exp42 F4 is not described at all).

All seven artifacts are written up with their tables, deviations and not-run items, and the iteration-7 repairs are complete. Three gaps remain:
- Only 8.4 and 8.6 position their claims; the two published works that partly occupy the base-versus-instruct result are absent, although the artifact flagged them.
- The circuit's held-out validation arm never edited the condition-span node, and the report does not say so.
- The landing claim lacks the name-masked control that the run itself used in iteration 1.

review.overall_assessment:
Iteration 8 answers the previous blocking review in full and reports its seven new artifacts with traceable tables. Its synthesis, however, states three conclusions that the run's own committed outcomes contradict, so soundness is 1 and the review is blocking. Every fix except one (a name-masked manifold) is a text edit.

What holds. The record audit (art_vjtPMtWGMjsB) settles all six must-fix items with validated work. The counting-sort recogniser was gated before the relabel (references 6/6, gold kappa unchanged, controls 5/5), and the relabel then moved 35 of 960 rows from other to counting sort. Pooled kth-smallest recovery falls to 1.01/1.00/0.99; recomputing it from tables/recovery_by_source.csv gives pooled DAS gains over full-state gains of 81/80, 80/80 and 79/80 slots. Table 297b, the three untrained-network ratios, the fork margin stated as a readout, Gemma's natural-variance shares and Table 371b are all present. Lines 1-8390 of the iteration-8 draft differ from the audit's report_corrected.md only by one marked iteration-8 note, so the chronology holds.

I recomputed the headline numbers of every iteration-8 artifact from its own result files and found no mismatch:
- Fork dosing (k1_verdict.json, amendment.json): MAE 0.017/0.017/0.039/0.047/0.010; on connected components the filtered arm gives DFS 0.18 and Hill-1 1.54, +0.38 over the best comparator with lower bound 0.011.
- DAS (analysis.json, summary.md, rinit_*.json): recovery 8.43, 0.82, 3.07 and 1.22; label controls 0.87/0.63/0.77 and 0.11/0.11/0.20; random init 0.69/0.41/0.18/0.54; clamp 218 to 221.
- Circuit (results/summary.json): 9/10 and 8/10 nodes pass; McNemar 7:1, p 0.070; 24:0 at dose 0.5.
- Gemma (analysis.json, dormancy.json): 39:0; 38 against 13; 11:5, p 0.21; wordings 14-49; retention 0.28-0.18.
- Temperature law (cells of analysis_L.json): 0.029/0.054/0.043/0.033/0.014/0.142.
- Prohibition (screen.json, landing.json, landing_robustness.json): 17/50 survivors; g 10.9-21.6; p 0.0001/0.057/0.20; 10/15 robustness cells.

What does not hold.
(1) Section 8.10 'Established', Table 414 and the closing call Qwen3-8B's fork circuit 'the same shape as Gemma's'. The preregistered circuit claim included that the two shapes match. Its committed motif test returned DIFFERENT MOTIF: condition share 0.01 against the band 0.21-0.51, and fork-stack depth 0.86 against 0.45-0.80. Table 416 itself lists 'motif differs'. The layer-0 condition-span MLP that carries the 'injection' story also has exactly zero effect on all 10 held-out prompts, because the edit is never applied to them, and the report does not say so.
(2) The 8.4 verdict and the closing say DAS found a handle 'in both families' that writes the algorithm. The committed verdict at Qwen3-8B's fork is NO HANDLE (Table 391): the edit toward BFS writes BFS in 29 of 30 programs, but 24 of those fail. The closing quotes only the DFS direction.
(3) The closing says the fork is 'the highest-entropy position ... in every sample'. Section 8.3 measures 2 of 50 slots on connected components and 0 of 37 on trapped rain water.

Further issues:
- The base-versus-instruct result of 8.7 is partly occupied by two published papers. The artifact's own positioning file names both; the report cites neither.
- The 8.8 'opposite side' landing rests on a manifold of alias-named prompts with no name-masked control, although iteration 1 built such a control for exactly this reason.
- Gemma's filtered dial is said to beat min-p and block-start temperature, neither of which was run on Gemma.
- The iteration-8 MDS, Isomap and handle-coordinate plots have no figure markers.
strengths: Every must-fix item of the previous review is answered with validated work, not wording. The counting-sort recogniser was validated before relabelling (bench references 6/6, gold kappa 0.951/0.964 unchanged, constructed controls 5/5). The relabel changed 35 of 960 rows, all from other to counting sort. (3) K2: one DAS protocol at decision and task sites in two families, with every control including dormancy, and the mediation clamp plus a prospective test on 24 fresh directions. (4) K3: a matched-random-validated path-patching circuit at two Qwen3-8B decision tokens with generation steering and a motif comparison with Gemma (plus the transcoder graph if it fits). (5) G: the prefill-matched prompt arm, the free-generation dial and Gemma's dormancy checks. (6) L: the composed law on held-out units in three families and the base-versus-instruct decision margins. (7) TP: a five-family obedience screen and, if a model obeys, the survivor landing in actual activation geometry with held-out confirmation. NEXT ROUND. strategies.objective: Turn the decision-token account into the run's answer to the request's two central questions, in bf16 Qwen3-8B with gemma-3-4b-it as the second family. (1) Can we influence the idea with the simplest knob a user has? K1: temperature applied only at the counterfactually located decision token, at a dose read off its measured margin, should give the model's alternative algorithms in proportions predicted before sampling, at no loss of correctness, on collapsed tasks where global and entropy-adaptive temperature never move the idea. HR enumerates the top-64 branches at those tokens for correct ideas that no sampling reaches, adjudicated for novelty. (2) How does the idea manifest inside? K3 traces the circuit that turns the task and condition tokens into the decision token's odds in Qwen3-8B and compares its motif with Gemma's. K2 applies one DAS protocol, with dormancy controls, at the decision position and at the task-specification band in both families, and asks whether random pushes act through the fitted task-site variable. Beside these, the iteration repairs every blocking review item (Step 0); runs the Gemma dial with a matched prefill, in free generation and with dormancy checks (G); tests the composed law on held-out units in three families, with a base-versus-instruct margin test of the 'mean answer' (L); and answers the request's top-five question in a model that actually obeys a five-name ban, in actual activation geometry (TP).
strategies.rationale: WHY THIS DIRECTION. The direction block chose 'deepen' on the decision-token account, and iteration 7 makes its decisive tests cheap and well posed. Decision tokens are located counterfactually on four mixed units in two families (0.05 to 0.19 bits of algorithm entropy given the token's class) and on connected components (0 bits at token 11; forcing ' def dfs' gives 30/30 correct DFS). Their margins on collapsed tasks are measured (4.85 to 17.04 nats). Copying the task states of 'Implement <minority>' flips the token in 30 of 30 slots. One prediction follows directly and was never tested: if the idea is cashed out at one token, then temperature at that token alone, at a dose its margin sets, should change the idea where no global temperature can. Iteration 1's fork-window null used T 1.3, five to ten times too little for 5-17 nat margins, so the run's headline negative on temperature has a stated reopening condition. THE SIDEWAYS MOVES, WITHIN THE REQUEST'S QUESTIONS. From temperature as a global knob (a settled null on collapsed tasks) to temperature dosed at the decision token (K1). From a task-state DAS whose controls were uninformative by design (two-class permutations, a likelihood objective an untrained network can raise) to one protocol with a fork-margin objective, three-class sources and dormancy checks at two sites in both families (K2). From a circuit in Gemma only to a circuit in Qwen3-8B with a committed motif comparison (K3). From single-sample novelty, a settled negative, to the hidden tail at the decision token, which sampling never reaches at a 17-nat margin (HR). From five-name bans in two models that never obey to a screen for a model that does (TP). SLOT MAP (the direction's split). Main deepen, 3 slots: K1+HR, K3, K2. Fix, 2: Step 0 (every MUST-FIX and minor item; CPU) and G (Gemma, executed review checks). Extend, 1: L (composed law, held out, in three families, plus base margins). Cover, 1: TP. REVIEWER MAP. Major 1 (counting sort): Step 0 (0a). Major 2 (recovery by source, the untrained-network caveat): 0b. Major 3 (Gemma prefill): 0c restates, G executes the prefilled prompt and the free-generation dial. Major 4 (fork margin as a readout): 0d, and K2's mediation asks the question the margin could not answer, namely which property of a push moves the fork. Major 5 (Gemma controls): 0e restates, G runs reverse interchange and projected retention, and K2 removes the comparability problem by running one protocol in both families. Major 6 (positioning): 0f, plus a dated positioning search inside each new claim's artifact. Minors: 0g-0k. HARDWARE. Every experiment runs on one 20 GB RTX A4500, and artifacts cannot rent larger GPUs, so each artifact states its memory plan. K2 uses exact single-position recomputation at the decision site and cached-input training at the task band. K3 splits its backward pass on cached inputs, and its transcoder graph is a conditional extension. TP screens larger models through OpenRouter and extracts geometry with tagged 8-bit or 4-bit weights. BUDGET. About 21 GPU-hours across six experiments (K1 about 4.5, K2 about 4.5, K3 about 4, G about 1.5, L about 4.5, TP about 2.5) and a CPU evaluation. OpenRouter at most about USD 6.4 of the shared USD 20: Step 0 0.5, K1 1.5, K2 0.3, K3 0.3, G 0.2, L 0.6, TP 3.0. WHAT EACH OUTCOME BUYS. K1 positive: temperature is the creativity knob only at the decision token, at a dose its margin sets, a practical recipe that corrects the run's earlier conclusion. K1 failing by reversion: ideas are re-decided downstream. K1 failing by breakage: this bounds what intervention at the fork can buy. K2 with the decision site certified and the task site not: the idea becomes a low-rank variable only where it is cashed out. K2 with both sites certified: a pre-generation plan variable and a causal manifold exist. K3 with Gemma's motif: a cross-family account of how a code model turns a task description into its idea token. HR finding correct unreached ideas: the model holds more ideas than it shows, hidden behind the margin. TP with survivors: the edge-or-opposite question answered in actual geometry. Every branch is reportable.

hypothesis_update.direction_plan: 7 slots. Main cover 3: NOV-B1 and NOV-B2 (bin-packing evaluator search, same frozen protocol, disjoint seeds) and NOV-T (TSP replication): truly novel solutions, temperature as knob. Secondary 4: NOV-R (renaming under bans with an exact instrument: top-five and instruction parts), TP-G2 (mechanism vs surface program manifold, all survivor families: edge or opposite, geometry plots), BASE-W (weights that hold the sharpening: inside, mean answer), S0 (blocking record repair).
key_changes: Main object moves from names-versus-mechanisms (R6) to discovery with an evaluator (R7): evaluator-guided island search on online bin packing in two independent seed sets plus a constructive TSP replication fixed in advance, reusing the bin-packing harness that passed its gate before iteration 9's loss.

Decision-token branching is priced against T1.0, T1.6, a random-position placebo and an instruction to differ, at matched calls, with an exact name-blind behaviour instrument (bin choices on 2,000 probe states) and novelty scored against the textbook rules and every published discovered heuristic in the fetched corpus.

R6 restated on the corrected evidence: renaming is robust in non-obeying configurations and in Qwen3-14B (k=5 mechanistic 0.10-0.24 vs lexical 0.86); for Qwen3-32B the k=5 gap is 0.22-0.30 by tracer and hand reads, below the 0.4 bar, and its survivors are mostly other KNOWN disciplines.

Two coding artifacts of the exhaustion curve are recorded: grid Bellman-Ford read as iterative deepening, and greedy best-first counted as a violation at k=4 because the registered fine-class sensitivity was a no-op (corrected 0.48 vs 0.24).
The described ban is recorded as instrument-dependent (-0.07 to +0.58; about +0.21 per cell), and it is retested with an exact instrument on bin packing (P2).

The top-five answer is restated: unit-weight Dijkstra opposite on every language-built map and at the edge on the program map; Bellman-Ford/SPFA survivors opposite; language maps track names and textbook data-structure attributes (R_DS 0.65), not measured expansion order.

A factorial discipline-by-container program set (with four or more non-banned classes and every survivor family placed under preregistration) decides whether the program map's edge is in mechanism or in surface (G1, G2).

Sharpening localisation moves from component patching (non-specific: random late sets close 0.81) to weights: base unembedding rows of the fork tokens and late-MLP weights, with matched random-direction row controls and Fork-Patched Decoding as the baseline (W1-W3).
New measures tie discovery to the run's account: V5 (are new heuristics born at a few decision tokens?) and V6 (rename rate: offspring asked for a new idea that decide like a parent).
S0 answers all five MUST-FIX and five minor items of the blocking iteration-9 review in place, with the exact inputs named.

Newly closed: the tracer as an IDDFS/IDA*/JPS instrument, rotated name sets, the described manifold as name-free, fork-stack specificity and generation carrying, Llama base under its chat template, and 'the obeying model renames BFS'.
Infrastructure hedges against the iteration-9 losses: two redundant bin-packing artifacts, verified input copies, early hash commits, per-stage checkpoints and staged scaling.
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: The request's headline 'truly novel' question has never met its one untried route, an evaluator; the gated harness exists; the N and B leads are partial and get the other four slots.

Decision-token branching (forced non-argmax token at the fork proxy) as the mutation operator inside an evaluator-guided search loop.
Base-model fork distribution (Fork-Patched Decoding) as a mutation operator inside evaluator search.

Top-up of bidirectional BFS, IDDFS, JPS and bidirectional A* programs to classify landings over four or more non-banned algorithms.

critiques.description: The Qwen3-32B exhaustion-curve conclusion contradicts the record's own hand reads (Section 9.3 and Table 431, 9.8 'Established', Table 444, closing). The report concludes that mechanistic compliance falls to 0.22 at k=5 for Qwen3-32B (runtime label) and that 'banning the repertoire moves compliance to the names'. In the A_k5 cell of art_8nXdw3_lDAll (data/samples_v9.jsonl joined with data/manual_reads_v9.jsonl), 36 of 46 completed programs are runtime-label violations. 22 of them were hand-read, and the reads class 17 as non-banned disciplines: 9 iddfs-labelled grid Bellman-Ford programs, 3 raster flood-fill sweeps, 2 set frontiers, 2 random-choice frontiers and 1 mixed deque. Only 5, all unit-weight Dijkstra, are read as banned. Substituting the reads gives 27/46 = 0.59 (tracer 0.67, results/n3_tracer.json), a k=5 gap of about 0.30 (tracer 0.22) against the committed bar of 0.4. On the held-out templates the figures are 0.54 (tracer 0.52), gaps 0.40 and 0.42. Section 9.3 says the tracer's curve falls less 'because it reads the coordinate-key heaps and Bellman-Ford rounds of the late cells as compliant', yet Table 429 reads exactly those families as 'other'. The report also states that 'the runtime label reads the Bellman-Ford rounds as iterative deepening'. The closing paragraph then calls the survivors 'mostly not renamed BFS', which cannot hold together with 0.22 for this model. Qwen3-14B is unaffected (runtime 0.10, hand reads 0.12, tracer 0.24).
critiques.suggested_action: Add a 'mechanistic, hand reads substituted' column, with its gap and a Newcombe interval, to Table 431 for every k=5 cell, and restate the claim per model. It is supported for Qwen3-14B under all three readings. For Qwen3-32B only the runtime label meets the bars; the hand-read and tracer readings give a k=5 gap of 0.22 to 0.30, below the committed 0.4, and a non-monotone curve (tracer 0.47 at k=4, 0.67 at k=5). Replace the 9.3 'because it reads ...' sentence with the hand-read adjudication. Revise 9.8 'Established', the Table 444 verdict and the closing sentences 'falls ... to 0.22 (Qwen3-32B)' and 'banning the repertoire moves compliance to the names' to match.

critiques.description: Greedy best-first is counted as a violation at k=4, and the registered sensitivity for this case is a silent no-op (art_8nXdw3_lDAll). The cumulative order is bfs, dfs, iddfs, astar, gbfs (commit1a k_order), so greedy best-first is not banned at k=4. The coarse map sends gbfs and astar to the same HEUR class. As a result, 11 of the 35 runtime violations in Qwen3-32B's k=4 cell are gbfs-labelled programs that obey the ban; another 12 carry the iddfs label that the hand reads show is often grid Bellman-Ford. Counting only the greedy programs as compliant raises k=4 mechanistic compliance from 0.24 to 22/46 = 0.48 (tracer 0.47). About half of the curve's largest step (0.84 at k=3 to 0.24 at k=4) is therefore a coding artifact. commit1a registered exactly this sensitivity ('fine classes (e.g. greedy at k=4 is compliant)'). But mech_ok in src/analysis_v9.py applies fine classes only when MECH_FIELD == 'order_class', so under the runtime-label fallback the sensitivity reverts to the coarse map. results/n3.json reports fine-class values identical to the primary at every k, and the report never mentions the sensitivity.
critiques.suggested_action: Implement the fine-class sensitivity for the runtime label: give gbfs, astar, jps and idastar their own classes and ban only the algorithms named at each k. Report it beside Table 431 for both models, restate the k=3 to k=4 step with it, and say in 9.3 that the registered sensitivity was a no-op in the executed code.

critiques.description: The described-ban result (Section 9.3, Table 433) mixes instruments, and the artifact's tracer result, which reverses it, is omitted. Table 433 reports that describing the five mechanisms without names raises mechanistic compliance from 0.22 to 0.80 (difference +0.58, 0.39 to 0.71), using the runtime label in both cells. The artifact's tracer version (results/n3d_tracer.json) gives 0.60 (29 of 48) described against 0.67 (31 of 46) named, a difference of -0.07 (-0.25 to 0.12). The report argues that the runtime label is the closer reading for the described cell. It keeps the runtime label for the named k=5 comparator, however, where its own hand reads show that label misclassifies most violations. Taking the reading the record itself favours in each cell (runtime label for described, hand reads for named), the difference is about 0.80 - 0.59 = +0.21.
critiques.suggested_action: Add to Table 433 the tracer row and a named comparator with the hand reads substituted, report the difference under each reading, and restate the finding as instrument-dependent: from -0.07 to +0.58, and about +0.2 under the per-cell reading the record argues for. Carry the restatement into 9.8 and the closing.

critiques.description: The placements of the survivors that are not unit-weight Dijkstra were computed but not reported, and the report lists them as future work (Section 9.4 Table 438, 9.9, closing). The geometry artifact (art_VVA3P0ocZNA2, results/placement.json) placed all 38 iteration-8 survivors on each program frame, not only the 15 unit-weight Dijkstra programs in Table 438. On the Qwen3-32B primary frame, which passes its placement gate (LOO 0.85), all 15 Bellman-Ford/SPFA survivors land opposite. Their median g is 28.1 against the frame median of 24.8, and 14 of 15 are nearest the unit-weight Dijkstra programs. They also land opposite on the Qwen3-32B-only frame (15 of 15); on the Qwen3-8B frame 10 land edge and 5 opposite. The 3 BFS variants and the 5 other known programs land edge. Section 9.9 ('placing the other survivor families, the grid Bellman-Ford rounds ...') and the closing ('landings for the survivor families other than unit-weight Dijkstra') present this as open work. The closing's 'all 15 survivors place at the edge' reads as a statement about the survivors as a whole. These results bear directly on the request's edge-or-opposite question.
critiques.suggested_action: Add per-family placement rows for every frame to Table 438, with two caveats: they were not preregistered, and the frame has only two non-banned classes, so 'opposite' means farther than the median of unit-weight Dijkstra and IDA*. Revise 9.9 and the closing to say that the unit-weight Dijkstra survivors place at the edge and the Bellman-Ford/SPFA survivors place opposite on both Qwen3-32B frames.

critiques.description: The RSA table omits the best-fitting model matrix for the named manifold (Section 9.4 Table 437, closing). Table 437 and the closing ('the language manifolds track lexical distance', 'and not behaviour') report four of the seven model matrices in results/rsa.json. The omitted data-structure matrix d_DS is a Hamming distance over six flags of the reference implementations: FIFO, LIFO or recursion, heap, two frontiers, restarts and heuristic key. It is a component of the reported behavioural matrix (R_beh = d_order + 0.5 d_DS). It is the best fit on Qwen3-32B's named manifold (0.65, exact p 0.001, against lexical 0.46). It fits the name-only manifold about as well as lexical distance (0.44 against 0.47) and the described manifold less well (0.43 against 0.57). The expansion-order component alone (R_beh_order) fits none of the three (-0.03 to 0.16). So the language manifolds encode the algorithms' textbook mechanism attributes as well as their names. What they do not encode is measured expansion order.
critiques.suggested_action: Report R_DS, R_beh_order and R_desc_lex in Table 437. Change the 9.4 and closing sentences to 'track lexical distance and textbook data-structure attributes, not measured expansion order'. Because aliases often contain mechanism words, also report the correlation between the lexical and data-structure matrices and a partial RSA of each controlling for the other.

critiques.description: The held-out rerun's mean averages a bimodal effect (Section 9.5, Table 444 'half its pair values', closing). The repaired held-out effect of the layer-0 condition-span MLP is reported as 3.86 nats (ablation) and 3.85 (steering), 'against 8.14 and 7.41 on the pair prompts'. The ten held-out values in results/b3_summary.json split into two groups. Under ablation five lie between -0.25 and -0.11 and five between 7.14 and 8.85 (under steering, -0.27 to 0.46 and 6.15 to 9.78). They alternate with the clean (padded) and corrupt (forced) rows of results/b3_heldout_rows.jsonl. On every forced held-out row the effect is about the size of the pair-prompt effect (mean 7.9); on the clean rows it is about zero. Unless the 8.14 comparator averages the same two sides, 'half its pair values' is an averaging artifact. The sign-flip test also treats the two sides of five contrasts as ten independent units. In addition, two of the five contrasts (F11, F15) carry 153 of 765 empty edits.
critiques.suggested_action: Report the held-out effect per side and per contrast (n = 5), state how the 8.14 and 7.41 pair values were averaged, give the test on the five contrasts, and rephrase 'half its pair values' to match.

critiques.description: The random patching sets repeat components, and one computed null is not reported (art_cDba8_DycUJd). draw_random_sets in src/cmap9.py promises 'within a set no repeats' in its docstring but falls back to the full pool when the non-repeating pool is empty. In results/random_sets.json an MLP repeats in 47 of 50 'random sets without the circuit's top 15' on minimum spanning tree, in 36 of 50 matched random sets on connected components and in 50 of 50 pure sets there. Those sets patch 8 or 9 distinct components instead of 10, because an MLP patch is an idempotent replacement. Both comparisons the report relies on use these nulls: fork stack above the pure sets on minimum spanning tree (p 0.039) and above random sets on connected components (p 0.020). The file's third null (Rscaled: median 0.64, p 0.098 on minimum spanning tree) is not reported. On connected components the fork-stack share of 0.45 is a ratio of mean margins, while the mean of per-prompt shares is 0.13 (five fork MLPs: 0.41 against 0.07). That share is therefore carried by a few large-gap prompts.
critiques.suggested_action: Redraw the random sets without replacement, or report the effective set sizes and the nulls restricted to ten-component sets. Add the Rscaled null beside Rpure, and show the per-prompt share distribution on connected components.

critiques.description: The coarse-class reference and the obeying model's instrument range are missing outside the survivor reading (Section 9.3, closing). Under the coarse classes three of the five non-banned catalogue algorithms (unit-weight Dijkstra, IDA*, jump point search) fall in a banned class. The report gives this 0.6 null for the survivor reading only. My recomputation from results/retrace.jsonl shows the pooled rename gap is robust to it: 0.697 primary, and 0.662 when unit-weight Dijkstra, IDA* and jump point search labels count as compliant (294 of 371 covert programs are bfs or dfs labels). The obeying configuration C6 is not robust: runtime 0.63 against tracer 0.31, with post-hoc bounds of 0.30 to 0.70 (instrument_bounds.json), and 16 iddfs-labelled and 13 unit-weight Dijkstra programs among its covert ones. The closing also says the programs are 'read by runtime expansion order'. The runtime label is built from heap priorities, FIFO and LIFO evidence and restarts, not from the expansion order; the order-based instrument is the tracer.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the sensitivity that counts unit-weight Dijkstra as compliant to the rename-gap and exhaustion tables. State C6's instrument range wherever the obeying model's gap is quoted. Replace 'read by runtime expansion order' with 'read by the runtime label (heap priorities, frontier evidence, restarts) and by the expansion-order tracer'.

critiques.description: Small reporting slips that change how a number reads. (a) Section 9.4 gives the name-evocation probe as 'balanced accuracy 0.69 (chance 0.11) and the programs at 0.17' without noting that chance for the six program classes is 0.167, so the program transfer is at chance. (b) Section 9.3 and the artifact's deviations.json say seven of 280 rotated and described samples were lost. The B, C and D cells hold 350 planned rows (300 rotated, 50 described), of which 343 exist. (c) For Gemma's grid fork, Table 440's 'Base P(D)' of 0.089 does not show that the base model puts 0.25 on the alternative class and 0.66 of its fork mass on tokens mapped to neither class (base_mass_unmapped 0.663). Post-training there both reverses and concentrates the choice, and the section title 'sharpened the fork' fits the first-and-last forks better than this one. (d) Section 9.2 says 'within algorithms the relation vanishes'. That rests on a stratified test over three algorithms, with a null SD of 0.41, whose planted-control power was shown only across aliases.
critiques.suggested_action: State the six-class chance level beside 0.17. Correct the denominator to 7 of 350, or say which 280 rows were meant. Add base P(alternative) and the unmapped base mass to Table 440, and describe Gemma's grid fork as reversed and concentrated. Write 'not detected (three algorithms; underpowered)' instead of 'vanishes'.

critiques.description: The not-run section omits the bin-packing harness that passed its gate (Section 9.6, 9.9). The NOV-B gen_art workspace (gen_art_experiment_48) stopped on an API error after building an evaluation harness that passed its gate: results/harness_gate.json, 'G-HARNESS PASS' in logs/gate.log, and the best-fit OR3 excess of 5.37% reproduced. Recording the direction as lost, with no result, is correct. But iteration 10 is the last, and the closing names evaluator-guided search as the one untried route to the request's 'truly novel' question. Whether a validated evaluator already exists matters for planning it.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a line to 9.6 and 9.9 noting that the bin-packing harness was built and passed its gate before the failure, and can be reused for iteration 10's evaluator search. Keep the statement that no search ran.

dimension_scores.justification: A primary 'Established' claim, that Qwen3-32B's mechanistic compliance falls to 0.22 at five names and that 'banning the repertoire moves compliance to the names', is contradicted by the record's own hand reads. It is also contradicted by the report's own statement that the runtime label misreads grid Bellman-Ford as iterative deepening. With the hand reads substituted the value is 0.59 and by the tracer 0.67, and the committed k=5 gap bar of 0.4 fails under both. The rubric scores a conclusion that contradicts the run's own evidence at 1. The rest of what I checked is sound or conservatively hedged: the pooled rename gap, Qwen3-14B's curve, the landing split and the sharpening reading.

The record is dense but navigable. Tables carry n, intervals and committed bars, Table 444 states each verdict with its deciding evidence, and corrections are marked in place. Several computed columns are missing (hand-read compliance, the fine-class sensitivity, the tracer row for the described ban, the RSA data-structure matrix, per-family placements). Averaging the held-out rerun over clean and forced rows makes some numbers read differently from what the artifacts show.

Iteration 9 adds three things. First, a names-against-mechanisms gap that is robust (0.70 by the runtime label, 0.61 by the tracer, positive in every configuration, 0.66 even when unit-weight Dijkstra counts as compliant). Second, a name-free test of the request's edge-or-opposite question, which splits by the kind of map. Third, a component-level account of where post-training sharpened the fork in Qwen3-8B: late MLPs and the unembedding, not the task-specification nodes. The request's 'truly novel' question is still open, and the exhaustion curve's strength for Qwen3-32B is overstated.

review.overall_assessment:
Iteration 9 is recorded carefully and almost completely. The report covers every iteration-9 artifact: the rename and exhaustion artifact (art_8nXdw3_lDAll), the geometry artifact (art_VVA3P0ocZNA2), the base-model artifact (art_cDba8_DycUJd) and the record audit (art_iYh9zVP7myjJ). It names the three directions lost at gen_art (the second task TP-W, bin packing NOV-B and TSP NOV-T) as planned-not-run in 9.6, 9.8, 9.9 and the closing, not as nulls. I recomputed the headline numbers from the artifacts' own result files and they match the report: the pooled rename gap of 0.697 (from results/retrace.jsonl, positive in 10 of 10 configurations); the k-curve cells (Qwen3-32B k=5 runtime 10/46 = 0.217, Qwen3-14B 0.102); the hand-read share (23 of 76); all nine g/median ratios of Table 435 (1.631, 1.081, 1.200, 0.673, 0.317, 0.793, 1.173, 1.007, 0.630 from rederive.json); the Gemma grid gain (1.784 from the 20 per-prompt gains); the patching shares and nulls; the counts in Table 442; and the held-out means (3.857, 3.85). The 49 corrections of the record audit apply cleanly (lint 28 to 0; 400 checks, 0 mismatches). All five MUST-FIX items and both minor items of the previous review are addressed in place, and I do not raise them again.

One contradiction in a primary claim blocks the record. 'Established' (9.8), Table 444 and the closing say that under cumulative bans mechanistic compliance falls to 0.22 for Qwen3-32B, and that 'banning the repertoire moves compliance to the names'. The record's own hand reads (Table 429) contradict this for that model. They agree with the tracer on 0.88 of programs and with the runtime label on 0.64, and the report itself says the runtime label 'reads the Bellman-Ford rounds as iterative deepening'. In the Qwen3-32B k=5 cell the hand reads class 17 of the 22 read violations as non-banned disciplines. Substituting them gives mechanistic compliance of 27/46 = 0.59 (tracer 0.67), so the k=5 gap is about 0.30 (tracer 0.22), below the committed bar of 0.4. Section 9.3 explains the tracer's divergence by blaming the tracer for agreeing with these hand reads. The same closing paragraph calls the survivors 'mostly not renamed BFS', which cannot hold together with 0.22 for this model. At k=4, 11 greedy best-first programs are counted as violations although greedy is not yet banned. The registered fine-class sensitivity that covers exactly this case does nothing under the runtime-label fallback and is never reported. The Qwen3-14B curve holds under every reading (runtime 0.10, hand reads 0.12, tracer 0.24). By the rubric, a headline conclusion that contradicts the run's own evidence scores soundness 1, so blocking is true. The fix is local: add the hand-read and fine-class readings, then restate the Qwen3-32B claim in 9.3, 9.8, Table 444 and the closing.

The artifacts computed three more results that the report leaves out, and each one qualifies a closing sentence. (1) The tracer reading of the described ban gives 0.60 against 0.67, a difference of -0.07, not the reported +0.58. (2) The placements of the 23 iteration-8 survivors that are not unit-weight Dijkstra: all 15 Bellman-Ford/SPFA programs land opposite on the Qwen3-32B primary frame, yet 9.9 and the closing list this placement as future work. (3) The RSA data-structure matrix fits the named manifold best (0.65, against lexical 0.46). Smaller issues: the held-out rerun averages clean and forced rows together, the random patching sets repeat components, and some wording and bookkeeping slips. Each positive claim names its nearest published neighbours. The record covers most of the request: behaviour, temperature, top-k and seeds, context seeds, instructions, BFS-against-DFS internals, circuits and lenses, and a top-five prohibition placed on activation-space manifolds with geodesics, MDS and centroids. Coverage is still partial: the request's 'truly novel' question has not met its one untried route (an evaluator search), and the edge-or-opposite answer is split by the kind of map.
strengths: Complete artifact accounting for iteration 9. Every artifact is cited by id. The three lost directions are named as planned-not-run, with the explicit statement that the report records no result, null or dead end for them. The dead ends are labelled with the evidence that killed them: the tracer on iterative deepening, IDA* and jump point search (0 of 34, 1 of 22, 1 of 7), the degenerate alias name distance, and Llama's untrained chat-token embeddings.

Numbers trace to executed outputs. Every headline I recomputed matched the artifacts' files to the reported precision: rename gap, k-curve cells, hand-read shares, all nine g/median ratios, Gemma gains, patching shares and nulls, the Table 442 counts and the held-out values. The record-audit artifact re-derives 400 values with 0 mismatches.

Failed gates are handled honestly and by rule. The tracer's gold gate failed (0.70 against 0.90); the committed fallback was triggered, and every names-against-mechanisms number is labelled descriptive. The geometry's rank gate failure (0.894), the P2 failure and the committed MIXED outcome are all reported, as are the failed sharpening predictions.

The previous review is answered in place. The circuit claim now reads 'different motif' with held-out columns, and a rerun confirmed and repaired iteration 8's unapplied held-out edit. NO HANDLE is stated beside the DFS figures, the entropy superlative is replaced, Cantarero et al. and Sparse but Critical are positioned, and the alias-named manifold confound is tested and the manifold rebuilt without names.

The name-free geometry rebuild answers the request's edge-or-opposite question directly. It uses four maps and two models, with robustness grids, three distance variants, bootstraps, leave-one-out placement gates, an independent recomputation with scikit-learn and networkx, and the statement that the geometry is correlational.

The base-against-instruct work controls its main confound before claiming anything. It reproduces Cantarero et al.'s base-entropy pattern and shows the fork divergence is only 0.75 to 1.18 times that of entropy-matched positions. In both teacher forcing and generation it reports that matched random sets do as well as the fork stack (19 of 30 Prim for each), a careful negative.

Each positive iteration-9 claim names its nearest published neighbours and says what is added. The rename gap is set against Denial prompting, IFEvalCode, Semantic Gravity Wells and the white-bear study, and is called 'new only as a measurement'. The geometry is set against [154] and [155], and the sharpening against [142], [143] and [153].

strategies.expected_outcome: After this round the pool holds seven things. (1) A repaired record (S0): every MUST-FIX and minor item answered in place, an iteration-8 positioning table, and the alias-level Spearman of g against lexical overlap from iteration 8's own geodesics. (2) TP-B: a gated expansion-order tracer; the retrace of every five-name-ban program on disk (N1); the obeying model's survivors classified by trace (N2); cumulative bans k = 1..5 on Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-14B with thinking, with held-out confirmation at k = 5 (N3); a described five-mechanism ban; six rotated five-name sets (N5); an exploratory scale check. (3) TP-G: four manifolds (named, descriptive, name-only, program states) of the obeying model and of bf16 Qwen3-8B in actual activation coordinates, with iteration 8's survivors re-scored, the lexical regression and the behavioural distance (N4). (4) TP-W: the same test on weighted shortest path with a relaxation-order tracer and a name-free program manifold (W). (5) NOV-B and (6) NOV-T: evaluator-guided search at matched calls with temperature, decision-token branching, a placebo, instruction mutation and a no-selection arm on online bin packing and constructive TSP, scored on held-out instance families against textbook, tuned and published discovered heuristics (V1-V3). (7) BASE: base against instruct forks in Gemma and Llama with Cantarero's controls, base-component patching at Qwen3-8B's validated fork stack, and the circuit's held-out rerun (B1-B3). NEXT ROUND (iteration 10, the last): it confirms whichever of N, V and B landed on evidence it never saw (N: N5's rotated-set survivors placed on TP-G's frozen manifolds and a third prohibition task such as kth smallest; V: a third scored task or new instance families; B: Llama generation), writes the final record and declares what stayed null.
strategies.objective: Answer the request's top-five question with instruments that names cannot fool, and attack its layman question ('can we make LLMs give truly novel solutions?') with the one route the run has not taken. (1) NAMES VERSUS MECHANISMS (main): show that when a prohibition names a model's whole path-search repertoire, the model that obeys complies on names, not mechanisms. Its correct survivors keep a banned expansion order under new names; the gap between lexical and mechanistic compliance grows with the number of banned names; and the survivors land at the EDGE of the banned set in name-free activation geometry (program states, mechanism descriptions) while staying OPPOSITE in name geometry. Replicate on weighted shortest path, the inspiration repository's task. (2) TRULY NOVEL (secondary): show that an executable evaluator plus exploration spent at decision tokens makes Qwen3-8B write correct online bin-packing heuristics that beat best fit on held-out instances and differ behaviourally from every published discovered heuristic, with more behaviour clusters per call than temperature; replicate the operator contrast on constructive TSP. (3) MEAN ANSWER (extend): show in Gemma and Llama that the instruct default is a sharpened base choice, not the base mean, and locate where post-training sharpened Qwen3-8B's fork by patching base outputs of its validated fork-stack components. (4) FIX: answer every item of the blocking iteration-8 review in place.
strategies.rationale: WHY THIS DIRECTION. The direction block chose 'cover' on the request's most concrete open deliverable. Iteration 8 gave the top-five question its first answer (the obeying model's survivors land OPPOSITE the banned five), but on a manifold of alias-named prompts whose classes follow lexical overlap with the banned names, and the review blocks that answer. The survivors themselves point the other way: unit-weight Dijkstra (6 screen and 9 held-out catalogue survivors) and wavefront propagation (1) expand a unit grid in BFS order, and so does Bellman-Ford/SPFA on the grid (7) whenever its queue is FIFO. That turns the confound into a test the account predicts and nobody has run: a prohibition naming the whole repertoire is obeyed on names, not mechanisms. SIDEWAYS MOVES, WITHIN THE REQUEST'S QUESTIONS. From an alias-named manifold to name-free ones (program states, mechanism descriptions) with name-only and named manifolds as the contrast (TP-G): the same edge-or-opposite question, asked with an instrument that would show the edge if it is there. From name-based labels to executed expansion and relaxation orders (TP-B, TP-W): the same 'what did the model write under the ban', read by mechanism. From one ban cell with one landing algorithm (p 0.20 at the level of algorithms) to a dose-response over k = 1..5 and six rotated five-name sets, which give algorithm-level power. From single-sample novelty, a settled negative across eight iterations (0 novel among more than 40,000 correct programs), to a scored open-ended task where 'novel' is measurable (beats best fit on held-out instances; behaviourally distinct from FunSearch, EoH and ReEvo heuristics), with the run's fork finding turned into a mutation operator (NOV-B, replicated in NOV-T). From one family's base sub-arm (partly occupied by Cantarero et al.) to three families with Cantarero's controls, and from token-level splicing to the validated components that carry the sharpening (BASE). WHY THESE SHOULD COME OUT POSITIVE. N: 14 of 17 iteration-8 survivors are BFS-order candidates by definition (unit-weight Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford/SPFA with a FIFO queue, wavefront); 55-100% of banned-mechanism programs across ten configurations carry no banned name; single bans are obeyed mechanistically (DFS for BFS 86/100), so the dissociation should grow with k. V: FunSearch, EoH and ReEvo report evaluator-guided heuristics that beat best fit on Weibull instances, and iteration 7's search already beat instruction-only sampling 7.8x on kth smallest; the fork finding says ideas are decided at a few high-entropy early tokens, so branching there should buy behaviour clusters that global temperature spends on phrasing. B: the Qwen base sub-arm already shows +2.1 to +13.4 nats at the fork with phrasing almost unchanged, and iteration 5 saw Gemma pt more diverse than it. SLOT MAP (the direction's split). Main cover, 3 slots: TP-B, TP-G, TP-W. Secondary cover, 2: NOV-B, NOV-T. Extend, 1: BASE. Fix, 1: Step 0 (S0). REVIEWER MAP. MUST-FIX 1 (circuit shape; layer-0 node): S0 (0a) rewrites the record; BASE B3 executes the held-out arm with position-aligned means and recomputes the motif on matched contrasts. MUST-FIX 2 (DAS verdict): S0 (0b). MUST-FIX 3 (entropy superlative, 0.004 bits, law scope): S0 (0c). MUST-FIX 4 (base sub-arm novelty; positioning): S0 (0d) builds the iteration-8 positioning table, and BASE narrows and extends the claim. MUST-FIX 5 (alias-named manifold): S0 (0e) adds the alias-overlap Spearman from iteration 8's own geodesics; TP-G executes the name-free manifolds. Minor 1 (Gemma comparators): S0 (0f). Minor 2 (figure markers): S0 (0g). BUDGET. OpenRouter: USD 13.72 remained on 2026-10-23 for iterations 9 and 10 together, so this round's artifacts are capped at USD 6.2 combined (TP-B 3.5, TP-W 1.2, TP-G 0.4, NOV-B 0.4, NOV-T 0.3, BASE 0.2, S0 0.2), leaving at least USD 7.5 for iteration 10. GPU: about 3 h (TP-G), 2.5 h (TP-W), 4.5 h (NOV-B), 4 h (NOV-T), 4 h (BASE), each on its own A4500 pod; TP-B is CPU plus OpenRouter. WHAT EACH OUTCOME BUYS. R6 holds: the request's edge-or-opposite question gets the answer 'opposite in names, at the edge in mechanisms', and denial prompting gets a mechanism-level negative: an exhaustive ban buys renamed defaults, not new ideas. R6 fails (survivors are mechanistically distinct and land opposite in name-free geometry too): iteration 8's 'opposite' becomes robust in every geometry. V positive: the run's first correct novel solution, produced by a knob grounded in the fork finding. Operators tie: the evaluator, not where randomness is spent, is what matters. B positive in three families with component localisation: 'the model gives a sharpened choice, not the mean', with where it was written.

artifacts.summary: NOV-B1: FunSearch-style island search on online bin packing with Qwen3-8B-FP8 (vLLM 0.11, thinking off) as mutator, evaluated by the iteration-9 FunSearch harness (copied, sha256-verified, re-gated: G-HARNESS PASS, BF 5.37% OR3 / 3.98% Weibull 5k, c12 3.11%, c14 0.68%, gate block identical to BP9). Arms at matched calls (C*=2,000 per arm and seed, seeds 0-1, lockstep lag-1 rounds of 25): T1.0, T1.6 (top-p 0.95), DTB (force a rank 2-8 token at the highest-entropy code token of the first 48), RPB (random-position placebo), IDEA (one-sentence 'different idea' instruction); NS (no selection, 1,000 per seed) afterwards. Everything hash-committed (6 commits, hash chain). Results: V1 SUPPORTED - every core arm's best program beats 0.8x best fit on both primary held-out sets (FSW5k/OR3 excess %: T1.0 1.53/3.55, T1.6 1.40/3.55, DTB 2.43/4.18, RPB 1.73/3.48; IDEA 1.85/3.38; NS stays at best fit 3.98/5.37; tuned ab baseline abFF(5,22) 2.14/3.06; c12 3.03/3.11). V2 PARTIAL - behaviour clusters (complete linkage, all pairs agree >=0.95 on 2,000 probe states) over 4,000 calls: T1.0 148, T1.6 373, DTB 446, RPB 212, IDEA 770; R1 (DTB/T1.0)=3.01 [2.66,3.43], R2 (DTB/T1.6)=1.20 [1.13,1.33] < 1.5, R3 (DTB/RPB)=2.10; DTB's best is the weakest on held-out; per-token and rarefied ratios agree (R2 1.08/1.15); 200 label shuffles never reach R1>=1.5. V3 - 211 candidates, 70 pass both held-out bars with max corpus agreement <0.9 (86-entry corpus: textbook, Sum-of-Squares, FunSearch, EoH x60, ReEvo, HSEvo, MCTS-AHD, LLM4AD, ab family + tuned ab; also all 3,843 ab-grid points), 53 joint clusters, 30 audited. Judge gate unmet (mistral 9/10, deepseek 5/10, kimi 6/10), so the arm-blind manual read decides: 22 reduce to the known ab principle (tight fit else avoid medium leftovers, b tied to item size); 8 NOVEL (gate-passing judge agrees 8/8, advisory majority 5/8), all one idea family: prefer a leftover that is a whole multiple of the item size (T1.0 2, DTB 4, IDEA 2; caveats: the 0.9 probe filter did no work - positive control 70->70; one novel program is stochastic; no ablation of the modular term). V5 (descriptive): reversion at birth tokens 0.40 vs controls 0.36, sign test p=0.49. V6 PARTIAL: rename rate IDEA 0.44 vs T1.0 0.86. Evaluator effect: NS never beats best fit. Provides method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out: every call with code/F/cluster, best programs, V3 candidates, corpus, V5), results/*.json, figures F1-F8, data/main and data/ns raw rows and decision vectors, audit/rederive.py. OpenRouter spend $0.14.

artifacts.summary: NOV-B2 is the pre-registered, independently implemented replication (seeds 2 and 3) of a FunSearch-style island search on online bin packing with Qwen3-8B-FP8 (vLLM 0.11, thinking off) as the mutator, plus an exploratory, separately pre-registered extension on seeds 4 and 5. Harness: FunSearch's exact priority harness, sha256-verified and re-gated (BF 5.37%/3.98%, c12 3.11%, c14 0.68% reproduced). Arms at matched calls (C* = 2000 per arm-seed, committed rule): T1.0; T1.6 with top-p 0.95; DTB (force a rank-2..8 token at the highest-entropy eligible position of the first 48 body tokens); RPB (same forcing at a random position, placebo); IDEA (instruction to use a different idea); NS (fixed FF/BF parents). Selection on SEL-OR+SEL-W; held-out H-FSW5k and H-OR3 (primary) plus 6 sets. Behaviour = bin choices on 2,000 committed probe states; clusters by complete linkage at 0.95; novelty = agreement < 0.9 with 82 corpus programs (FunSearch, EoH, HSEvo, MCTS-AHD, ReEvo, LLM4AD, RAISE, textbook, dependency scan) and all 3,843 ab-family members, then gated judges and an arm-blind manual read. Verdicts (seeds 2-3, all re-derived by a separate stdlib audit): V1 PARTIAL - best-program held-out excess H-FSW5k/H-OR3: DTB 2.395/3.852%, RPB 1.720/3.703%, IDEA 2.133/3.554% pass the 0.8xBF rule; T1.0 3.672/4.821% and T1.6 (= BF) fail. V2 PARTIAL - behaviour clusters per 2,000 calls (seed 2/3): DTB 230/143, RPB 269/233, IDEA 134/150, T1.0 13/8, T1.6 1/1; R_T1.0 17.8, R_T1.6 186.5, but R_RPB 0.74 < 1.2; shuffled-arm placebo 0/200 supported. V3 DISCONFIRMED - 151 candidates, 50 pass the 0.8 rule, 48 also pass the corpus-novelty filter, 0 of 40 judged are NOVEL (all recombine published principles: BF on near-exact fits, an avoided residual band as in ab/c12, a residual target ~c*item as in EoH run 3/MCTS-AHD); rule-of-three bound 7.5%; no judge passed its 10-control gate (judges advisory). V6 PARTIAL - rename share IDEA 0.670 vs T1.0 0.959. V5 (descriptive, n=30): forcing the argmax back at the offspring's high-entropy deviating token reverts it to a parent in 49.8% of continuations vs 25.5% at random positions (sign-flip p=0.0086). Exploratory seeds 4-5: V2 rule SUPPORTED (R_RPB 1.47) but pooled 4-seed R_RPB = 1.08: entropy targeting is within seed noise, while forcing (or the IDEA instruction) beats temperature robustly (pooled R_T1.0 25.5). The tuned ab member ab-FF(5,22) (F 0.740 vs best searched 0.726) beats every arm's best on H-OR3. Provides: method.py + src/ pipeline, 42,000 logged programs with evaluations and decision vectors (data/), all analyses (results/), figures F1-F7, commitments.log hash chain, method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out) with full/mini/preview, audit/rederive.py.

artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_53
artifacts.summary: NOV-T experiment (claim V4): does decision-token branching (DTB: force a rank-2..8 token at the highest-entropy code position of the first 48 body tokens, then continue at T 1) make an LLM program search find more distinct heuristic behaviours than temperature? Task: constructive TSP with the ReEvo/EoH select_next_node interface; Qwen3-8B-FP8 on vLLM 0.11 (NVIDIA L4) mutates programs in a FunSearch-style 5-island search seeded with nearest neighbour (NN); fitness F normalised to NN on 64 selection instances (n 50/100) against LKH-3 tours.
