critiques.description:
Section 10.3 records the novelty claim as 'supported, with a flag'. It rests on eight programs that 'prefer a bin whose leftover after packing is a whole multiple of the item size'. The closing calls the question unresolved and lists what it needs (10.12): 'an ablation of the term, a second blind reader, and a direct comparison' with EoH run-3 and MCTS-AHD. The ablation needs no new generation, and I ran it from art_k7A5-5vcXY1g's own files.

Method: the packing loop and family excess of src/bp.py; probe agreement on data/probes/P1.json against the stored decision vectors of data/corpus/corpus.json and ab_grid.json. It reproduces best fit at 3.984%/5.368% and each full program's Table 451 values exactly. The code is checks/ablate_whole_multiple.py and the output results/ablation_whole_multiple.json.

Four programs have the term as a separate line. Held-out excess, Weibull test set / binpack3 (%):
- cand_22 (temperature 1.0): 1.529/3.554 full; 1.539/3.728 without the multiple bonus; 1.580/3.752 also without the leftover-equals-item bonus.
- cand_20: 2.425/4.100, then 2.475/3.902, then 2.535/4.026.
- cand_09 (instruction): 1.771/3.405, then 1.861/3.405.
- cand_29 (instruction): 1.580/3.554, then 1.580/3.504, then 1.751/3.554 with its distance-to-nearest-multiple score also removed.

What the ablation shows:
- Every ablated variant still clears both bars (3.19%, 4.29%).
- Each keeps 1.4 to 2.4 points of its advantage over best fit on the Weibull test set and 1.3 to 2.0 on binpack3.
- Removing the multiple bonus alone makes binpack3 better for cand_20 and cand_29.
- Every variant still agrees with every corpus and ab-grid program on fewer than 0.9 of probe decisions (maxima 0.8135, 0.8805 with best fit, 0.8150 and 0.6925).
In these four programs the held-out gain therefore comes from near-exact-fit bonuses, fragmentation penalties and an avoided residual band, not from the whole-multiple term.

That is the ab principle of Herrmann and Pallez [162], the run's own source for the ab family. Their reading of FunSearch's c14 is 'apply BestFit if a perfect-fit bin exists; otherwise, if there exists a bin whose remaining space exceeds the item size by more than 20, apply WorstFit'. Their closed form of EoH's heuristic already has an item-relative band term (+0.5 if b > 4s).

The idea that remains, leaving room for whole further copies of the same item, is the principle of Lee and Lee's Harmonic-k (J. ACM 32(3), 1985), which packs items of class (C/(j+1), C/j] j per bin. The artifact implemented it (src/bp.py harmonic_k; results/corpus.json 'stateful': Harmonic_4 at 35.2% and 40.8% held-out excess, Next Fit at 28.8% and 31.7%). The report never names it, and Table 448 omits both rows.

In cand_20, cand_22 and cand_09 the multiple test is an exact equality (np.isclose, or % item < 1e-5). It can fire only because every selection and held-out set has integer item sizes (data/instances/*.json).

This is the part of the original request left unanswered: the 'truly creative and novel solutions' half of its plain-language question. The record's own files can answer it.
critiques.suggested_action: Run the ablation for all eight programs: for cand_01, cand_12, cand_18 and cand_24, drop the 1/|gap - item| and 1/|gap - 2 item| spikes and keep the exact-fit term; run cand_01 under a fixed noise seed. Add a table beside Table 451 giving each variant's held-out excess on all eight sets and its maximum corpus and ab-grid agreement. Add Harmonic-k and Next Fit to Table 448. In 10.3 and 10.6, name Harmonic-k and Herrmann and Pallez's readings of c14 and EoH as the nearest neighbours. Then restate the 10.3 verdict, the 10.11 'Established' entry and the closing answer to the request: at this scale the searches found no heuristic whose new element carries its held-out gain; the eight are ab-type rules with an inert or marginal whole-multiple term. That agrees with the replication's 0 of 40 (rule-of-three bound 7.5%) and TSP's 12 of 12 known. If any program keeps a novelty claim, test its term on a non-integer item-size distribution and add a second blind reader.

critiques.description:
The replication (art_dq4MiqNM89Go) stores six sensitivity counts per arm and seed in results/analysis_clusters.json (per_arm_seed): clusters excluding stochastic programs, clusters with F < 1, clusters per million tokens, rarefied counts, counts on informative probe states, and counts after rescoring. Section 10.4 reports none of them, although Table 450 reports the first search's equivalents.

The stochastic exclusion is the one that moves. In seed 2, 11.0% of branching's valid programs are stochastic (stochastic_share_valid 0.110, against 0.018 for the placebo, 0.033 for the instruction arm and 0 for both temperature arms). Excluding them leaves 157 of branching's 230 clusters. The placebo goes from 269 to 261 and temperature 1.0 stays at 13. In seed 3: branching 143 to 142, placebo 233 to 232, temperature 1.0 8 to 8; the instruction arm goes 134 to 120 and 150 to 139.

Effect on the ratios, pooled over seeds 2 and 3:
- Against temperature 1.0: 17.8 falls to 14.2.
- Against temperature 1.6: 186.5 falls to 149.5.
- Against the placebo: 0.74 falls to 0.61; seed 2 alone goes from 0.86 to 0.60.
- Clusters with F < 1: branching and the placebo tie (80 + 29 = 109 against 54 + 53 = 107).
- Rarefied to the placebo's valid count: 0.65 against the placebo.
- Informative states: 0.76; rescored programs: 0.75.
(checks/replication_sensitivities.py; results/replication_sensitivities.json.)

No verdict changes. But a stochastic program's decisions vary between evaluations, so it can add behaviour clusters that are not new heuristics, and that favours the arm that writes the most random programs. In the first search the same exclusion changes nothing: my recomputation from data/main/programs.jsonl with a random-call regex gives 3.01, 1.19 and 2.10.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the sensitivity columns to Table 452, or add a Table 454b with per-seed and pooled ratios under each. In 10.4 and 10.6, state that excluding stochastic programs cuts branching's advantage over temperature by about a fifth and widens the placebo's lead, with the ordering unchanged. Give the first search's stochastic exclusion beside Table 450 for parity.

critiques.description:
Table 454 (and results/verdicts.json) gives 95% bootstrap intervals over round blocks, and two of them exclude their own point estimates. Against temperature 1.0 the ratio is 17.8, with bootstrap median 14.9 and interval 13.0 to 17.6. Against temperature 1.6 it is 186.5, with median 139 and interval 127 to 151.

The likely cause is this. A percentile bootstrap that resamples blocks with replacement leaves out about 37% of the blocks in each resample, so clusters seen in only one block often disappear. That pulls the count down for arms with many rare clusters (branching) and hardly at all for arms whose few clusters recur (the copying temperature arms). The interval then describes the resampled statistic, not the ratio the report states. No verdict depends on it, but the paper step will quote these intervals.
critiques.suggested_action: Use an interval that is valid for ratios of distinct counts: a block jackknife, a bias-corrected (BCa) bootstrap, or subsampling without replacement at a fixed number of blocks. Alternatively, rarefy both arms to a common block count before resampling. Recompute Table 450's intervals the same way and say in 10.4 why the method changed.

Add [FIGURE] markers beside Tables 463 and 464 for the factorial frames and the full frame with placed families, and one for the held-fixed MDS frames. State the readout, block and k beside each marker. In 10.9, add markers for the readout-plane and block-35 PCA plots, and name the data file each figure draws from.

critiques.description:
Two reproduction-gate shortfalls are recorded in the artifacts' deviations files but not in the report.
- Weights experiment (art_a7CQm-6CXmoJ, results/deviations.json S0_reproduction_partial, which the artifact itself labels major). The per-prompt Spearman correlation with iteration 9's margins is 0.983 (instruct) and 0.898 (base) on connected components, and 0.783 and 0.908 on minimum spanning tree, against a 0.99 rule. The largest per-prompt instruct deviation is 1.09 nats (S0_per_prompt_T10). Section 10.9 and Table 465 give only the 0.061-nat difference in means.
- Geometry experiment (art_ho7tqaOyBjkN, D-repro-cosine). States recomputed for 10 cached iteration-9 programs reach a minimum cosine of 0.99981 (Qwen3-8B) and 0.99990 (Qwen3-32B), recorded as below the 0.9999 threshold. Section 10.8 says only that the frames matched 'bit for bit'. That is true because the catalogue states were read from the iteration-9 cache.
Neither shortfall changes a verdict, since the weights shares use the run's own margins. They do limit how far per-prompt comparisons with iteration 9 can be read.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the per-prompt Spearman values and the largest per-prompt deviation to Table 465. Add one sentence to the 10.8 setup giving the recompute cosines and saying which states were recomputed and which were read from the iteration-9 cache.

dimension_scores.justification: Claims are preregistered in hash-chained commits, verdicts follow the committed rules, and the closing hedges where the evidence is thin. It is not a 4 for three reasons. The one positive novelty verdict (10.3) rests on one reader, an inert filter and no ablation, and the ablation I ran shows that the new term does not carry the held-out gain in four of the eight programs. The replication's cluster ratios are not shown with stochastic programs excluded, though that exclusion moves them by about a fifth. And the percentile bootstrap in Table 454 is biased for distinct-cluster counts.

A reader who was not on the run can follow each iteration's reasons, setup, verdicts and checks, and each table is introduced by what it settles. Iteration 10 is dense but in order. The gaps: Sections 10.8 and 10.9 place no activation-space figure, although the closing cites geometry plots for iteration 10 and the artifacts rendered them. Table 454 prints intervals that exclude their estimates without comment. Table 448's comparator list leaves out the stateful baselines the artifact scored.

Almost all of the run is preserved: every artifact, every iteration, the dead ends and failed predictions, and the corrections made in place. The misses are partial, not whole experiments. They are the replication's sensitivity counts, the stateful bin-packing baselines, two reproduction-gate shortfalls recorded only in deviations files, and the activation-space figures of 10.8 and 10.9.

review.overall_assessment:
The record holds ten iterations, one section each and in order. Every one of the 66 artifacts in the supplementary list is cited in the report, and each of the seven iteration-10 artifacts has its own section with tables: the record repair (10.2), the two bin-packing searches (10.3, 10.4), TSP (10.5), the prohibition experiment (10.7), the factorial geometry (10.8) and the weights experiment (10.9). The previous review was blocking. Its five blocking and five minor items are closed by 27 verbatim edits applied in place and marked as iteration-10 corrections, backed by an apply test, an 861-check re-derivation and a 45-value spot-check (Table 446). None of them is raised again here.

I recomputed the iteration-10 headline numbers from the artifacts' own files, and they match.
- First search: per-arm bests (Tables 448-449); clusters per 1,000 calls 37.0, 93.25, 111.5 and 53.0; ratios 3.01, 1.20 and 2.10; the novelty funnel (211 candidates, 70 better, 53 joint clusters, 30 read, 8 novel; judge gates 9, 5 and 6 of 10; 70 of 70 under the permuted corpus); rename rates 0.436 against 0.861.
- Replication: per-seed clusters (Table 452); ratios 17.76, 186.5 and 0.743; funnel 151, 50, 48, 40, 0; rename shares 0.670 against 0.959.
- TSP: bar 19.15; nearest neighbour 23.94; ratios 0.963, 2.315 and 0.948; 12 of 12 programs known; the stop at 1,056 calls, which the report discloses.
- Prohibition: the cells and rename rates of Tables 460-462.
- Geometry: the partial RSA and placement values of Tables 463-464.
- Weights: the shares and generation counts of Tables 465-469 (0.548 [0.440, 0.707]; 5 of 30; 21 of 90 against 4; 72 of 90 against 17; 21 and 30 of 30 at twice and three times the dose).
I also rebuilt the harness's packing loop and probe agreement. They reproduce best fit (3.98%, 5.37%) and, for four of the eight 'novel' programs, the held-out excess and corpus agreement to the printed digits. results_reported is therefore true.

Three problems remain.
(1) The run's one positive answer to the request's 'truly novel' question is the eight whole-multiple-of-item programs. Section 10.3 still records that claim as 'supported, with a flag', and the closing calls it unresolved. The ablation the record asks for in 10.12 was never run, although it takes CPU seconds on files already on disk. I ran it on the four programs where the term is a separate line. Removing it changes held-out excess by +0.05 to +0.17 points on the Weibull test set and by -0.07 to +0.20 on binpack3. Every ablated program still clears both 0.8 bars and still agrees with every corpus program on fewer than 0.9 of decisions. What carries the gain over best fit is the ab principle (Herrmann and Pallez [162]), which is what the replication's reader concluded. The nearest classical neighbour of the remaining idea is Harmonic-k (Lee and Lee 1985). The artifact computed it (results/corpus.json) but the report never names it.
(2) The replication's sensitivity counts in results/analysis_clusters.json are missing from 10.4. Excluding stochastic programs alone removes 73 of branching's 230 seed-2 clusters and lowers the pooled ratios to 14.2, 149.5 and 0.61.
(3) Smaller items:
- Two of the three intervals in Table 454 exclude their own point estimates.
- The activation-space geometry figures of 10.8 and 10.9 have no markers, although the closing says they exist.
- Two reproduction-gate shortfalls appear only in the artifacts' deviations files.

Coverage is partial for one reason: the novelty half of the request's plain-language question is left open, and the record's own files can close it. Soundness is 3 and results_reported is true, so the review is not blocking.
strengths: Complete at the artifact level. All 66 supplementary artifacts are cited, and each iteration-10 artifact has a section with its tables (Tables 446-469). Dead ends and failed predictions stay on record: the TSP operator claim was disconfirmed; novelty was disconfirmed in the replication and on TSP; the late-MLP claim failed; the described ban was a weak test; the base-distribution forcing arm was dropped because two engines did not fit on the GPU; the TSP search stopped at 1,056 of the 2,000 projected calls.

The iteration-9 record repair is a model of how corrections should be made. Its input was checked byte-identical to the report before editing. Seven positive controls reproduced stored values. All 27 edits applied once each, in place and marked. An apply test, a residual-claim lint and an independent 861-check re-derivation back them (10.2, Table 446). The chronology is intact.

The numbers trace and recompute. Every iteration-10 headline I checked matches its result file to the printed digit. Values the report flags as moving between evaluations are given in each version, for example the branching best at 2.42/4.17, 2.44/4.15 and 2.44/4.08.

The searches carry the controls that let their claims be read: a no-selection arm, a random-position placebo for entropy-targeted forcing, 200 label shuffles, and a permuted-corpus positive control that showed the novelty filter did no work. They also have judge gates scored on planted controls, a strict comparator (the 3,843-member ab grid, with a member tuned at matched evaluations), and an independent second implementation of the whole search on fresh seeds. That second implementation is what exposed the prompt-dependence of temperature's effect.

The novelty claim is scoped honestly. The report states that the probe filter did no work, that one reader decided, that one of the eight programs is stochastic, that no ablation was run, and that none of the eight beats the published ab members or FunSearch's heuristics. It sets the replication's opposite verdict beside the first (10.6), and the closing calls the question unresolved instead of answered.

The bin-packing prohibition experiment has the run's cleanest instrument: exact behavioural identity on 2,000 committed probe states, gated with renamed and reimplemented copies of each rule. It separates genuine renaming in the non-thinking model (gap +0.40) from real behavioural change in the thinking models. It also reports against its own claim that held-out templates shrink Qwen3-8B's gap to +0.08.

The weights experiment reports its specificity failure plainly. The base-row effect clears the isotropic null but sits inside the residual-subspace null (p 0.37), so it is called readout-level, not token-specific. The late-MLP claim is reported as failed against Frobenius-matched early swaps. The Stage-0 fallback, which uses the run's own margins, is explained together with a measured bfloat16 numerics floor.

The closing goes through the original request point by point: question 1a-c on temperature, seeding, prompt instructions, the internals of BFS against DFS runs, the manifold with centroids coloured by implemented count, and the edge-or-opposite reading of the top-five ban. It says which parts are answered only descriptively or in part (circuits, the circle manifold).

strategies.expected_outcome: Seven artifacts. (1-2) NOV-B1 and NOV-B2: evaluator-guided island searches on online bin packing with Qwen3-8B as mutator, four seeds in two independently implemented artifacts, five arms at matched calls plus a no-selection control. Each artifact verifies the iteration-9 harness first and scores its arms on held-out instance families against best fit, the tuned ab-heuristic and every retrievable published heuristic, with exact behaviour clusters, judged novelty candidates, birth-token reversion (V5) and the rename rate of instruction-level novelty (V6). (3) NOV-T: the same operator contrast on constructive TSP against LKH reference tours and TSPLIB optima. (4) NOV-R: cumulative, described and held-out name bans plus the two novelty instructions on bin packing in three Qwen3 models, read by one gated name-blind instrument, with the no-evaluator novelty rate (P3). (5) TP-G2: a factorial discipline-by-container program manifold in two models with partial RSA and preregistered placements of every survivor family, plotted in actual activation coordinates. (6) BASE-W: the unembedding-row and late-MLP weight tests of where post-training wrote the default, with matched random controls, generation tests and Gemma's reversed fork. (7) S0: every review item answered in place and a request ledger for the final report. Iteration 10 is the last: the final record then answers the 'truly novel' question positively, as bounded, or negatively, each with its budget, answers the top-five question by mechanism and by kind of map, and declares every null.
strategies.objective: Answer the request's layman question ('can we make LLMs give truly creative and novel solutions?') with the one route the run has never taken. With an executable evaluator on online bin packing, where 'better' and 'new' are exact, and on constructive TSP fixed in advance as a replication, show that Qwen3-8B, whose unaided repertoire is bounded, writes heuristics that beat the textbook rule on held-out instances and decide unlike every published heuristic we can retrieve. Show also that spending the sampling randomness at the decision token buys more distinct behaviours per call than temperature, which answers 'is temperature the creativity knob' in the discovery setting. Beside it: renaming under prohibition, tested on a second task with an exact name-blind instrument; whether the program map's edge is an edge in mechanism or in surface; where post-training wrote the default in weights; and the record repaired as the blocking review requires.
strategies.rationale: WHY THIS DIRECTION. Nine iterations show a bounded repertoire: no single-sample knob, internal edit, forced branch or prohibition produced a correct novel algorithm in more than 20,000 audited programs. Temperature only reweights the alternatives the fork tokens already weigh, and an exhaustive ban is answered by renaming. On catalogue tasks the literal 'novel algorithm' question is a settled negative, because anything new must leave a finite textbook set. The sideways move, within the same question, is to a scored open-ended task where novelty and quality are measured exactly (bin choices on frozen probe states; excess bins on held-out instances), using the one mechanism the field's discovery systems rely on and the run never used: selection by an evaluator. The fork finding becomes an operator: branch at the highest-entropy early token, priced against temperature, a random-position placebo and an instruction to differ, at matched calls. WHY IT SHOULD COME OUT POSITIVE. V1: FunSearch's Weibull heuristic reaches 0.68% against best fit's 3.98%, and two-parameter rules already beat best fit (Herrmann and Pallez), so 0.8 of best fit is within reach of short searches. The harness's fitness weights both families equally, which matches the V1 rule. Iteration 7's evaluator search composed known techniques at 7.8 times the instruction rate. V3: evolved priority functions rarely coincide decision-for-decision with published ones, and the instrument is exact. V2: 90% of positions have entropy below 0.0003 to 0.05 nats, so temperature spends its randomness off the decision, while forcing at a random position mostly breaks or rephrases code. SLOT MAP (the direction's split). Main cover, 3 slots: NOV-B1, NOV-B2 (same frozen protocol, disjoint seeds, so one stalled session cannot erase the main claim) and NOV-T. Secondary, 4 slots: NOV-R (extend: names against mechanisms with an exact instrument), TP-G2 (deepen: factorial program manifold), BASE-W (deepen: weights) and S0 (fix). REVIEWER MAP. MUST-FIX 1 (Qwen3-32B exhaustion curve against the hand reads) -> S0 (0a). MUST-FIX 2 (greedy at k = 4; no-op sensitivity) -> S0 (0b). MUST-FIX 3 (described ban mixes instruments) -> S0 (0c), and NOV-R's P2 retests it with one instrument. MUST-FIX 4 (placements not reported) -> S0 (0d), and TP-G2's G2 places every family under preregistration. MUST-FIX 5 (RSA omits the data-structure matrix) -> S0 (0e), and TP-G2's G1 separates discipline from container. Minor items -> S0 (0f)-(0j); the random-set repeats also shape BASE-W's draws without reuse; the harness note (0j) is acted on by NOV-B1/NOV-B2/NOV-R reusing the gated harness. BUDGET. OpenRouter phase pot USD 20.00 (live, 2026-10-24); caps NOV-B1 0.6, NOV-B2 0.6, NOV-T 0.5, NOV-R 5.0, TP-G2 1.0, BASE-W 0.3, S0 0.3 (8.3 in all, leaving at least 11.7 for the report and figure steps). GPU: one A4500 per experiment, about 3 to 3.5 hours each inside the 6-hour box. INFRASTRUCTURE. Iteration 9 lost three artifacts at execution, so every experiment follows anti-stall rules (background jobs with PID polling, request timeouts, append-only checkpoints, resumable stages, wall-clock milestones, partial results every 15 minutes) and carries the exact vLLM settings that worked on this GPU. WHAT EACH OUTCOME BUYS. V1 and V3 hold: the run's first correct novel solutions and the answer 'an evaluator, not a knob, makes an 8B open model creative'; with V2, a cheap operator grounded in the fork finding. V1 without V3: search improves the score but stays inside the published heuristic space at this budget. V2 ties: where randomness is spent does not matter once an evaluator selects. No arm beats best fit: a direct negative, stated with its budget.
strategies.title: Evaluator-guided search for truly new heuristics
